categories.label: Art & Galleries
categories.description: Contemporary art galleries, studios and street art. Programmes move in months rather than weeks, so most of this category is harvested monthly.

categories.label: Churches & Cathedrals
categories.description:
Working churches whose public programme is largely not religious: organ recitals, choral evensong open to anyone, lunchtime concerts, festival performances borrowing the acoustics, heritage openings and civic events.
A category rather than a corner of `music` because these sources do not fit one: the concerts belong to music, the tower tours to museums, the carol services to neither, and the buildings themselves are the reason people come. Bristol's existing church venues had ended up scattered — `music/st-georges-bristol` is a deconsecrated concert hall and belongs where it is — and the point of this file is the ones still in use as churches, which nothing else claimed.

categories.label: Cinema
categories.description: Independent and commercial cinemas, plus film festivals and pop-up screenings.

categories.label: City-wide
categories.description: Cross-category listings sites, the council and the tourist board. These are the safety net: anything the category catalogues miss — pop-ups, one-off community events, venue-less happenings — tends to surface here first.

categories.label: Comedy
categories.description: Comedy clubs, improv, and the venues whose comedy programme is substantial enough to be worth watching on its own.

categories.label: Learning & Talks
categories.description: Public lectures, adult education and outreach — the programmes whose purpose is that someone leaves knowing something. A university publishing its own public programme belongs here rather than among the city-wide aggregators, which is why `education/university-of-bristol` was re-homed out of `citywide`. UWE stays there for now: unlike Bristol's, its entry has real harvest history behind it.

categories.label: Family & Kids
categories.description: City farms, play spaces and companies producing for children. Programmes spike hard in school holidays, which is the main thing to get right here.

categories.label: Festivals
categories.description: Annual, mostly venue-less events. The largest things that happen in the city live here, and almost none of them appear on any venue's website. Announcements cluster in winter and spring for a summer that sells out early.

categories.label: Food & Drink
categories.description: Food halls, breweries and taprooms with public event programmes. Only sources that actually programme events belong here — a restaurant with no events is not a source, however good it is.

categories.label: Gardens & Horticulture
categories.description: Botanic gardens, nurseries, growing projects and open-garden schemes. Sharply seasonal: plant fairs and open days cluster in spring and early summer, and most of this category has nothing on at all in January.

categories.label: Literature & Talks
categories.description: Bookshops with event programmes, literary festivals, spoken word and poetry nights, and public talks.

categories.label: Making & Craft
categories.description:
Makerspaces, workshops, printmaking, woodwork and craft courses.
The distinctive problem in this category is that most listings are *courses*, not events — a ten-week evening class is not the same thing as a one-off workshop, and a "what's on" page is much less useful if it fills up with enrolment listings. Prefer one-off and short workshops, open days and public makes; record a recurring course as `occurrence.kind: recurring` with the pattern stated, rather than as a stream of dated events.

categories.label: Markets
categories.description: Street and indoor markets. Almost all are `occurrence.kind: recurring` — a weekly or monthly pattern rather than dated events — which makes them a good test of that part of the schema.

categories.label: Museums & Heritage
categories.description: Museums, heritage sites and science centres. Mostly permanent collections (`occurrence.kind: ongoing`) punctuated by temporary exhibitions and events.

categories.label: Music
categories.description: Concert halls, grassroots venues, club spaces and the promoters who programme them. Bristol's densest category by volume.

categories.label: Parks & Outdoors
categories.description: Estates, woods and green space that host public events. These are places before they are venues — most of the year they have no programme at all, and then a single weekend brings fifty thousand people.

categories.label: Sport
categories.description: Professional clubs and their grounds. Fixtures are published a season at a time and then move for TV, so the value here is in re-checking dates rather than discovering new events.

categories.label: Theatre
categories.description: Playhouses, studio theatres, circus and physical theatre, and the companies that programme into other people's spaces.

TOUR: Join us on an exploratory tour of the Georgian House Museum, learning about the

events.summary: Half an hour over four floors of a 1790s merchant's house, told through one household — including the colonial wealth and the trafficking of enslaved Africans that paid for it. Runs Friday to Sunday, so it covers most of the long weekend.
events.description:
Join us on an exploratory tour of the Georgian House Museum, learning about the history of
the house and the people who lived there.

Through the lens of a single household, guests will learn, not only about day-to-day life
in Georgian times, but about the dramatic and harrowing global events which fuelled an era
of both prosperity and tragedy, technology and romance, tradition and progress.

Tours are approximately 30 minutes long. Visitors will be taken on a brief historical
journey throughout four floors of the 230 year old Georgian town house. You can book a
tour online up to two days before the event; box office tickets may be available to buy on
the day (subject to availability). Please arrive no more than five minutes early to avoid
having to wait around outside.

Eating and drinking (with the exception of bottled water) is not permitted inside the
museum.

Be aware that the tour deals with more difficult themes relating to the house’s colonial
past and involvement with the trafficking of enslaved Africans which some visitors may
find distressing.

**Accessibility.** The number of stairs in the museum mean that the tour is not accessible
for those with reduced mobility. **Facilities.** There is no access to toilet facilities on
premises.

**Book tickets.** Standard ticket: £5. Under 16s ticket: Free. Carer/sighted guide ticket:
Free.

Tours start: Fridays – 11:30am and 2pm; Saturdays – 11:30am and 2pm; Sundays – 11:30am and
2pm. You can book online up to two days before the event, box office tickets may be
available to buy on the day (subject to availability).

events.raw:
"Good health of both body and mind for all." — John Wesley

John Wesley believed that it was mind, body, and soul that gave somebody
good health. Following this holistic approach would lead to living a happy
life.…

8th April, 2026 onwards. Free with normal Museum admission.
events.summary:
A small display drawn from the New Room's collection and archive on Wesley's
interest in medicine and natural remedies — he ran a free dispensary here,
and when the money ran out wrote a self-help medical guide that stayed a
bestseller for a century. Included in museum admission.
events.description:
"Good health of both body and mind for all." John Wesley

John Wesley believed that it was mind, body, and soul that gave somebody
good health. Following this holistic approach would lead to living a happy
life.

John was interested in medicine and natural remedies. At The New Room, he
created a dispensary of free medical care. When John ran out of money to
continue this, he wrote a self-help guide to medicine. The Primitive Physic:
or an Easy and Natural Method of Curing Most Diseases was published in
Bristol in 1747 and became a bestseller for a century.

Explore items from the John Wesley's New Room collection and archive linked
to health and wellbeing.

8th April, 2026 onwards.

Free with normal Museum admission.

**Visit Our Museum**

The Museum at the New Room tells the incredible history of John and Charles
Wesley, the early beginnings of Methodism and its relevance today. The
museum is housed in the original 1748 rooms.

Discover how the New Room played a vital role in providing healthcare and
education for those in need. Discover the challenges faced by Wesley in his
fight for social justice and be inspired to continue that work today.

Your ticket entitles you to 12 months free entry to the museum.

This is part of the Care & Repair Festival, organised by Sparks, John
Wesley's New Room, and Bristol BID. The Care & Repair Festival is a joyful,
family-friendly celebration of making, mending, and creativity, taking place
from 7-19 April 2026.

events.raw:
19 June – 20 September 2026

Join Mr B on a historic walking tour of Bristol’s harbourside.
events.summary: A three-mile costumed walk round the Floating Harbour in the company of Brunel himself, taking in Underfall Yard, Cumberland Basin and Queen Square. The schedule is Sundays and Fridays — plus the bank holiday Monday.
events.description:
Unearth the stories, mishaps and mayhem behind Brunel’s legacy, and discover how the city
of Bristol helped to forge one of history’s greatest engineers.

Covering just over 3 miles of the harbourside, the tours last approximately 2 hrs 15 mins
and commence and finish outside The Board Walk restaurant in Brunel Square - located just
outside the main entrance to Bristol Dockyards.

Primarily following a circular route around Bristol’s Floating Harbour, Mr. Brunel will
discuss his Bristol born projects, tales from his own life, the history of the harbour as
well as some interesting chapters from Bristol’s past and present. Main stops on the tour
include Underfall Yard, Cumberland Basin, Queen Square and of course, the SS Great
Britain.

**Tickets.** Online advance booking only, subject to capacity. See dates available:
August: Sun 9, Fri 14, Sun 23, Mon 31. September: Sun 6, Fri 11, Sun 20. General
Admission to the site is not included, however an Afternoon Saver can be added to your
ticket.

depart. Mr. Brunel is a stickler for timekeeping! Price: £14.00. Suitable for: Families,

events.title: Folly
events.raw:
**Folly** — 23 June - 30 August 2026. Kenny Gallery, RWA, Queens Road,
Bristol, BS8 1PX. Admission free. Tuesday - Sunday: 10am - 5pm (Closed
Mondays).
events.summary: Four RWA Academicians, curated by Peter Burke, on folly in every sense: the ornamental towers and mock ruins of the eighteenth century, the obsolete monuments of modern ideology, and the private project pursued against all logic. Free, and in its final fortnight.
events.description:
Curated by Peter Burke RWA, with works by Peter Burke RWA, Judith Jones
RWA, Jemma Gunning RWA RE and Karl Singporewala RWA RIBA.

The exhibition explores folly through several lenses. It looks at the
tradition of folly building that emerged centuries ago in Britain,
where wealthy individuals chose to demonstrate their prosperity by
commissioning ornamental structures, often as towers or mock ruins. It
asks whether modern structures shaped by political, religious or
commercial ideologies, now redundant or obsolete, constitute
contemporary follies. And it explores the urge to undertake an
idiosyncratic project for its own sake, flying in the face of logic.

Across a wide range of mediums, these themes run as a common thread for
contemporary artistic exploration.

Kenny Gallery, RWA, Queens Road, Bristol, BS8 1PX. Admission free.
Tuesday – Sunday: 10am – 5pm, closed Mondays.

events.title: Polly Braden: Against the Tide
events.raw:
**Exhibitions** — 27 June - 27 September 2026

Polly Braden: Against the Tide

_September newsletter:_ LAST MONTH TO SEE… This September marks the final month to experience our major exhibitions, Polly Braden: Against the Tide and Jonathan Baldock: Held.
events.summary: Polly Braden's photographic project on young lives in Britain's coastal towns — in its final month, closing 27 September.
events.description:
This summer, Arnolfini presents *Against the Tide*, a new exhibition by
documentary photographer Polly Braden, created in collaboration with
young people growing up in some of the most deprived and often
forgotten places across England.

Known for her intimate, long-term collaborations, Polly Braden's work
focuses on overlooked communities and social issues, and her
distinctive style combines quiet observation with deep empathy.

*Against the Tide* is a project led by Braden in collaboration with
journalist Lisa Bachelor as part of *The Guardian*'s Seascape series.
The pair have spent more than a year visiting coastal locations,
talking to young people about their lives and what matters to them. The
result is a layered picture of coastal England today that goes beyond
the usual, negative portrayals and which shines a light on the hope
that is sometimes hidden from public view.

Across intimate portraits and first-hand testimony, *Against the Tide*
brings audiences face-to-face with a generation navigating life at the
sharp edge of inequality, while also imagining something different.
Alongside accounts of isolation and lack of opportunity are expressions
of resilience, ambition and hope, and a clear message: coastal towns
are not just sites of decline, but places of creativity and
possibility.

Spanning places that include Weston-super-Mare, Scarborough, Grimsby,
Southend, Portsmouth, Whitehaven, Tendring, Rhyl and Blackpool, the
work reveals a side of coastal Britain rarely seen in national
narratives. It was developed over a year through sustained
collaboration with 16–25-year-olds across these towns.

Supported by Arts Council England, the Guardian's Seascape series, the
University of Lancaster and UCL.

events.title: Jonathan Baldock: Held
events.raw:
**Exhibitions** — 27 June - 27 September 2026

Jonathan Baldock: Held

_September newsletter:_ LAST MONTH TO SEE… This September marks the final month to experience our major exhibitions, Polly Braden: Against the Tide and Jonathan Baldock: Held.
events.summary: Jonathan Baldock's major show of soft sculpture and ceramics on craft, materiality, the body and world-building — in its final month, closing 27 September.
events.description:
Known for his striking installations, Jonathan Baldock combines
ceramics, textiles and sound to create environments that are both
playful and thought-provoking. His work draws on folklore, traditional
craft and personal history, shaped by skills passed down through
generations of making.

*Held* features a monumental wild bear sculpture, commissioned by
Arnolfini. It invites visitors into a direct physical encounter — not
to be held, but to hold us.

> "The English artist has created a tense world of folkloric
> psychedelia and pagan aesthetics that is weird, threatening — and
> utterly compelling" — Eddy Frankel, *The Guardian* (5-star review)

At Arnolfini, the galleries become a colourful, sensory landscape
inspired by the natural world, somewhere between a garden and a
wilderness. *Aether* — a work formed from beeswax, ceramic and glass —
hovers overhead, evoking a space between worlds. At the entrance,
visitors are welcomed by *The Caretakers*, ceremonial costumes adorned
with hand-stitched plant motifs, setting the tone for a space rooted in
care. Beyond, a vivid array of ceramic and wall-based textile
sculptures unfolds: flowers with faces emerging from petals, trailing
roots and body parts, creating a cultivated wilderness that blurs
boundaries between the human and the natural.

Sound by artist Luke Barton and a custom scent by Lora Hemy fill the
space, adding to the exhibition's immersive and intimate atmosphere.

The bear itself draws on a long cultural history, from ancient myth to
the familiar comfort of childhood toys. Over the course of the
exhibition, its surface will become worn through use, carrying the
marks of the thousands of people who encounter it. Its face, modelled
on a scan of the artist's mother, adds a deeply personal dimension.

In an age increasingly defined by loneliness, accelerated by the rise
of AI and a gradual loss of communal spaces, *Held* proposes physical
closeness as a radical and necessary gesture.

This exhibition has been generously supported by the Henry Moore
Foundation. A monograph published to coincide with the show is
available from the Arnolfini Bookshop.

events.title: If Schools Were Ours to Imagine
events.raw:
When: 1 Jul 2026 – 2 Jan 2027
Where: Open City Lab
Recommended for: Families

Head to our Open City Lab, get creative and add to our evolving exhibition exploring how
schools could be made fairer for everyone.
events.summary: An exhibition that visitors add to as they go, collecting ideas about what a fairer school would look like. In the Open City Lab until January.
events.description:
What would it look like if we could decide what schools were like in future? Get creative
and add to our evolving exhibition exploring how schools could be made fairer for everyone.

There are six mini-activities in the space:

- Head to the retro desks and smell, touch, and listen to connect with local Bristolian's
  memories of school.
- It's school dance time. Express how people's stories of school make you feel through
  movement.
- Make a clay model of what would you add to school to make it better (fairer)?
- If you could do anything on your dream school day, what would it be? Decorate a piece of
  bunting to add to the display.
- Share your thoughts and reflections on what you've experienced in the space, and your own
  school stories. Write it down or record it with the team.
- Explore an interactive map of Bristol with stories from the repair-ed archive.

This project is in partnership with Reparative Futures of Education (Repair-Ed) from the
University of Oxford. This collaboration builds on the team's existing work which explores
people's experiences of schooling in relation to racial and class inequality in Bristol and
how schools could be made fairer in future.

**Access considerations** — This activity takes place in a slightly enclosed ground floor
space that is wheelchair accessible with a lot of room between tables and information stands.

From raging wildfire to the vision of an owl, from a river to multiple
galaxies, SENTIENTS is about being something else.

video games and virtual reality invites you to see through other eyes.

events.title: 1000 Years of Fashion History – an exhibition in miniature

price.text: Free, donations welcome. Drop in, no booking necessary.

events.raw:
18 July—1 November 2026

EXHIBITION: A timeline in miniature, with more than 100 hand-made costumes modelled by
fashion dolls.
events.summary: More than a hundred hand-made period costumes on twelve-inch dolls, Saxon to the 1980s, made over six years by Lisa Jayne Smith while she was being treated for breast cancer. Open across the weekend, free.
events.description:
From Saxon robes to Elizabethan ruffs, Victorian tartan and punk piercings, come and see
how what we wear has changed across time… in miniature!

This exhibition has been created by Lisa Jayne Smith, following a career working in theatre
and running her own business making and adapting period costume.

She has been an avid fan of costume history for as long as she can remember, and the
exhibition is inspired by a book she came across while costuming for a play, ‘The Change in
Fashion from 1066-1960s’.

Lisa spent six years researching and making more than 100 miniature historical costumes
while receiving treatment for breast cancer.

Each hand made outfit, modelled by a 12-inch fashion doll, is complete down to the tiniest
detail. The amount of time spent on each model would depend on the size and era of each
costume, anything from a week to a month.

Journey through time, from the Saxons through Medieval, Renaissance, Tudor, Elizabethan,
Jacobean, Carolean, Restoration, Stuart, Georgian, Victorian, Edwardian, 1910’s, 1920’s,
1930’s, 1940’s, 1950’s, 1960’s, 1970’s up to the 1980’s.

"I hope you enjoy looking at them as much as I have in making and creating them!" — Lisa
Jayne Smith

**Booking information.** This exhibition is located in the first floor costume gallery,
please be aware there are only stairs to this floor, no lift is available. Suitable for
children of all ages. Drop in, no booking necessary. Free, donations welcome.

events.raw:
Conservation Carnival! — 18 July – 31 August

Celebrate the incredible conservation success stories helping to protect our oceans and
wildlife this summer at Bristol Aquarium.

Join us for **Conservation Carnival**, where you’ll discover inspiring stories of species
recovery, habitat restoration and the amazing work of conservation charities making a real
difference around the world. Through interactive activities, guided tours and
family-friendly experiences, you’ll learn how small actions can help protect our blue
planet.

**Activities**

- **Take on the Conservation Trail** — Collect stamps as you journey through the aquarium,
  discovering six fascinating species and the conservation projects helping them thrive.
- **Daily Save Our Seas Guided Tours – 11am** — Join our expert team each day for a free
  guided conservation tour through a different area of the aquarium. Tours last
  approximately 15–20 minutes and include time for questions.
- **Treasure or Trash: Sandpit Search – Daily at 4pm** — Become a marine explorer as you
  dig through our interactive beach combing sandpit. Discover shark teeth, shark egg
  cases, fossils, seashells, coral fragments and ancient marine specimens. You’ll also
  uncover examples of plastic pollution and learn why keeping our beaches clean is so
  important for marine wildlife.
- **Visit the Conservation Corner** — Beach clean information, conservation charities you
  can support, how Bristol Aquarium and Aspro Parks help protect wildlife, and children’s
  colouring activities.

All Conservation Carnival activities are included with standard aquarium admission.

address.street: Great Western Dockyard, Gas Ferry Road

18 July – 2 September 2026

A summer of games, adventure and silliness down at the Dockyards.
events.summary: Interactive games threaded through the ship and dockyard — jar fishing, a giant skipping rope, orders shouted down the speaking trumpets — all drawn from real voyages. Included with admission and running right through the bank holiday weekend.
events.description:
Pack up your playmates and set sail for fun.

This summer at Bristol Dockyards – home of SS Great Britain – we're bringing the stories
of one of the world's most extraordinary ships to life through games, challenges and a
whole lot of laughs.

From the dockside to the dining room, take part in interactive challenges inspired by the
SS Great Britain’s global voyages. Here’s a taste of what’s in store:

- **Jar Fishing:** Child passengers would dangle jars into the sea to catch fish –
  without even being able to see what they'd caught! Now it's your turn.
- **Jump Rope:** Swing into action with our giant jump rope – a favourite from the
  streets of New York City. How long can you keep going?
- **Good Shout:** Head down to the engine room and listen out for your orders – called
  out through the speaking trumpets just like the real crew. How many commands can you
  get right?
- **Who Made All the Pies?** Race to make three fruit pies in the ship’s galley before
  anyone else! Flip cards to build your desserts, based on a real menu from 1863.

Key info — Time: 10:00am-5:00pm. Price: Included in your ticket.

**Kids Go Free - all summer long.** One child free for every paying adult – from now
until 2 September. Come back as many times as you like at no extra cost: One ticket, a
whole year of adventures.

events.description:
This summer we've got three fun activities in the kitchen, all delving into food chemistry
and how we can eat sustainably.

Learn a bit more about what our food is made of and some of the hidden chemistry that goes
in to cooking, have a fun tasting experience and learn some new foody skills to try at home!

**Activities on offer:**

- **The Big Green Grill-Off** — Love a BBQ? Not sure about all the meat? Become a
  sustainable chef as you invent and cook your own meat-free burgers.
- **Supercool Sorbet** — How can salt help things freeze? Use some clever chemistry to make
  sorbet in minutes.
- **Will it Mix?** — We've heard that oil and water don't mix but, with a bit of science, we
  reckon they might. It's time to get saucy – and make some mayonnaise!

Activities running will vary depending on term time verses weekends and holidays. Please
always check the activity screens on arrival to see which activities are running at what
time each day.

**Accessibility / allergens** — This activity takes place on a raised kitchen counter. When
the venue is busy, you may need to share space and equipment with other visitors. Allergens
include milk, eggs and gluten though the activity can be adapted. Please speak to a member
of staff about any allergies before taking part.

events.title: Besides the Sea
events.raw:
01 August - 25 October 2026

Besides the Sea

What does living in Weston, and in similar coastal towns, mean for young people trying to build creative lives today? Besides the Sea celebrates the many ways creativity shapes life…
events.summary: Gallery 5 show on what living in Weston-super-Mare and similar coastal towns means for young people trying to build creative lives.
events.description:
*Besides the Sea* celebrates the many ways creativity shapes life in
Weston: how it brings people together, enriches everyday experiences,
amplifies new voices and helps us imagine new possibilities.

The exhibition brings together work by six young artists based in
Bristol and Weston. The work was developed through workshops led by
artist Jamie Dormer-Durling, connected to *Against the Tide* (27 June –
27 September 2026), a project developed by photographer Polly Braden in
collaboration with journalist Lisa Bachelor for *The Guardian*'s
Seascape series.

Inside the gallery, photographs by Bayan Alahmad, Archie Byron, Braden
Evans, Siobhan Evans, Jess May Long and Will Shergold explore place,
identity and creativity through their personal experiences of growing
up in Weston. Their work weaves together everyday moments, memories,
dreams and nostalgia, the textures of the natural environment, and the
rhythms of working-class culture — revealing the quiet beauty found
within Weston's streets, shorelines and communities. The exhibition
also features a collaborative poem written by the young people with
poet Beth Calverley.

Along the corridor walls, Weston's creative landscape — nurtured over
the years by residents and organisations such as Super Culture and
Common Waves CIC — unfolds through vibrant snapshots of gatherings,
public artworks and interventions, with Calverley's words woven
throughout.

Once a small fishing village, then a Victorian seaside resort, and now
a regenerated coastal town with a growing arts scene, Weston provides
the backdrop for this exploration of how creativity can shape a place
and the people who call it home.

events.description:
A special programme of walks designed to explore the Blaise Estate and celebrate 100
years of public ownership.

Each walk focuses on an aspect of the estate's rich wildlife, its historical
connections or its archaeological discoveries. Walk leaders will take you for a gentle
stroll to different parts of the park sharing what makes the Blaise Estate so special.

**Hidden Blaise** — Join the estate rangers for a guided tour around the estate and
visit areas usually closed to the public. Dates: Sunday 25 October. Time: 11am–12:30pm.

**Blaise Community Garden** — A guided tour around the Community Garden to learn about
the history of the site and how its changed over the years. If you want to discover
how a thriving community garden works then this is the tour for you! Dates: Saturday 15
August, Saturday 19 September. Times: 2pm to 3pm.

**Archaeology and wildlife** — Join the team from Blaise Museum and the Bristol
Regional Environmental Records Centre (BRERC) to find out more about Blaise's
archaeological discoveries and rich wildlife. Dates: Thursday 10 September. Time:
11am–12:30pm.

**Humphrey Repton's landscape** — Join the team from Blaise Museum and explore the
picturesque parkland created for the Harford Family by the famous landscape designer
Humphrey Repton. Dates: Thursday 8 October. Time: 11am–12:30pm.

**St Mary's Church and churchyard** — A guided walk exploring St Mary's church and
churchyard. Learn about the history of this amazing space, the historic memorials and
its links to Bristol's merchant history. Dates: Thursday 22 October. Time:
11am–12:30pm.

All walks last around 90 minutes and start from Blaise Museum unless otherwise stated.
Please arrive at least five minutes before the start of the walk. Suitable outdoor
clothing and a bottle of water are recommended. This event may have to be cancelled at
short notice due external factors such as weather conditions. Tours will go ahead in
wet weather unless the conditions are extreme. Well behaved dogs on leads are only
permitted on walks that specify this in the information above.

Free, donations welcome. Booking essential.

events.title: Bristol's Grenfell Memorial Panel
events.raw:
**Bristol's Grenfell Memorial Panel** — Mon 17 Aug | 10:00 – 16:00, to Mon 14 Sep.

Bristol Cathedral is honoured to display Bristol Star Stitchers' contribution to the Grenfell Memorial Quilt, a moving tribute to all those affected by the Grenfell Tower disaster.

Bristol Star Stitchers have created a 12ft x 12ft panel honours the 72 people who died in the fire on 14 June 2017, as well as those who survived, were injured, or lost their homes. It forms part of a nationwide memorial project inspired by a call from relatives and friends of those affected, with around 90 panels created by groups across the UK ahead of the disaster's tenth anniversary in 2027.

At the heart of the panel are 72 embroidered stars, each bearing the name and age of a person who died. Families and loved ones are stitched close together, reflecting the lives, relationships and communities behind the headlines.

Free admission. All welcome.
events.summary: Last three days of Bristol's twelve-foot panel for the national Grenfell Memorial Quilt, stitched by more than thirty people from recycled charity-shop fabric and carrying 72 embroidered stars, one for each person who died. Free, in the cathedral until Monday 14 September.

events.description:
Shaun the Sheep is coming to Bristol Zoo Project for Aardman's 50th Anniversary!

This August Bank Holiday ONLY, Shaun the Sheep will be joining us for a weekend of
fun at our Aardman Summer Special!

Meet Shaun the Sheep, take part in Shaun's Wildlife Mission trail, make your very
own clay model of Shaun or get creative with our fun activity pack! All FREE at
Bristol Zoo Project in celebration of Aardman's 50th Anniversary.

**Meet Shaun the Sheep!** Shaun will be at the zoo every day between 28-31 August
inclusive, making appearances at regular intervals throughout the day. So remember
to bring your camera when you visit!

**Join a Claystation.** Make your own Shaun the Sheep at our Aardman Claystation in
Bear Wood. Book your place online with your ticket.

**Complete your Wildlife Mission.** Join Shaun on a Wildlife Mission with Friends —
solve the challenges, collect the stamps and complete the mission!

**Activity packs.** Get your FREE activity pack on entry! Filled with baa-rilliant
crafts, puzzles and colouring.

All activities are FREE with entry!

More info: Aardman Claystations are free with a Bristol Zoo Project ticket or
membership; workshops must be booked online with your entry ticket. One booked slot
qualifies for one attendee. Carers must remain with children at all times during the
workshop. Head to Bear Wood Classroom for your timeslot. A self-led activity, guided
by an instruction sheet and a member of our team. You can take your model home with
you, a bag will be provided. Please note, animation is not part of the activity.
Recommended for ages 6+.

Shaun will be making regular appearances throughout the day; meeting him is free
with entry. Due to his popularity there will likely be a wait. Meet and greet takes
place at the picnic area opposite the Wilder gorilla sculpture and timings are
displayed on the area board. Activity packs can be collected at the entrance.

From the event terms: "There is no entry fee for the Claystation or Shaun the Sheep
Meet and Greet. However, it is only available to visitors to Bristol Zoo Project
between Friday 28 and Monday 31 August 2026."

folklore come to life through oral storytelling. Old stories are
given the space to become relevant and meaningful to contemporary

"FORWARDS Festival returns to Bristol for another year with its most ambitious and..." TEMS, SELF ESTEEM, WET LEG, LITTLE SIMZ AND MORE!
events.summary: Forwards' fifth edition on Clifton Downs over the bank holiday weekend, headlined Saturday by Tems, Self Esteem and Wet Leg and Sunday by Little Simz, Amyl & The Sniffers and Dijon.
events.description:
**TEMS, SELF ESTEEM, WET LEG, LITTLE SIMZ AND MORE!**

FORWARDS Festival returns to Bristol for another year with its most ambitious and musically expansive programme to date. Taking place at Clifton Downs on Saturday 29th and Sunday 30th August 2026, the festival celebrates its fifth anniversary with a powerful lineup of global stars, genre-spanning artists, and boundary-pushing performances.

Across two days of music, culture and conversation, FORWARDS continues its mission to spotlight both internationally acclaimed acts and emerging voices — a formula that has helped it become one of the UK's most forward-thinking festivals.

### Headliners for the 2026 Lineup

Saturday's lineup is led by an all-female trio of headliners. Grammy Award-winning Nigerian superstar Tems will make her Bristol headline debut, bringing her soulful, globally influential take on R&B to the Downs. She will be joined by British pop powerhouse Self Esteem, known for her bold, theatrical performances and outspoken lyricism, and indie favourites Wet Leg, whose sharp wit and infectious energy have made them one of the UK's most exciting bands of recent years.

On Sunday, the festival shifts gears with another genre-spanning headline bill. Little Simz, the Mercury Prize-winning rapper widely regarded as one of the most important voices in British hip-hop, takes top billing alongside Australian punk firebrands Amyl & The Sniffers and acclaimed American singer-songwriter Dijon, who will also be performing in Bristol for the first time.

### Saturday 29th August

Tems · Self Esteem · Wet Leg · Joy Crookes · Tricky · Goldie (Live) · Paraorchestra presents Kraftwerk Re:Werk with Charles Hazlewood · Special Guests: Maribou State

### Sunday 30th August

Little Simz · Amyl & The Sniffers · Dijon · Viagra Boys · Oklou · Jim Legxacy · Princess Nokia · Jean Dawson · Gena ft. Liv.e & Karriem Riggins · Anaiis

### More Than a Music Festival

Since launching in 2022, FORWARDS has established itself as more than just a music event. Alongside the performances, the festival's "The Information" stage will return in 2026, offering discussions, debates and talks.

international music to Bristol Downs. The festival aims to present high
quality, diverse and heritage music acts alongside emerging artists from
Bristol & beyond.

The festival presents a contemporary curation of music while paying homage
to Bristol's long standing history of being a music city. In addition,
FORWARDS is more than just a music festival, it looks to challenge what
metropolitan festivals can be today and how they can do good, from the
inside out. The 2-day festival aims to harness the power of live events to
bring people together for incredible music moments and lasting positive
change.

At the heart of the festival is FORWARDS THINKING, a platform for year round
social initiatives in Bristol, all through our partners, Big Team CIC and
Team Canteen CIC. Alongside these partners is The Information, a dedicated
space at FORWARDS for debate and understanding on today's current affairs
and cultural issues.

events.description:
Take a steam train ride on Bristol Harbour Railway from M Shed. The train will be pulled
by the locomotive Henbury.

Bristol Harbour Railway was built by the Great Western Railway in the 1870s and extended
in the 1900s. After a century as a goods railway, it was handed over to the museum and
has run as a heritage railway ever since. The railway runs on the quayside between
M Shed and the SS Great Britain.

Our two Bristol-built steam locomotives, Henbury and Portbury, served their working lives
on the docks railway system at Avonmouth. The wagons are types once commonly seen on the
docks at Avonmouth and here in the old City Docks.

- Saturday 29 to Monday 31 August
- Saturday 12 and Sunday 13 September
- Saturday 26 and Sunday 27 September
- Saturday 10 and Sunday 11 October
- Saturday 24 and Sunday 25 October
- Saturday 31 and Sunday 1 November

Please note, M Shed’s large working exhibits are operated by volunteers. Occasionally
crew shortages, mechanical difficulties or adverse weather conditions may force us to
alter or cancel the advertised event. We advise you to check with us to avoid
disappointment by calling 0117 352 6600.

**Booking information.** Please note train rides are running on weekends only. Buy
tickets on the day from the ticket office by the M Shed platform. Single £3.50 /
Return £5. Children under six years old travel free. Dogs welcome. From 11am – subject

events.description:
**PART CHIMP**

_Part Chimp have long made it their mission to shake speakers, fry brains and push volume to its limits. Underground legends of primal riffing, their fifth album Drool sees them sharpen that intensity into something even more focused and ferocious._

_Blending crushing heaviness with a skewed sense of melody, Drool channels echoes of Melvins and Sonic Youth while carving out a sound that’s wholly their own — pulverising, chaotic and strangely life-affirming. Tracks like Back From The Dead, Drool and Up, With Notes showcase a band revelling in the alchemy of loud amps, strange tunings and raw instinct._

_Recorded across London, New York and Somerset, the album captures the band at their most honest and unfiltered. Equal parts panic, chaos and catharsis, Part Chimp’s music thrives on the edge of collapse — shambolic, unpredictable and full of joy._

_Drool is loud, enveloping and uncompromising — a blast of heavy music that hits as hard as it exhilarates._

**AAA GRIPPER**

_AAA Gripper emerged from the first Wrong Speed Records festival in Glastonbury in 2023. Built from long bass-and-drum improvisations and shaped into tense, wiry post-punk, the band quickly developed a reputation for explosive live shows and unpredictable songwriting. Featuring members connected to acts including Sweet Williams and Hey Colossus, AAA Gripper balance tightly wound grooves with jagged guitar work and a restless experimental streak._

_Their debut album 'We Invented Work For The Common Good' dissects the absurdities of modern working life through frontman M. Edward Cole’s stream-of-consciousness lyrics, dark humour and anxious intensity. Channeling the rhythmic force of Fugazi and The Jesus Lizard, AAA Gripper have quickly become one of the UK underground’s most exciting new post-punk bands._

**RESURRECTION MEN**

_RESURRECTION MEN are a brand new heavy band, featuring members of SANS, Modern Rituals, and Talons._

events.summary: A-Sun Amissa x Lauren Mason/ Rowan Evans/ Samatar Elmi x Roscian at Exchange, drone, experimental and poetry, doors 14:15.
events.description:
An afternoon featuring some of the UK's most innovative poets and musicians, collaborating across language and sound!

In _Water Scores,_ **Lauren Mason’s** dark and experimental poetics respond to **A-Sun Amissa’s** tide-like currents of guitar, synth, sampled hydrophone, loops, and clarinet. This long-form piece ranges through deep ambience, crashing chaos and ebbing aftermath. During this new work Mason explores the curses of corporate extraction and pollution on our planet’s water, and listens in, as water speaks back.

**Rowan Evans** will be performing his poem and sound sequence _The Last Verses of Beccán,_ plus some new material. Bilingual poetry and sound composition explore medieval hermitage, sea-exile, ecology and language hybridity, with field recordings made in the inner Hebrides. New unreleased material will combine Ancient Greek translation and dream lyric with tape samples, drum loops, synths and bass.

**Samatar Elmi and Roscian (solo)** will be performing a brand new collaboration featuring Samatar's highly charged political poetry, freestyle rap and gospel singing, alongside Roscian's darkly heavy synth and sample soundscapes. Not one to miss!

**Artist bios:**

**Lauren Mason** is best known as bassist with now-defunct existential sludge band Torpor, where she often wove her spoken word pieces through heavy soundscapes. She has been developing her poetic practice for many years and published her first pamphlet ‘Rust Canyon’ in 2025.

**A-Sun Amissa** are a group in a permanent state of metamorphosis, existing on the fringes of some kind of avant-rock, relentlessly pushing forward, shapeshifting and presenting their unique noise in new ways and on their own terms. A sound underpinned and overlaid with drones, moving in and around a diverse chasm of post-rock, melancholic drone, noise, doom and ambient sounds.

**Rowan Evans** is a poet, composer and sound artist whose debut collection _A Method, A Path_ (Bloomsbury Poetry, 2023) was shortlisted for the Forward Prize. His chapbook _The Last Verses of Beccán_ (Guillemot Press, 2019) won the Michael Marks Award for Poetry. He received an Eric Gregory Award in 2015 and a selection of his work appears in _Penguin Modern Poets 7: These Hard and Shining Things_ (Penguin, 2018). Evans records and performs music for theatre, dance, film and art installation.

**Samatar Elmi** is an award-winning writer, musician and educator. His debut pamphlet, ‘Portrait of Colossus’ (flipped eye press, 2021), was selected as a PBS Pamphlet Choice. His stunning debut collection, ‘The Epic of Cader Idris’ (Bloomsbury, 2024), includes the 2021 Geoffrey Dearmer Prize winning poem. His poems have appeared widely including in Poetry, Prairie Schooner, Poetry Review, Poetry Wales, Magma, and Iota and anthologised in More Fiya, Filigree, After Plath, and The Echoing Gallery. Elmi is an Obsidian Fellow, flipped eye press associate poetry editor, and is a specialist tutor in 'Neurodiversity and the Creative Process'. He is currently touring nationally throughout 2026, reading from a pair of collections ( Agen Bien Fou, Kulvert Books, 2026; and Reclamations: Disregard Prior Prompt ,Aout Fecit, 2026).

As Knomad Spock, his debut album, ‘Winter of Discontent’ was critically acclaimed in print (Clash Magazine, Afropunk, GoldFlakePaint, Equate Magazine) and radio (BBC 6 Music, BBC Wales, Amazing Radio, Radio X). His recent albums ‘A Darker Light’ and ‘Through the Walls’ are available on Bandcamp. He raps under his own name and has recorded with UK hiphop luminaries, Jesht and Chester P.

**Roscian (solo)** is Simon Mason, better known as drummer of existential sludge band Torpor. Roscian sees him creating a different kind of heaviness with synthesis and samples.

Doors 14:00 for a prompt start! Music over by 16:40

events.description:
An enchanting tale of ritual magic and misfortune set by the sea in 1917 – a brand-new show from acclaimed folk theatre company Riddlestick Theatre (*Barleycorn*, *The Cabinet of Madame Fanny Du Thé*)

Lizard Point, 1917. While the war grinds on in France, the mysterious Crow and his company of runaways spend their days in a fever of conjured dreams. In their refuge amongst the cliffs, hidden away from the prying eyes of the police, the troupe rejoice in strange rituals and tales of long-lost loves.

But the tides are turning. Crow has taken to watching the sea. The voices of the dead are getting louder. And when a soldier from the front line washes up on the rocks nearby, the truth about Crow, and Lizard Point, threatens to drown them all.

A brand-new show from acclaimed folk theatre company Riddlestick Theatre, conjuring a darkly comic blend of occult intrigue and enchanting live music.

**Performances:** Sun 30th August at 7:00 pm, Mon 31st August at 7:30 pm, Tue 1st September at 7:30 pm. Tickets £14. Running time 75 mins (no interval). Suitable for ages 12+.

the song has no ending present

Virtuoso songwriting from far and near FFO: Cameron Winter, Weyes Blood, BCNR, Rundgren, Nilsson

Skydaddy is the moniker of London-born Lebanese/Grenadian songwriter-producer/artist, Rachid Fakhre. He has released two mini-albums through his own label Bathtime Sounds as well as albums of his former project, Spang Sisters. This year he will be releasing his debut solo album and will be supporting Geese on their UK shows in the run-up. He (and his band) will be stopping off at The Cube for a very special show midway.

Southern California singer-songwriter Mia Wilson (and band) will be gracing the cube with her debut UK performance before going on to play End of the Road Festival. Mia's self titled LP - Produced by Tim Ramsey (Vetiver, Little Wings, Kacey Johansing) - blends piano and guitar based compositions with lush orchestral arrangements to create a backdrop for her introspective lyrics and captivating mezzo-soprano vocals. The album recalls the golden glow of late 60's & early 70's LA records like Carole King's Tapestry, Judee Sill's Heart Food, and Jackson Browne's Late For the Sky.

North Yorkshire born folk-songwriter Nile Robinson began performing live music after moving to Bristol in 2023. His work blends influences of American Primitive, Anti-Folk & Glock-Rock across an eclectic array of instrumentation.

events.description:
**Whether you’re a fan of the series or looking to delve into romance fiction, our Romance book club offers a joyful escape. We're building a community to gush over swoon-worthy characters and a safe space to discuss themes like relationships. With *ACOTAR 6* coming out this Autumn, our Romance Book Club is reading through the entire series in anticipation of its release. **

**In August, we will be looking at Books 3 and 4 in Sarah J Maas' *A Court of Thorns and Roses *Series. Let’s share the love!**

**Date:**
Monday 31st of August

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**
Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *A COURT OF WINGS AND RUIN (BOOK THREE)***

Feyre has returned to the Spring Court, determined to gather information on Tamlin's manoeuvrings and the invading king threatening to bring her land to its knees. But to do so she must play a deadly game of deceit – and one slip may spell doom not only for Feyre, but for her world as well.

As war bears down upon them all, Feyre must decide who to trust amongst the dazzling and lethal High Lords and hunt for allies in unexpected places. And her heart will face the ultimate test as she and her mate are forced to question whether they can truly trust each other.

**ABOUT *A COURT OF FROST AND STARLIGHT (BOOK FOUR)***

In this companion tale to the bestselling *A Court of Thorns and Roses** series*, Feyre, Rhys and their friends are working to rebuild the Night Court and the vastly changed world beyond after the events of *A Court of Wings and Ruin*.

But Winter Solstice is finally near, and with it a hard-earned reprieve. Yet even the festive atmosphere can't keep the shadows of the past from looming. As Feyre navigates her first Winter Solstice as High Lady, she finds that those dearest to her have more wounds than she anticipated – scars that will have a far-reaching impact on the future of their court.

***ABOUT SARAH J. MAAS***

**Sarah J. Maas** is the #1 bestselling author of the Court of Thorns and Roses, Throne of Glass, and Crescent City series. Her books have sold more than seventy-five million copies and are published in forty languages.

Tue, 1 Sept 2026 10:00 – Tue, 8 Sept 2026 18:00.
Centrespace Gallery & Studios, 6 Leonard Lane, Bristol BS1 1EA.

For the duration of *Searching for the Future: A decade of reportage
illustration*, artist Niki Groom will be transforming Centrespace
Gallery into a giant sketchbook. The illustrated stories of people
she's met will adorn the walls, resulting in a colourful display of
community.

**Exhibition Dates:** Tuesday 1st September - Tuesday 8th September
**PV:** Friday 4th September, 6:00 - 9:00 pm
**Opening Hours:** Daily, 11:00 am - 6:00 pm
events.summary: Ten years of Niki Groom's reportage illustration, hung as if the gallery were one enormous sketchbook of the people she has drawn. The first show after the bank holiday gap.
events.description:
For this exhibition, artist Niki Groom will be transforming Centrespace
Gallery into a giant sketchbook. The walls will carry the illustrated
stories of people she's met — life-size paintings of dancers and
musicians, and a celebration of events that bring people together, such
as festivals, protests, sport and food.

Groom has specialised in reportage illustration for the humanitarian
and cultural sectors since 2016, when she documented the Calais
'Jungle' for Choose Love — creating impactful imagery that allows
people to remain anonymous. She has worked with local organisations
including Refugee Women of Bristol and Bristol Refugee Festival.

The exhibition includes workshops, talks on creativity and community, a
sketching table, and merchandise featuring original artwork.

**Dates:** Tuesday 1 September 11:00 – Tuesday 8 September 2026 18:00
**Private View:** Friday 4th September, 6:00 – 9:00 pm
**Opening Hours:** Daily, 11:00 am – 6:00 pm
**Entry:** Admission is free; tickets are not required.

events.raw:
**Charity Shop World launch with Tansy E. Hoskins** — Bookhaus

Tuesday 1st September, 18:00. Genres: workshops & classes, talks.

Headfirst Editor's Pick: "The feel-good alternative to the skip and the
shopping centre, or just another stop on the conveyor belt? Tansy E.
Hoskins' Charity Shop World delivers a reality check on the afterlife of
your donated wares, interweaving far-reaching research into overconsumption
with her personal experiences of the shop floor."
events.summary: Tansy E. Hoskins on what actually happens to the bags you drop at the charity shop, from the sorting floor to overseas landfill. Ticket includes a drink and £2 off the book.
events.description:
Have you ever wondered what happens to the contents of the bags you drop off
at the charity shop?

With over 80 billion pieces of clothing produced each year and with human
made stuff now outweighing living biomass, this is the story of the first
sorting site for the deluge of items we discard every single day.

Having spent decades exploring charity shops for bargains and treasure,
Tansy Hoskins decided to dig deep into the world of charity shop
volunteering. From used underwear to wolf pelts, *Charity Shop World* is a
personal account of sorting through donations to reveal the entanglement of
people and products. This book also investigates the export of clothes to
overseas markets and landfill, revealing hidden shareholders behind a
multi-million pound business.

Taking us to the heart of a country hit by austerity and the cost of living
crisis, *Charity Shop World* reveals surprising places of human
connectivity, where local communities struggle to find their way through
economic hardship to reach a more sustainable way of living.

Tansy will be joining us to discuss all this. Tickets cost £7 and include a
glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off the book. Presented by bookhaus.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

events.title: The World Beneath Our Feet launch with Frank Ashwood

price.text: £7 including a glass of wine or soft drink and £3 off the book (£7.60 with the booking fee)

events.raw:
**The World Beneath Our Feet launch with Frank Ashwood** — Bookhaus

Wednesday 2nd September, 18:00. Genres: workshops & classes, talks.

Headfirst Editor's Pick: "Subterranean ecologist Frank Ashwood launches a
low-key revolution in pop-science soil biodiversity. He's in the Haus
lifting the lid on the neglected universe of beetles, earthworms, microbes
and life-giving dirt."
events.summary: Soil ecologist Frank Ashwood on the most biodiverse habitat on the planet, in conversation with Josiah Judson of the Soil Association. Drink and £3 off the book included.
events.description:
To appreciate the wonders of the world around us, we're often told to look
up. But what if we need to look down instead?

Everything that happens below ground sustains all life above it — yet we
rarely think about this mysterious, dark underland. In *The World Beneath
Our Feet* soil ecologist Frank Ashwood scratches the surface and takes us on
an eye-opening safari through this precious ecosystem, from the ancient
forests of New Zealand to the vast black soil deposits of the US and China.

The ground beneath our feet hums with a staggering abundance of winding
roots, interconnecting fungal networks, wriggling creatures and mind-blowing
microbial life. This hidden ecosystem is the single most biodiverse habitat
on the planet. Half of all our species exist underfoot, and just a handful
of soil can contain an entire world. Without soil, there would be no life as
we know it.

In a story of connection and communication, we meet pioneering plants and
minute animals that are essential to the health and wellbeing of our planet.
We learn how soil makes our very existence possible, allowing us to
cultivate crops as well as storing precious carbon and the water we need to
survive.

Frank Ashwood will be in conversation with Josiah Judson (Soil Association).
Tickets cost £7 and include a glass of wine or soft drink and £3 off the
book. Presented by bookhaus.

Josiah is a soil scientist within the Soil Association's Farming and Land
Use team, contributing to European research programmes and advising on
technical soil health issues in the UK.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

events.raw: **The Light House** — Weds 2nd Sept 2026. 7.30pm. £14. Alys Williams & Company present a real-life love story about holding onto each other, even in the darkest times – tender, funny and defiantly hopeful, it's a love letter to life
events.summary: Alys Williams & Company's true-story love letter to holding on, one night only.
events.description:
*'Man overboard, man overboard! Call control. Blow the whistle.'*

Love is a complicated business. It gets even more complicated when the person you love doesn't want to be alive. Tender, funny and defiantly hopeful, *The Light House* is a real-life story of falling in love and staying in love, even when the lights go out and you're lost in the dark. Join the emergency response as we dance in the kitchen, sing in the streets and try to turn the lights back on. It gets lonely, muddling through these days and nights. So why don't we do it together?

*The Light House* is the highly acclaimed debut play of theatre artist, Aly Williams.

**Date:** Wednesday, 2nd September 2026, 7:30pm. Tickets £14. Running time 1 hour (no interval). Suitable for ages 12+.

**Content warnings:** References to depression, suicide/suicidal ideation and hospitalisation.

events.title: Free mindful eating information session
events.raw:
**Free mindful eating information session** — Thu 03 September 2026, 13:00
- 14:30, online: Microsoft Teams. Free, booking required. A free session
explaining mindfulness and mindful eating, and what the Mindful Eating -
Conscious Living programme entails.
events.summary: A free online orientation for UWE's eight-week Mindful Eating course, including a short guided practice. Open to anyone over 18.
events.description:
Mindful Eating - Conscious Living is an eight-week mindfulness programme
that will help you to establish a regular mindfulness practice, and help
you to make better choices to manage your mood and stress levels.

The focus will be around learning how to be less anxious and more at
ease around food and eating. By practicing paying attention to the
present moment, without judgement, we can cultivate the capacity to tune
into the physical experience of eating and how they relate to our moods
and emotions. In time, we can regain our natural freedom around food.

This short course is appropriate for anyone over the age of 18 who is
interested in mindfulness meditation or mindful eating. You need to be
willing to practise the in-class exercises at home between sessions, to
fully benefit from the programme.

**Registration and tickets.** The orientation session is a chance to find
out more about the course and ask any questions you may have. It will
also be an opportunity for you to experience a short practice in a small
group environment, which can help you to assess whether this course is
right for you at this time. Upon completion of your orientation session,
you will be invited to formally register on the course and pay your
course fees via the UWE Bristol WPM System. Attendance at the orientation
session is a course requirement.

Cost: Free. Attendance: booking required. This is an online event on
Microsoft Teams.

A free monthly meet-up for creatives, artists and technologists
interested in making things happen in/with communities.

Whether you already work with communities or are curious to begin,
you're welcome here - all that's needed is a genuine interest in
community-centred, collaborative ways of making. These meet-ups are
always evolving in response to the group. Currently, they range from
hands-on making, reflection, project-sharing, artist-led workshops and
inspiration.

events.ageRestriction: 16+; under 18s must be accompanied by a 21+ adult on a 1:1 ratio
events.raw: **The People's Comedy** — Sep 4, 19:00–22:00. £8.
events.summary: Grassroots political, social and cultural comedy with no headliner and every act paid, run to fund the collectively owned PRSC building. Winner of Chortle's Best Comedy Format 2026 for South West & Wales.
events.description:
A night of political, social and cultural comedy featuring some of the
most exciting grassroots comedians of Bristol and beyond – and the acts
ACTUALLY get paid. Come join the revolution!

The founding principle is platforming comedians with a message (think
counter-culture, underrepresented, original) and ensuring that they're
paid for their craft. There are no headliners, so each performer's
comedic voice gets room. Proceeds support the collectively owned PRSC
building: the more they make through tickets, the more they can pay
acts, so attendees are encouraged to contribute what they can afford.

The night has won multiple Chortle awards, including Best Comedy Format
2026 for South West & Wales.

16+; under 18s must be accompanied by a 21+ adult on a 1:1 ratio. Bar
opens at 7pm, show starts 7:30pm. Tickets via Headfirst Bristol.

events.title: Kaleidoscope Fusion – Dance Night
events.raw: **Kaleidoscope Fusion – Dance Night** — Sep 5, 19:30–23:00. £5.
events.summary: A fusion social dance party — partner dancing without the baggage — opening with an all-levels intro workshop and running into DJ sets. No partner or experience needed; sliding-scale entry.
events.description:
We throw dance parties where all bodies are invited. You already know
how to dance, we're just here to give you permission to embrace all of
the ways your body wants to move.

The evening opens with an all-levels workshop at 7:45pm, with local
teachers offering an intro to social dancing, followed by DJs playing
tracks ranging from slow and squishy to high-energy bangers. No partner
or prior experience is necessary.

One core principle: be excellent to one another — respect boundaries
and consent. Fusion is partner dancing, without the baggage, fusing
various dance styles through improvisation. The organisers note their
approach is queer, it is feminist, and they don't want anyone left
behind.

The single-level venue provides accessible entry from pavement to
dancefloor, with modifications available on request.

Sliding scale: £5 (low income), £10 (general release), £15
(pay-it-forward). Tickets via hdfst.uk/kaleidoscope-fusion.

events.description:
## Stand Up For The Weekend with Andrew Bird Featuring Javier Jarquin & compere Ross Smith

#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly show from The Comedy Box featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: ANDREW BIRD

Andrew Bird is a top headline act throughout the UK and Ireland and has performed all around the world. He is highly in demand as a tour support for big name comics such as Rhod Gilbert, Rob Brydon, Jon Richardson and Michael McIntyre playing venues such as Wembley and O2 arenas, and is one of the hardest working TV warm-up acts in the industry having worked on shows as varied as Pointless, Have I Got News For You, The Jonathan Ross Show and Taskmaster.

There is a very good reason for Andrew Bird’s popularity. He is always funny and frequently hilarious. He’s a nimble storyteller, with a relaxed, personable style. He simply proves cracking company, whether he’s got an angle or not. Fast, fluid and animated, you might mistake his relentless chatter for a spontaneous stream of consciousness, were it not so effortlessly reliable in generating laughs.

#### “*A great storyteller, funny, likeable and effortless*” Time Out

#### “*Comedy gold…Bird’s going to be a big star, catch him close-up now*” The Scotsman

#### [andrewbirdcomedian.com](https://www.andrewbirdcomedian.com/)

**Free mindful eating information session** — Mon 07 September 2026, 10:30
- 12:00, online: Microsoft Teams. Free, booking required. A free session
explaining mindfulness and mindful eating, and what the Mindful Eating -
Conscious Living programme entails.
events.summary: The second, morning orientation session for UWE's Mindful Eating course, online and free to attend.
events.description:
Mindful Eating - Conscious Living is an eight-week mindfulness programme
that will help you to establish a regular mindfulness practice, and help
you to make better choices to manage your mood and stress levels.

The focus will be around learning how to be less anxious and more at
ease around food and eating. By practicing paying attention to the
present moment, without judgement, we can cultivate the capacity to tune
into the physical experience of eating and how it relates to our moods
and emotions. In time we can regain our natural freedom around food.

This short course is appropriate for anyone over the age of 18 who is
interested in mindfulness meditation or mindful eating. You need to be
willing to practise the in-class exercises at home between sessions, to
fully benefit from the programme.

**Registration and tickets.** If you are interested in this course, you
will be invited to attend an orientation session. The orientation session
is a chance to find out more about the course and ask any questions you
may have. It will also be an opportunity for you to experience a short
practice in a small group environment, which can help you to assess
whether this course is right for you at this time. On completion of your
orientation session, you will be invited to formally register on the
course and pay your course fees via the UWE Bristol WPM System.
Attendance at the orientation session is a course requirement.

Cost: Free. Attendance: booking required. This is an online event on
Microsoft Teams.

price.text: Free etickets — the event is free, but please book your place in advance

events.raw:
**Fakers with Rory Cormac in partnership with Bristol Radical History
Group** — Bookhaus

Monday 7th September, 18:00. Genres: workshops & classes, talks.
Free etickets.
events.summary: A free evening with Professor Rory Cormac on the Information Research Department, Britain's secret Cold War disinformation unit, followed by a Q&A chaired by the Bristol Radical History Group's Rosie Wild. Book ahead.
events.description:
Bristol Radical History Group and Bookhaus are delighted to present Professor
Rory Cormac speaking about his new book *Fakers*, a history of Britain's
little known governmental disinformation and propaganda unit, the
Information Research Department.

Published in May 2026, *Fakers: a top-secret tale of phantoms and forgeries
on the disinformation front line* is based on 8,000 recently declassified
documents and covers the Information Research Department's covert work
countering communism from the 1950s to its demise in 1977. It offers
important insight into current questions of countering disinformation and in
conceptualising Black Propaganda more widely.

Professor Cormac's international archival research provides insight into how
the IRD's targets and recipients perceived British propaganda and the
process by which propaganda was developed, highlighting the role of local
and regional actors in places like Sub-Saharan Africa.

The event is free, but please book your place in advance. Professor Cormac's
talk will be followed by a Q&A with the audience, chaired by BRHG's Rosie
Wild, who has researched the IRD's domestic connections with Britain's secret
SDS spycops unit.

Rory Cormac is a Professor of International Relations at the University of
Nottingham and a Fellow of the Royal Historical Society. He is the author or
co-author of six books, including *How to Stage a Coup* (2022), *Disrupt and
Deny* (2018), and *The Secret Royals* (2021).

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

events.summary: A ninety-minute gong and singing-bowl session led by Rounik Sound Healing, with breathwork and a chakra-balancing guided meditation, high above the gorge.
events.description:
Relax, re-balance mind & body in a heart-opening, healing Sound Bath with breath taking
views of Bristol's iconic suspension bridge.

Join the experience led by Rounik Sound Healing at Clifton Observatory. Participants
will find themselves in a tranquil and grounding setting of soothing candles,
glimmering fairy-lights, and the serene sounds of gongs, singing bowls and sacred
chimes.

The session includes a journey of relaxation, guided meditation and sound therapy.
Spaces are limited; attendees should bring yoga mats and blankets.

Sound healing offers a relaxing and re-tuning experience that assists our brain to
enter deeper, slower states and encourages physical repair on a cellular level. The
practice supports emotional processing and life transitions.

The session begins with a check-in and intention-setting, followed by breathwork for

events.title: The Breaking of the English Working Class launch with Jonas Patrick Marvin

price.text: £7 including a glass of wine or a soft drink and £2 off the book (£7.60 with the booking fee)

events.raw:
**The Breaking of the English Working Class launch with Jonas Patrick
Marvin** — Bookhaus

Tuesday 8th September, 18:00. Genres: workshops & classes, talks.

Headfirst Editor's Pick: "Jonas Patrick Marvin safely detonates his tome of
socialist history in Bookhaus; The Breaking of The English Working Class is
a radical revision of our impossibly fractured class consciousness at a time
when we might need it the most."
events.summary: Jonas Patrick Marvin on forty years of class politics from Thatcher to the gig economy, with Shanice McBean, his co-host on The Life of the Party podcast.
events.description:
What has become of the English working class in the twenty-first century?

After a decades-long absence, class is once again central to our
understanding of ailing Britain. But what does it mean to be working class
today? As Jonas Patrick Marvin shows, questions of class have often been
replaced by talk of race and geography. Meanwhile, a collective identity
capable of pushing for change has become increasingly weakened and sidelined.

Retelling the story of the working class over the last forty years — from
Thatcher's war against the unions to New Labour neoliberalism — Marvin shows
how power and capital have combined to shatter a radical identity into many
parts: white, male, northerner, homeowner, immigrant, unemployed, disabled.
These fragments are then set in conflict against each other. Blending
political analysis with an account of his own experiences of class in London
and the rustbelt Midlands, Marvin shows how the working class have been
demonised and managed into impotence.

The working class is more than just an identity. As Marvin argues, it
embodies a collective will to demand change, one that can — and must — be
rekindled.

Jonas will be here at bookhaus to discuss all this in conversation with
Shanice McBean, his co-presenter on The Life of the Party podcast. Tickets
cost £7 and include a glass of wine or a soft drink and £2 off the book.
Presented by bookhaus.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

Tuesday 8th September, Gloucester Road Bookshop at 7.00 pm

events.summary: The shop opens its autumn season with Karishma Jobanputra's debut short story collection, in conversation with the poet and novelist Nell Osborne.
events.description:
Our autumn events programme begins with the brilliant Karishma Jobanputra
who will be discussing her scintillating short story collection, *The Body
of the Thing*, in conversation with award-winning poet and novelist, Nell
Osborne.

One of 2026's most anticipated debuts, the stories in *The Body of the
Thing*, at their core, examine the myriad ways in which women negotiate all
manner of body politics. Written with great wit and a fierce sensitivity,
it's a stunner of a first outing, making this an event not to be missed!

Here's more on the book from its award-winning publisher, And Other Stories:

> A lyrical and visceral short story collection, *The Body of the Thing*
> unpicks the hierarchies that thrum under our relationships. Moving from
> bougie neighbourhoods in Manhattan to the sun-drenched piazzas of Italy,
> from coastal Maine to the bustle of London, these stories chase the
> fallout when women's bodies are valued for their beauty and youth,
> dismissed and discarded when ill, or made useful as parents and
> caregivers. Fluid, sensual, and fearless, *The Body of the Thing* explores
> motherhood, body dysmorphia and eating disorders, and celebrates female
> desire in all its complicated wonder.

Karishma Jobanputra is a British-Indian writer currently based in London. A
graduate of Columbia University's MFA Fiction Programme, her work has been
listed for the Brick Lane Short Story Prize and The Disquiet Literary Prize.
*The Body of the Thing* is her debut publication.

Nell Osborne is a poet and novelist. Her debut novel, *Ghost Driver* (Moist
Books, 2025), jointly won the Queen Mary Small Press Fiction Prize in 2026.

**## FIRST HALF ##Comedy Games, Improvised Live**

*(Think Whose Line Is It Anyway? meets Game Changer, with a sprinkling of Taskmaster.)*

A fast, funny first half built around short improvised games – the kind where performers get a prompt from the audience and have seconds to turn it into something brilliant. Points will be awarded. Consequences may follow.

Featuring a brand new cast for a new season! TBA

And your host, Ste Brown.

**## SECOND HALF ##BIRDWATCHERS**

Birdwatchers are a two-prov team made up of Anna Kemp (This is Your Musical) and Paige Tummons (Jazz Police). In their original “epilogue” format, Birdwatchers explore the present and past of 2 characters reminiscing together. The exploratory flashbacks combine comedic elements, heartfelt scenes, and absolutely ridiculous moments that are sure to make you laugh and think that maybe your own family isn’t that weird after all.

Birdwatchers have performed extensively in Bristol and won the Improv Cagematch in 2019.

—

Whether you’re a seasoned comedy fan or just curious about what happens when performers make it all up as they go, this is a perfect night to dive into Bristol’s thriving improv scene. Expect laughter, surprises, and something completely different — every single time.

**Up the Youth Club with Emma Warren** — Bookhaus

Wednesday 9th September, 18:00. Genres: workshops & classes, talks.
events.summary: Emma Warren on a century of British youth clubs — from Victorian boys' and girls' clubs to the rooms that produced The Specials and Stormzy — and what their disappearance costs.
events.description:
'Youth clubs have always existed. They always will, because there will
always be young people. How we care for our youth, and what we owe them, is
a question for all of us.'

In *Up the Youth Club*, Emma Warren maps the shifting story of youth clubs in
the UK and Northern Ireland, from factory workers in Victorian Boys' and
Girls' clubs to renegade self-emancipatory spaces in the 1970s and the
music-generating youth clubs of more recent decades. With a mixed lineage in
church evangelism, the patronage of the upper classes, grassroots' DIY, and
erratic state funding, the youth club has had a huge, yet almost invisible,
effect on music, sport, culture and society.

Arguing that we cannot advocate for what we do not understand, Warren
positions youth clubs as a kind of engine room — from the famous success
stories to come out of their doors, such as The Specials or Stormzy, to the
untold stories of young people finding shelter, sustenance and stimulation
for over a century — and why their dwindling numbers, largely due to
austerity and funding cuts, is of serious concern for us all.

With this impassioned history, Warren invites us to pick up the torch and
play an active part in protecting and re-igniting this vital part of UK
society.

Emma will be in conversation about this here at bookhaus. Tickets cost £7
and include a glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off the book. Presented by
bookhaus.

Entry requirements: no age restrictions.

**Everyone is welcome at our Contemporary Fiction book club, where on the first Wednesday of every month we discuss a recently-published paperback novel. In September, we'll be delving into *The Correspondent *by Virginia Evans, winner of the 2026 Women's Prize of Fiction. **

***Date:*

**Venue:**

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**

Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *The Correspondent***

***Winner of the 2026 Women's Prize of Fiction***

Every morning, Sybil Van Antwerp sits down to write letters – to her brother, to her best friend, to the president of the university who will not allow her to attend a class she desperately wants to take, to her favourite authors to tell them what she thinks of their latest books, and to one person to whom she writes often yet never sends the letter. Because at seventy-three, Sybil has used her correspondence – witty and wise – to make sense of the world.

But beyond the page, she has spent the last thirty years keeping the people who love her at arms’ length... Until letters from someone in her past force her to examine one of the most painful periods of her life. Now, Sybil must send the letter she has been writing for all these years - and find forgiveness within herself in order to move on.

Sybil Van Antwerp’s life of letters might not be an extraordinary one, but she also might be one of the most memorable characters you will ever read.

events.summary: A six-week beginners' course covering breathwork, meditation, movement and yoga philosophy, deliberately run in blocks with gaps between so the practice has time to settle.
events.description:
Get ready to build your yoga foundation in this 6-week course that
will leave you feeling centered and strong.

Yoga Foundations — 6-Week Beginners Course (formerly Yoga for
Beginners at Yogasara)

- St Anne's House, BS4
- Wednesdays, 6.00–7.00pm
- 9 September – 14 October

**What this course is about**

This 6-week course offers a gentle, supportive introduction to yoga.
We'll explore the four core elements of practice:

- Breathwork, to calm and steady the nervous system
- Meditation, simple practices for presence and perspective
- Asana (movement), building strength, steadiness and mobility
- Yoga philosophy, practical ideas you can take into everyday life

You don't need any experience, and you don't need to be flexible.
This isn't about achieving shapes, it's about learning how to work
with your body, your breath and your attention in a way that actually
supports real life.

**How the course is structured, and why**

This course runs several times a year, by design.

We learn together over six weeks, then there is space between courses
to integrate. Time to practise at home, attend regular classes with
new understanding, and notice what changes when you live with the
practices rather than rushing on to the next thing.

This is how learning really sticks.

When we repeat a practice, pause, and then return to it, the brain
lays down stronger neural pathways. Things that felt abstract start
to make sense in the body. You hear familiar instructions
differently. You move and breathe from a more informed, embodied
place.

Each time you return, you're not starting again, you're building on
lived experience.

**Saturday morning workshops, between courses**

In the spaces between the 6-week courses, I also offer Saturday
morning workshops for those who'd like to go a little deeper.

events.description:
Bristol's legendary, bold, endlessly inventive and genre-defying theatre company, Action Hero (*The Talent*, *Oh Europa*, *Watch Me Fall*) return with something brand new: Lost inside a recurring nightmare, a reluctant actor returns to the stage after 8 years to conquer his stage fright and banish his ghosts, but he's not gonna make a big song and dance about it.

Lost inside a recurring nightmare, a reluctant actor returns to the stage. In an attempt to conquer an 8-year period of intense stage fright – and inside a dream-world inhabited by the phantoms of his disapproving ancestors – he is replaying his own autobiography and starting to lose the plot. But he's not gonna make a big song and dance about it. Instead, he's determined to keep the show on the road, re-writing his anxiety dreams live on stage in the hope of banishing the ghosts of performances past.

*A Song & Dance* is an absurdist nightmare of a performance about masking, performing and 'acting the part'.
