events.description:
A special programme of walks designed to explore the Blaise Estate and celebrate 100 years
of public ownership.

Each walk focuses on an aspect of the estate’s rich wildlife, its historical connections or
its archaeological discoveries. Walk leaders will take you for a gentle stroll to different
parts of the park sharing what makes the Blaise Estate so special.

**Walk programme**

- **Hidden Blaise** — Join the estate rangers for a guided tour around the estate and visit
  areas usually closed to the public. Sunday 25 October, 11am–12:30pm.
- **Blaise Community Garden** — A guided tour around the Community Garden to learn about
  the history of the site and how its changed over the years. Saturday 19 September,
  2pm–3pm.
- **Archaeology and wildlife** — Join the team from Blaise Museum and the Bristol Regional
  Environmental Records Centre (BRERC) to find out more about Blaise’s archaeological
  discoveries and rich wildlife. Thursday 10 September, 11am–12:30pm.
- **Humphrey Repton’s landscape** — Explore the picturesque parkland created for the
  Harford Family by the famous landscape designer Humphrey Repton. Thursday 8 October,
  11am–12:30pm.
- **St Mary’s Church and churchyard** — A guided walk exploring St Mary’s church and
  churchyard, the historic memorials and its links to Bristol’s merchant history. Thursday
  22 October, 11am–12:30pm.

**Book tickets.** Free, donations welcome. Booking essential. Please select the walk or
walks you are interested in and book your place.

All walks last around 90 minutes and start from Blaise Museum unless otherwise stated.
Please arrive at least five minutes before the start of the walk. Suitable outdoor clothing
and a bottle of water are recommended. This event may have to be cancelled at short notice
due to external factors such as weather conditions. Well behaved dogs on leads are only
permitted on walks that specify this.

events.title: Crossings: A journey across water, memory and belonging
events.timesText: Exhibition Sat 12 – Wed 16 Sep, daily 11:00–18:00; Private View Fri 11 Sep 18:00–21:00

price.text: Admission is free; tickets are not required.

events.raw:
**Crossings: A journey across water, memory and belonging** — Fri, 11 Sept 2026 18:00 to Wed, 16 Sept 2026 18:00, Centrespace Gallery & Studios

Crossings: A journey across water, memory and belonging is a group exhibition by three artists who each explore how movement across water shapes memory, identity and culture.

Exhibition Dates: Saturday 12th September - Wednesday 16th September
PV: Friday 11th September, 6:00 - 9:00 pm
Opening Hours: Daily, 11:00 am - 6:00 pm
events.summary: Three artists from island histories — Iceland, the British Isles, and Tonga and Aotearoa — on how crossing water shapes memory and identity; private view tonight, then daily to Wednesday 16 September. Free.
events.description:
For thousands of years, waterways have connected people long before they divided nations. Oceans, rivers and estuaries have carried migration, trade, conflict, ceremony and stories, allowing cultures to meet, separate and evolve. This exhibition brings together three artists whose practices emerge from different island histories—Iceland, the British Isles, and the Pacific islands of Tonga and Aotearoa, New Zealand—to explore how movement across water shapes identity.

**Dates:** Friday 11th September - Wednesday 16th September
**Private View:** Friday 11th September, 6:00 - 9:00 pm
**Opening Hours:** Daily | 11:00 am - 6:00 pm

**Workshops and Events:**

**Handkerchief Embroidery Workshop with Radical Embroiderer** | Tuesday, 15th September | 2:00 - 4:00 pm

_“I will be exploring the crossings people have made across large bodies of water. My great-grandfather travelled by boat from Belfast to New Zealand with his family in 1875. The journey took two months. Boredom on long voyages was relieved by novel sights such as seeing dolphins, albatrosses and whales, playing games and writing letters. The monotony was also relieved by passing ships. People waved handkerchiefs, and letters were sometimes passed to home-bound vessels via small rowing boats, although it has to be said that in the Southern Ocean encounters with other ships were rare. What would you write? Does the way the words are embroidered affect how the words are perceived? In the workshop, we will be embroidering words onto vintage handkerchiefs reflecting experiences, real or imagined.”_

All equipment will be provided. Workshop attendees will be able to take their embroidered handkerchief home. Refreshments will be provided, including a New Zealand "Bumble Bee". Payment by Donation on the day (£15 recommended). Booking essential (booking terms TBA).

Radical Embroiderer is an award-winning embroiderer who is interested in the way embroidery can be used to highlight, question and challenge. Any profits she makes from this exhibition and workshop will be donated to the UK Greenpeace and Tongan campaigns against deep-sea mining.

**Participating Artists:** [Iris Thorsteinsdottir](https://iristhorsteinsdottir.com) | Radical Embroiderer | Sarah Cocks
**Instagram/Website:** @iris.thorsteinsdottir | @radicalembroiderer
**Entry:** Admission is free; tickets are not required.

**Accessibility:** The exhibition space is fully wheelchair accessible, with step-free entry and wide pathways throughout. An accessible toilet is available on-site. Seating is provided within the exhibition for visitors who may need to rest. We welcome assistance dogs, and staff are available to offer support if needed.

If you have specific access requirements or would like to plan your visit, please contact centrespacegallery@gmail.com — we’re happy to help.

events.title: Reds - Paul Mason on the Past, Present and Future of Communism

price.text: £30 includes a copy of the book / £6 general admission

events.raw:
**Reds - Paul Mason on the Past, Present and Future of Communism**

Friday 11th September 2026 19:00 at Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries

A major analysis as we head into a dangerous new world order where China and Russia threaten major change to the world's democracies

£30 includes a copy of the book / £6 general admission
events.summary: Journalist and former Newsnight economics editor Paul Mason on his new global history of communism, *Reds*, from ancient revolts to the totalitarian twentieth century and what it means for today's stagnant democracies. In conversation with Andrew Kelly, formerly of Bristol Ideas.
events.description:
It starts in antiquity, not in 1917. It centres not just on the obvious leaders and thinkers but asks how the idealism of millions of working-class activists could lead to their acquiescence in mass murder, repression and social atomisation. A fact whose legacy – unfortunately – is alive and kicking in both Russia and China today.

**Paul Mason**’s startling new book will argue that the desire to live without hierarchy and property is an impulse deeply rooted in our human nature. Reds traces the history of communist ideas through revolts in the ancient and medieval worlds, and chronicles the rise of 19th century anti-capitalist movements. Using first hand testimonies of both the perpetrators and the victims, Mason gives a new and terrifying account of how the 20th century experiment in communism turned into a totalitarian nightmare.

But, he argues, the story is not over. Western democracies are stagnant and lacking self-belief. Looming climate chaos demands radical economic answers. Millions of people in the global south see China’s offer of authoritarian, state-led development model as a viable alternative. And among the Western left, new forms of techno-egalitarianism vie with right-wing libertarianism in the battle over the digital future.

**Paul Mason** is a British journalist, author, broadcaster, and political commentator known for his economic and political analysis. Formerly Economics Editor at _BBC Newsnight_ and _Channel 4 News_, he has written for _The New European_, _Social Europe_, and _Frankfurter Rundschau_, authored books like _Postcapitalism_ and _How to Stop Fascism_, produced award-winning documentaries, and is active in progressive politics and defence policy.
He will be in conversation with **Andrew Kelly**, formerly director of _Bristol Ideas_.

Bordeaux to the Big Screen on Millennium Square.

Pack a picnic and be transported to the rhythms of Broadway by one of France's most
prestigious orchestras, Orchestre National Bordeaux Aquitaine.

This concert will be broadcast at venues across the Bordeaux region. We're delighted to
be able to share in celebrating music together as part of Bristol and Bordeaux's twinning
partnership.

**Programme — Leonard Bernstein.** *Fancy Free*, Three Dance Variations; *On the
Waterfront*, Suite Symphonique; *On the Town*, Three Dance Episodes; *West Side Story*,
Danses Symphoniques; *Candide*, Ouverture. Musical Director: Joseph Swensen.

Deckchair seating will be available on a first come, first served basis, so feel free to
bring your own camping chairs or beanbags too.

The Bristol Bordeaux Partnership celebrates it's 80th anniversary next year, with an
itinerary of events planned across the city to mark eight decades of friendship and
cultural exchange.

EXPLORE OVER 500 WORKS OF CONTEMPORARY ART THIS AUTUMN

We open the doors to the **173 Annual Open Exhibition** on Saturday 12th September. With over 500 artworks by 381 artists, ranging from sculpture to video, to ceramics to print - and everything in between - this is our largest event of the year.

The Annual Open is as much about enjoying art as it is about celebrating the artists, so we're bringing you exciting new opportunities to make the most of your visit to the exhibition. and established artists.

architecture, sculpture and mixed-media installation, from

events.title: An Evening of Kate Bush
events.raw:
**An Evening of Kate Bush** — Sat 12 Sep | 19:30 – 22:30.

Performed live by a full band, vocalists and string quartet in the ethereal surroundings of the UK's most stunning Cathedrals and Minsters.

**Let Me In** are _back_ with a brand new show, exploring the evocative music of Kate Bush, on a UK Cathedral tour in late 2026. After three years of sell out productions, including _An Evening of Radiohead_ and _An Evening of Pink Floyd_, Let Me In Presents are proud to announce a brand new show, featuring a 10 piece band, accompanied by the ever-present Mike Nowland String Quartet.

The show will move through **Kate Bush's** music chronologically, starting with the groundbreaking debut album – _The Kick Inside_ – and delving deep into classics such as _Hounds of Love_ and _Never For Ever_, until we reach the maternal warmth of 2005's multi-award winning comeback record – _Aerial_, touching on everything in between. Expect the classics – _Running Up That Hill_, _Cloudbusting_, _Wuthering Heights_, but also some rarities and hidden gems, including _The Ninth Wave_ suite, from _Hounds of Love_, in it's entirety.

Your band for the evening will be fronted by the sensational Lydia Gardiner, alongside Eleanor Kinsey, Amelia Harrison, Lucia Carmignani, Colleen Curran, Alfie Woods, Bruce Higgs, Daniel Anketell, Josh Semans & Musical Director – Ewan Steady.

_Please note: this event is presented by an external organiser and hosted at Bristol Cathedral. This event is organised by Let Me In Presents._ Tickets are available from the event organisers.
events.summary: Let Me In's ten-piece band and string quartet play Kate Bush's catalogue in order, from The Kick Inside to Aerial, with the whole Ninth Wave suite included. Tomorrow night, tickets from the promoter rather than the cathedral.

events.description:
## Stand Up For The Weekend with Steve Bugeja Featuring Eleanor Tiernan plus compere Meryl O’Rourke

#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly show from The Comedy Box featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: STEVE BUGEJA

Steve Bugeja is one of the circuit’s most exciting comedians. Steve hosted the BBC Radio 4 series Economics with Subtitles and has made numerous appearances on TV shows including The Russell Howard Hour (Sky One), Love Island: Aftersun (ITV2), Russell Howard’s Stand Up Central (Comedy Central) and Zoe Ball on Saturday (ITV1).

Making a name for himself internationally, Steve has twice been invited to perform at the Melbourne International Comedy Festival, appearing on Opening Night Comedy Allstars Supershow (ABC1) and on Comedy Up Late (ABC1).

A prolific writer, Steve was a key member of the writing team for The Russell Howard Hour (Sky One) and for Iain Stirling’s CelebAbility (ITV2) and has contributed material to Mock the Week (BBC2), 8 Out of 10 Cats (Channel 4) and BBC Radio 4.

Steve won the BBC New Comedy Award in 2013 and has since performed numerous Edinburgh Fringe shows and national tours.

#### “*Plentiful jokes and compelling storytelling*” — The Scotsman

#### “*Drum-tight, as if polished by a sitcom writers’ room to cram as many jokes in as humanly possible*” — Chortle

#### “*Blends the intelligence of a well-crafted hour with some touching emotional honesty*” — The Scotsman

[STEVE BUGEJA](https://www.stevebugeja.com/)

events.title: Youth Event: Evening Bat Walk in Stoke Park
events.raw:
**Youth Event: Evening Bat Walk in Stoke Park** — Saturday 12 September 2026,
6:00pm – 8:00pm, Grow Wilder, Bristol.

"Join us for an evening walk through Grow Wilder and across to Stoke Park to see
some great bats in action!"
events.summary: A dusk walk out of Grow Wilder and over into Stoke Park with detectors, listening for the bats working the hedgerows. Part of the Trust's youth programme, meeting at the growing site.
events.description:
Did you know there are 18 different species of bat in the UK? Did you know they
are the only true flying mammals in the world? Join us for an evening walk
through Grow Wilder and across to Stoke Park to see these great creatures in
action.

The event involves discussion of bat habitats, yearly cycles and conservation
needs, along with use of bat detectors to identify the species observed during
the walk. No prior expertise is required.

Participants should prepare for outdoor conditions with sturdy shoes,
appropriate clothing and a torch, as the return journey will occur in darkness
over uneven terrain.

This event is part of our Youth Programme so we ask anyone attending to be
between 14-25 years old. Anyone under 18 must have parental consent to attend.
Parents and siblings are also welcome. Meet at Grow Wilder, 181 Frenchay Park
Road, Bristol, BS16 1EL.

events.title: John Boorman and Bristol: Part II
events.ageRestriction: 16+, any under 18s accompanied by 21+ adult 1:1 ratio
events.raw:
**John Boorman and Bristol: Part II** — 12th Sep 12pm, runtime 4hrs 30mins.

Before he went on to Hollywood fame, film director John Boorman worked at BBC Bristol
where he made many films about the city. Five documentaries and one fictional film,
almost all set in Bristol and the West of England. None of these titles have been seen
for decades. With thanks to the BFI National Archive and the BBC Archive.
events.summary: Six BBC Bristol films John Boorman made before Hollywood — Concorde at Filton, art students, Citizen 63 portraits — unseen for decades, on the city's biggest screen.

Rendezblues, a soulful jazz ensemble, will be performing two sets of mesmerising vocals
and elegant jazz accompaniment on 13th of September.

from the rooftop bar and views of the Clifton Suspension Bridge.

7PM with an opportunity to purchase drinks and a second set beginning at 7:30PM.

The evening features a summertime sunset on the rooftop with unique arrangements of
jazz and blues classics.

Tickets are non-refundable.

events.title: In Conversation with Stacey Yu and Freya Bromley
events.raw:
**In Conversation with Stacey Yu and Freya Bromley**

— Bookhaus

Event Cancelled

workshops & classes / talks
events.description:
We are very pleased to be joined by two rising literary stars for a double
header, in which Freya Bromley and Stacey Yu will be in conversation.

Freya will be here to discuss *A Real Piece of Work*. What does it mean for
a stranger to think you're brave? *A Real Piece of Work* is a sparkling and
spiky story of complicated families and even more complicated sisters,
narrated with tenderness, nuance and wit.

Stacey will be discussing *Kitten*. A magnetic novel about a young woman who
falls in love with her boyfriend's cat. Delicately playful and unexpectedly
heartfelt, *Kitten* is a sensitive reckoning with the allure of helplessness
and the uncertainty of becoming yourself in a world that is as disorienting
as it is full of hope and connection.

Join Freya and Stacey as they discuss their novels here at bookhaus. Tickets
cost £7 and include a glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off each book.

events.description:
**Whodunnit? Let's find out together! Our Crime and Thriller Book Club is built for readers who love the thrill of a good chase. Whether you're a lifelong fan of golden-age whodunnits or looking to dive into the genre for the first time, our goal is to create a welcoming, lively space to share theories, analyse motives, and celebrate great storytelling. Each month, we'll gather in person to dissect everything from the atmospheric pacing of classic thrillers to the complex puzzles of modern murder mysteries. **

**In September, we will be discussing *The Big Sleep *by Raymond Chandler: a classic noir that follows a cynical private investigator, Philip Marlowe.**

**Date:**
Monday 14th of September

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**
Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *THE BIG SLEEP***

Los Angeles PI Philip Marlowe is working for the Sternwood family.

Old man Sternwood, crippled and wheelchair-bound, is being given the squeeze by a blackmailer, and he wants Marlowe to make the problem go away. But with Sternwood's two wild, devil-may-care daughters prowling LA's seedy backstreets, Marlowe's got his work cut out, and that's before he stumbles over the first corpse...

*The Big Sleep* is Raymond Chandler's first novel featuring laconic PI Philip Marlowe.

***ABOUT RAYMOND CHANDLER***

Raymond Thornton Chandler was born in Chicago in 1888, but moved to England with his family when he was twelve, where he attended Dulwich College, alma mater to some of the twentieth century's most renowned writers. Returning to America in 1912, he settled in California, worked in a number of jobs, and later married.

It was during the Depression era that he seriously turned his hand to writing, and his first published story appeared in the pulp magazine *Black Mask* in 1933, followed six years later, when he was fifty, by his first novel, *The Big Sleep.*

Chandler died in 1959, having established himself as the finest crime writer in America.

Pre-order the book at a discount with your ticket.
events.description:
_Storysmith, 236 North Street, Bristol, BS3 1JD ([click here for a map](https://maps.app.goo.gl/9N9dxXfnwxac83FY7))_

We are stoked to welcome a truly singular literary talent to Bristol in September: **Tice Cin** will be with us to discuss her second novel **Safe Spaces**!

As longtime fans of Cin’s debut novel Keeping The House, we are especially excited to be hosting – expect an enlivening and perspective-altering chat about a book which is already gathering incredible praise. Tice will be in conversation with **Ralf Webb**.

_**Pre-order your copy of Safe Spaces** (rrp £14.99)  for a special discounted price with your ticket, then collect on the night!_

**About Tice Cin**

**Tice Cin** is an interdisciplinary artist and author from North London. Her debut novel **Keeping the House** (2021) received a Somerset Maugham Award and a London Writers Award, was a Guardian Book of the Year and was shortlisted for a British Book Award and the Desmond Elliot Prize among other accolades. Its accompanying mixtape having her named as one of Notion Magazines Ones to Watch. Her BBC Radio 4 documentary How Much Can You Say? (2024) won an Audio Production Award. Her work has been published and commissioned by Granta Magazine, London Magazine, Somerset House, Montblanc, Cartier and more. She is the founder of the interdisciplinary production company Neoprene Genie. Cin’s sophomore novel **Safe Spaces** will be published by Granta in September 2026. Cin lives between North London and North Cyprus.

_Photo credit: Eric Aydin Barberini_

**About Safe Spaces**

Our unnamed narrator survives in London and Newark on a combination of Universal Credit, music production and songwriting, trying to figure out what she wants from home, and whether anyone is prepared to give it to her.

Navigating love affairs and halted by pain following the loss of her closest confidante, Safe Spaces is a portrait of the artist as a young musician. Of the DJ booths and dances that shape her, and the worlds she finds herself in: be they local raves, her Turkish-Cypriot family, the beauty parlour or the studio.

At once a songbook, a found poem of place, a therapy transcript and a community journal, Safe Spaces is a work of extraordinary lyricism and candour, confirming Tice Cin as one of the foremost stylists of her generation.

_“Being able to capture so much raw emotion through incredible writing like this is a gift. This book conveys magical and visceral energy, that everyone should have the luxury of experiencing. Powerful shit”_ – Lola Young

_“Safe Spaces makes a universe of London in all its glory, cruelty, poetry and bureaucracy. This is a book that evokes the shattering effect of trauma on prose, then painstakingly reconstructs a way to experience life, and talk about love. I saw in it a feat of outstanding energy to keep looking, keep listening and, feel everything in a time of grief, and yet somehow overstate nothing.”_ – Amber Hussain

_“At first discordant, finally symphonic, Cin captures the heavy beat of her city’s blood, its healing music, in ways that recall and update the vivid prose-poetry of Clarence Major and Elizabeth Smart. This is an honest, intimate, grief-soaked work of experiential wonder.”_ – Tom Benn, author of Oxblood

_“With arresting street smarts and vulnerability, Tice Cin reshapes London literature to ends previously unknown. We should all be grateful.”_ – Matthew Sperling

**About Ralf Webb**

Ralf Webb is the author of the poetry collections Rotten Days in Late Summer and Highway Cottage, as well as the nonfiction book Strange Relations: Masculinity, Sexuality and Art in Midcentury America, which was shortlisted for the Sunday Times Young Writer of the Year Award. His poetry, fiction, criticism and memoir has appeared widely, including in the Guardian, Granta, and Tolka. He previously taught creative writing at Goldsmiths.

Ian transcribed the vocal lines from early sacred music of the 12th and 13th centuries and then Dominic Beeton accompanied these sublime instrumental lines with harmonium, shruti box, and synthesisers. The result is a profoundly spiritual experience which is ideally suited for cathedrals, churches, abbeys and sacred spaces.

"In an era of great change and great beauty emerged the character of James McNeill Whistler. Considered by some to be one of the great innovators of 19th century art, he was a contemporary of the Impressionists, much admired by Van Gogh and Manet. Boldly experimental and famously witty, Whistler disrupted the strict conventions of Victorian society in pursuit of a new cult of beauty, creating "art for art's sake" and earning himself a place in the history of great art. [...] Tate Britain is now holding the first major retrospective of Whistler in three decades. This blockbuster exhibition promises to reawaken the world to just how important Whistler is to art history, uniting world-famous masterpieces with rarely seen works. Exhibition on Screen will bring these stunning works and the incredible story behind them to cinemas around the world while the exhibition is still running."

A friendly choir based in the heart of Bristol. We learn songs by ear, so there's no need to read music. We don't hold auditions - come along, have a go, and give it a try. Singing in a choir is one of the simplest ways to feel good.

The choir will cover a wide variety of folk songs, as well as some world and contemporary music. This choir is happy and fun-loving, our aim is to create a sense of community and a love of singing.

If you fancy giving it a go, meeting some friendly people, and having a good sing then do come along. We meet at the Bristol Folk House in the Hall. The choir is conducted by Nonny Tabbush, a folk singer and choral practitioner. Nonny is a fun and lively choir conductor who has experience working with singers of all ages. She has started and run several community choirs, singing a range of materials including folk, world, and contemporary. She also works as a vocal practitioner for Bristol Plays Music, teaching songs in primary and secondary schools and she currently runs the Glox Vox choir in Bristol too.

Nonny is also an experienced performer, she started her career in vocal harmony when she was 16 years old, as one of The Tabbush Sisters, who performed at folk festivals across the country. She is now in a ceilidh band called The Bristol Ceilidh Quartet.

Past themes have included wildlife gardening, running a community group,
guerrilla food growing and building a wildlife pond. This gathering provides

community, learn from peers, and exchange knowledge and passion.

young people interested in giving talks, running nature-based activities, or
staffing information stalls about their projects, and there is an interest form
on the event page for anyone under 30 who would like to take part.

events.title: In Conversation: Pete Wharmby & Lisa Galley
events.raw:
**In Conversation: Pete Wharmby & Lisa Galley**

Tuesday 15th September 2026 19:00 at Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries

How can we really help autistic children in education?

£6 / £5
events.summary: Neurodivergence campaigner Pete Wharmby (*Different Minds*) and autism family consultant Lisa Galley (*Parenting your Autistic Child*) on how schools and parents can better support autistic children, with questions and a signing.
events.description:
We're delighted to host **Pete Wharmby** and **Lisa Galley** for a discussion on education and care for autistic children.

In _Different Minds_, neurodivergence campaigner Pete Wharmby shines a light on what it's like to be autistic in Western school systems today, so we can understand how to support our children through the most important years of their lives.

With gentle science, practical tools and deep validation, Lisa Galley's _Parenting your Autistic Child_ explains exactly what is happening in your child's brain and body during these difficult moments – when they refuse to get dressed, experience sensory overload or meltdown at 3.30pm – offering practical strategies that work with their nervous system rather than against it.

This informative and compassionate talk will be your chance to learn more, ask questions and get copies of the books signed.

**Peter Wharmby** is a neurodivergence campaigner and former teacher who was diagnosed autistic at age 34. He is also father to an autistic child. Shocked by the statistics around depression, anxiety and life expectancy for autistic people, Pete has immersed himself in working to improve neurodiversity awareness, acceptance and making the world a more suitable place for the neurodivergent community to live in.

**Lisa Galley** is an Autism Family Consultant, and former Speech and Language Therapist. She is also a dedicated mum to grown-up autistic kids. Her mission is to empower parents of neurodivergent children to reject the unrealistic neurotypical expectations that society places on autistic children, and to embrace intuitive parenting that aligns with the unique needs of their amazing kids.

events.title: How Not to Save the World: Doing Good Without Annoying Everyone

price.text: £7 (includes a glass of wine or soft drink)

events.raw:
**How Not to Save the World: Doing Good Without Annoying Everyone**

— Bookhaus

workshops & classes / talks
events.summary: Author and campaigner Anthea Lawson (*How Not To Save the World*) in conversation with St Pauls community organiser Liam Barrington-Bush on doing good without self-righteousness — how activists stay open and humane without alienating the people they need to convince. Headfirst editor's pick with a sell-out warning; £7 includes a drink and £2 off the book.
events.description:
> "Sell out warning! Ever wondered if your noble mission to save the world has wandered into the swamp of sanctimony? Author Anthea Lawson and organiser Liam Barrington-Bush discuss how to make positive change without getting lost in self-certainty, exploring how campaigners can stay open, humane and connected in the messy work of collective change."

**Do you want to change the world but wonder if there’s any point trying?**

**Are you unsure what you can offer, or don’t feel that you fit the activist mould?**

**Do you think activists can be self-righteous, even oblivious to the very people they’re trying to help?**

‘A wise, rich and crucial book.’ **George Monbiot**

_How Not To Save the World_ is a book about doing good, for anyone who has looked at politics or public discourse and thought, ‘we need better than this.’ The fervour that drives us to change the world can create blind spots, where we don’t see our own behaviour, or disregard it because the cause is urgent.

Realistic, candid and hopeful, _How Not To Save the World_ is a sympathetic exploration of alternatives to righteousness, purity traps and other unhelpful habits. It shows that there are ways to work together for what matters, without alienating the people we need to convince.

We are delighted to welcome Andrea Lawson to bookhaus, where she will be in conversation with Liam Barrington-Bush. Come and engage in a deep conversation about activism and organising. Tickets are £7 and include a glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off the book. Presented by bookhaus.

**Anthea Lawson** (she/her) is an author and campaigner. Her books _How Not To Save The World_ and _The Entangled Activist_ help people who want to change the world think about the psychological, spiritual and philosophical foundations of what they’re doing, what’s getting in the way, and how they can be more effective. After training as a journalist at _The Times_, she worked for campaign groups including Global Witness and Amnesty International. She has fought for many issues over three decades including controls on the arms trade and an end to the financial secrecy offered by tax havens.

**Liam Barrington-Bush** (he/him) is a social movement facilitator, community organiser and occasional writer. He lives in St Pauls, Bristol and is constantly searching for ways to undermine capitalism that are possible within the confines of parenthood. He is a co-founder and co-director of RadHR, started a community organising workshop series called Embrace the Mess, and is currently co-developing a peer to peer management training for collectively-run activist and community groups. In 2013 he wrote a book called _Anarchists in the Boardroom_ and still stands behind at least half of what he said in it.

‘The stories in this book show how we can build bridges in order to work together for the world that we want.’ **Brian Eno**

‘Read it and weep, laugh, cringe… it might bring more compassion and togetherness in a broken world.’ **Dr. Gail Bradbrook, co-founder of Extinction Rebellion**

‘Anthea Lawson’s provocative book provides us with deep insights into the tactical, emotional and ethical complexities of campaigning.’ **Sir Jonathon Porritt**

events.title: The Liberties

price.text: Free and open to the public

events.raw:
**THE LIBERTIES EXHIBITION**

The Liberties, is a deeply personal reflection by artist Gearoid Simms on growing up in Dublin's historic Liberties area.

Simms possesses a unique ability to recount memories with striking clarity, and has channelled this gift into a body of work that captures both the vibrancy and the complexity of his hometown.

"The Liberties was, and still is, a great place to grow up. Its streets were full of life, both commercial and domestic. The people were talkative and witty. Yet many of its children suffered through heroin, and today the area is no longer a market and trading hub but one defined by digital and technology culture."

Simms invites the public to look deeply into these paintings and, through them, to reflect on their own past.

Free and open to the public 17th - 20th September, 12 - 6pm.

[The Island Gallery](https://us.list-manage.com/QgfUm5r2nG1?c2id=5d93719d43fa326bdad19fdd9203ff9a), Bridewell Street, Bristol. BS1 2QD
events.summary: Four days of paintings by Gearoid Simms recalling a childhood in Dublin's Liberties — its street life and wit, and the heroin years that followed — in The Island Gallery on Bridewell Street. Free, no booking.

events.raw:
When: 17 Sep – 2 Dec 2026

Official Planetarium Show from Pink Floyd, 10 tracks from The Dark Side of the Moon set
to cosmic 360° visuals.
events.summary: The authorised Dark Side of the Moon planetarium show — the album in full against 360-degree visuals, on an evening run into December.
events.description:
The Dark Side of the Moon returns to Bristol's Planetarium!

Celebrate over 50 years of Pink Floyd's legendary album The Dark Side of the Moon with a new
awe-inspiring audio-visual show.

Set to the newly remastered audio by James Guthrie and Joel Plante of das boot recording,
the sound is richer, deeper, and more powerful than ever. The breath-taking 360° visuals,
produced by the award-winning team at NSC Creative in collaboration with Pink Floyd's iconic
creative director Aubrey Powell, bring the music to life in spectacular style.

Each song has a different theme; some futuristically looking forward and some a retro
acknowledgment to Pink Floyd's visual history, all relating to a time and space experience,
embracing technology that only a Planetarium can offer.

So, join us for a truly immersive cosmic celebration of one of the greatest albums of all
time, now showing at the Planetarium.

**Autumn shows now available to book:** Thursday 17th Sept 6pm, 7:15pm, 8:30pm; Friday 2nd
Oct 6pm, 7:15pm, 8:30pm; Friday 6th Nov 6pm, 7:15pm, 8:30pm; Thursday 26th Nov 6pm, 7:15pm,
8:30pm; Wednesday 2nd Dec 6pm, 7:15pm, 8:30pm.

**Access considerations** — A hearing loop is available. Limited wheelchair spaces are
available, please book ahead. The Planetarium is a dark environment with a stepped walkway to
access seats. Planetarium shows can feature loud noises and flashing lights; visitors with
epilepsy and photosensitivity may suffer a seizure if exposed to flashing or strobe lighting.

**Planning your visit** — Doors open 20 minutes before start time. There will be a bar.
Tickets are checked at the entrance on Millennium Square next to the Planetarium. You can
explore the Space Gallery before being invited to enter the Planetarium. Please aim to arrive
at least 10 mins before your show; late entry will not be permitted.

events.summary: Furniture, tableware and sculpture in locally sourced timber from eleven makers, from award-winning young designers to green woodworkers who have taught in Bristol for decades; private view Friday 18 September, then daily to 30 September. Free.
events.description:
Showing what’s possible when an artistic eye meets traditional skill, **_Connections Through Wood_** brings together a wide range of talents united by their appreciation of the wooden object.

Using locally sourced timbers to create furniture, tableware and sculptures, the artists explore the boundaries between woodworking and sculpture.

Artists range from award-winning young designers and green woodworkers to makers who have been working and teaching in Bristol for decades.

Including: Geoff Hannis (QEST Emerging Maker 2024), Flo Hamer (winner of the Worshipful Company of Basketmakers’ 2023 Contemporary Basketry award), Alistair Park, Adam Morgan, Johannes Roux, Alex Skawinski, Oliver Dorman, Rae Woods, Louis Johnston and Harry Morris (winner of the Heritage Crafts Association’s ‘Young Woodworker of the Year’ award 2023).

**Dates:** Saturday 19th September - Wednesday 30th September
**Private View:** Friday 18th September, 6:00 - 9:00 pm
**Opening Hours:** Daily | 10:00 am - 6:00 pm

**Workshops/Additional Events:**

**BRUSH MAKING WORKSHOP WITH RAE WOODS** | Monday, 28th September, 6 pm - 8 pm.
_Learn the basics of traditional brush making with Rae in the Centrespace Gallery as part of the Connections Through Wood Exhibition. Together, we will go through different varieties of UK timber, shaping your brush handle and fitting the bristles, leaving you with a finished household brush. No two brushes will be the same!_
_The event is held at the Centrespace Gallery in Bristol on Leonard's Lane. Turn up from 5.30pm for a 6pm start. The event should finish around 8pm._

Additional Workshops **TBA**. For more information, go to [https://treetotreen.com/ctw2026/](https://treetotreen.com/ctw2026/) or head over to our Instagram page.

**Participating Artists:** Adam Morgan | Alistair Park | Alex Skawinski | Flo Hamer | Geoff Hannis | Harry Morris | Johannes Roux | Louis Johnston | Oliver Dorman | Pheobe Goldman | Rae Woods
**Instagram/Website:** @connectionsthroughwood | [https://treetotreen.com/ctw2026](https://treetotreen.com/ctw2026)
**Entry:** Admission is free; tickets are not required.

**Accessibility:** The exhibition space is fully wheelchair accessible, with step-free entry and wide pathways throughout. An accessible toilet is available on-site. Seating is provided within the exhibition for visitors who may need to rest. We welcome assistance dogs, and staff are available to offer support if needed.

If you have specific access requirements or would like to plan your visit, please contact centrespacegallery@gmail.com — we’re happy to help.

events.summary: A three-hour introduction to kintsugi, the Japanese art of repairing broken ceramics — epoxy, natural urushi lacquer and a brass-powder gold finish. Suitable for complete beginners; morning and afternoon sittings.
events.description:
Learn the Japanese art of kintsugi repair for broken ceramics.

Spend the session immersed in the processes, tools and materials of
kintsugi and complete a repair using epoxy, coated with traditional
natural Japanese Urushi (tree sap) lacquer and finished to a stunning
gold-hued shine with fine brass powder.

Suitable for complete beginners. Materials and hot drinks are included.
Bring your own piece — small, under 20cm diameter, with simple breaks
into 2-3 pieces, open shapes like plates or dishes preferred — or
choose from pieces available on the day. The session covers epoxy,
epoxy putty, urushi and brass powder finishes.

£30 – £70, concessions available; your booking is secured with a £20
deposit. Two sittings on the day: 10:30–13:30 and 14:30–17:30.

workshops & classes / talks / exhibition
events.summary: Launch of Bookhaus's new artist-in-residence programme with CJ Reay of Black Lodge Press, the Cumberland printmaker behind fifteen years of agitational zines, prints and fabric work and one of The Underground's Anarchist Gardeners Club. A conversation on his practice; £7 with a drink.
events.description:
Since taking over the bookshop a year ago we have been keen to begin expanding our artistic and cultural offering further. Phil, our new Co-Owner, is an Illustrator with strong links to artists and illustrators around the country. The shop has great big window displays that have the potential for displaying more visual art in all kinds of formats. We are delighted to finally be launching this new program by welcoming Black Lodge to bookhaus as our first artist in residence. We will be welcoming CJ Reay, the person behind Black Lodge to bookhaus for a conversation on his artistic practices. Tickets cost £7 and include a glass of wine or a soft drink. Presented by bookhaus.

_Cj Reay is an artist from Cumberland in the North West of England. Inspired by autonomous movements, radical history and DIY culture he creates agitational art in print and fabric. He’s also one of [the underground](https://www.headfirstbristol.co.uk/whats-on/the-underground) horticulturists responsible for the Anarchist Gardeners Club. For the last 15 years he has operated Black Lodge Press; a publishing project putting out zines, prints and other radical ephemera._

events.description:
## Stand Up For The Weekend with Andrew Maxwell Featuring Burt Williamson plus compere Jack Campbell

#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our weekly flagship comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: ANDREW MAXWELL

The stupendous Andrew Maxwell headlines for The Comedy Box for the first time in decades. We first booked Andrew back in the 90s, then he grew a little too big for us. Now he’s back and we are proud to offer to you one of the best stand ups in the British Isles.

Throughout his long career, Andrew Maxwell has enjoyed many sell-out seasons at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe; he has also performed at The Amnesty / Channel Four’s Secret Policeman’s Ball (alongside Eddie Izzard, Chevy Chase and Dylan Moran), Glastonbury, The HBO US Comedy & Arts Festival in Las Vegas (alongside Jerry Seinfeld and Chris Rock), and made several appearances at the Montreal Just for Laughs Festival.

He was the special guest of friend Jim Jefferies for his Hammersmith Apollo dates in London. He is also a founder member of Altitude Comedy Festival, staged in the Alps. Andrew has recorded three Live DVDs with 2Entertain (Conflict Revolution, Andrew Maxwell: Live In Dublin & Andrew Maxwell: One Inch Punch).

**AS SEEN ON:**

Live At The Apollo (BBC One), Have I Got News For You (BBC One), Comedy Game Night, Never Mind the Buzzcocks, QI, The Secret Policeman’s Ball, I’m A Celebrity Get Me Out Of Here! (ITV) Celebrity Juice (ITV2) and Mock The Week (BBC Two). He is also the voice of Get Your Tats Out: Kavos Inc (Channel 5). Winner of King of Comedy.​

[Andrew Maxwell On Tour – Official Website](https://www.andrewmaxwellontour.com/)

#### “*One of the funniest men in Britain*” THE TELEGRAPH

#### “*Infuriatingly excellent*” THE SUNDAY TIMES

#### “*If you can only see one stand-up act, see Maxwell*” THE MIRROR

events.title: Intelligence Squared: Anthony Scaramucci - The All The Wrong Moves Tour
events.raw:
**Intelligence Squared: Anthony Scaramucci - The All The Wrong Moves Tour**

Saturday 19th September 2026 19:00 at St George's Bristol, Great George Street, Bristol, BS1 5RR

This event is hosted by our partners at Intelligence Squared.

Tickets available through Intelligence Squared
events.summary: Former White House communications director turned Trump critic Anthony Scaramucci, co-host of The Rest is Politics: US, on how America reached its current moment and how it might find a way back, ahead of the midterms — with an audience Q&A. An Intelligence Squared event at St George's.
events.description:
This event is hosted by our partners at Intelligence Squared.

American democracy is on the brink. Masked agents menace the streets of Minneapolis. Donald Trump jokes about cancelling elections. And traditional allies like Canada and the UK are beginning to look for alliances that could replace their pivotal relationships with the US.

According to Anthony Scaramucci, former White House Communications Director turned outspoken Trump critic and host of the Rest is Politics: U.S., President Trump represents one of the most serious challenges the country has faced.

This autumn, on the eve of the pivotal US midterm elections, Scaramucci comes to live audiences across the UK to offer an insider’s account of how America reached this moment and to offer a hopeful message for how it might find a way back. Drawing on his forthcoming book All The Wrong Moves, he will trace a series of catastrophic decisions made by both Democrats and Republicans that in Scaramucci’s view dismantled decades of postwar stability and prosperity. And he will describe how undoing these mistakes can unlock a new era of success for America and the world.

Don’t miss this opportunity to see Anthony Scaramucci – hilarious, irreverent, insightful and deeply sourced within both the Republican and Democratic parties – live in-person and ask your own questions in the audience Q&A.

events.raw:
**Littleton Warth** — 20.09.2026, 2:30 pm. Leader: David Hawkins. Category: Botany.

"Littleton Warth offers a wide expanse of grazed saltmarsh, with fine views across
to the Forest of Dean and down to the Severn Bridge, and a remote, untamed
atmosphere. A good array of common saltmarsh plants should be visible in September
and the Warth supports a particularly large population of Slender Hare's-ear
*Bupleurum tenuissimum*, an anomalous and nationally scarce member of the carrot
family."

"Meet at car park at end of Whale Wharf Lane, ST588910 ///clincher.alive.begun,
nearest postcode BS35 1NP."
events.summary: Saltmarsh botany on the Severn with David Hawkins, hunting the nationally scarce Slender Hare's-ear that grows here in unusual quantity, plus sea clover and bulbous foxtail if the group is lucky. Big views to the Forest of Dean and a genuinely remote feel twenty minutes from Bristol.
events.description:
Leader: David Hawkins. Category: Botany. Date: 20th September 2026, 2:30 pm.

Littleton Warth offers a wide expanse of grazed saltmarsh, with fine views across
to the Forest of Dean and down to the Severn Bridge, and a remote, untamed
atmosphere. A good array of common saltmarsh plants should be visible in September
and the Warth supports a particularly large population of Slender Hare's-ear
*Bupleurum tenuissimum*, an anomalous and nationally scarce member of the carrot
family. Sea Clover *Trifolium squamosum* may prove harder to find amongst the
swathes of Strawberry Clover *Trifolium fragiferum*, and we may also be fortunate
enough to encounter a third nationally scarce species, the grass Bulbous Foxtail
*Alopecurus bulbosus*. With the seawall supporting a few common grassland plants
as well, there should be much to see.

Meet at car park at end of Whale Wharf Lane, ST588910 ///clincher.alive.begun,
nearest postcode BS35 1NP.

events.title: The Mulai: Munir Hachemi
events.raw:
**_The Mulai_: Munir Hachemi**

Monday 21st September, Gloucester Road Books at 7.00 pm

The great Spanish author will be in conversation with author and academic, Constantine Blintzios

[Book tickets](https://hdfst.uk/e160391) (this link will take you to external site HeadFirst Bristol)
events.summary: Spanish novelist and translator Munir Hachemi — a Granta Best of Young Spanish-Language Novelist — on *The Mulai*, his Borges-and-Le Guin-inflected metafiction about an archaeologist among a lost space colony whose language and customs have drifted beyond recognition, newly translated by Julia Sanches. In conversation with Constantine Blintzios; ticketed through Headfirst.
events.description:
We're honoured to be hosting the great Spanish author and translator, Munir Hachemi, who will be discussing his wonderful novel, _The Mulai_, in conversation with the author, poet and creative writing teacher, Constantine Blintzios.

_The Mulai_, newly translated from Spanish by Julia Sanches, is a wholly original examination of lanaguage, identity and the fragile nature of civilisations. Here's more from the novel's publisher, Fitzcarraldo Editions:

An archaeologist travels to a distant planet to spend time among a mysterious community, a people who live in temperature-controlled domes, worship a deity called Dog, and repeat an elliptical phrase from which they draw their name: mulai, the tree comes. The descendants of a long-forgotten space mission, the Mulai have abandoned the social norms that once bound them to Earth. Over centuries of isolation, their language has become more about change than stability, and the ways they eat, write, reproduce, bury their dead and understand gender have all transformed into something almost unrecognizable.

Drawing on Borges, Le Guin and Calvino, _The Mulai_ is a mind-bending work of metafiction whose interlocking puzzles resound with Munir Hachemi's singularly playful and eclectic style.

---

Munir Hachemi's career as a writer began with them selling their stories in the form of fanzines in the bars of the Lavapies neighbourhood of Madrid. They are the author of _Living Things_ and _The Mulai_, and are also a translator from Chinese and English. In 2021, they appeared on Granta's Best of Young Spanish-Language Novelists list.

Constantine Blintzios is a writer, translator and academic whose debut novel, _The Smoke is Me, Burning_ was published in 2022. He has had poetry, short stories and reviews published in journals such as _Visual Verse_, _Ash_ magazine, _Paris Lit-Up_, the _Oxonian Review_ and the _Literary Review_.

Munir Hachemi photo credit: Carlos Gil

'Wild, insightful and impressive.'
— Publishers Weekly

'A beguiling tale of Otherness that is not only a translation from another language but another planet, a story told so well that every familiar word feels as new as an alien horizon.'
— Anton Hur, author of _Toward Eternity_

'If Borges wrote hard science fiction, it might well look like this... You can almost feel the author grinning at you as you read, and I daresay you'll end up grinning back by the end.'
— Drew Broussard, LitHub

events.title: Home Education Day

address.street: Great Western Dockyard, Gas Ferry Road

events.raw:
21 September 2026

Meet real-life engineers, enjoy hands-on STEM activities, and discover Brunel's legacy at
our special Home Education Day.
events.summary: A day built for home-educating families — working engineers on site and hands-on STEM around Brunel's ship.
events.description:
Bristol Dockyards is home to the remarkable legacy of Victorian engineer Isambard Kingdom
Brunel, but engineering is far from history. Join us this autumn for a special Home
Education Day where you can meet real-life engineers from Babcock and Bristol Dockyards,
discover what they do, and take part in hands-on STEM activities. You'll also have the
chance to learn more about Brunel and explore our newly opened museum dedicated to his
most famous ship, the SS Great Britain.

**What's included:** whole site access including the Brunel Institute, Being Brunel
Museum, SS Great Britain & NEW museum and Historic Dockyards.

**Key info** — Price: £9.00 pp; free for children 3 and under and carers accompanying a
paying disabled person. Date & time: Monday 21st September 2026, 10am-3pm.

**Additional bookable activities:**

- **Guided Tour of SS Great Britain** — Find out about the SS Great Britain's long and
  adventurous life, discover passengers and crew stories as you explore the ship with our
  knowledgeable volunteer tour guides. 10:30-11:30, 60 mins, on board the ship, meeting at
  the stern. £2 per child, adults free but must be booked in.
- **Brunel's Big Ideas** (education workshop) — Take a closer look at some of Brunel's
  sketches, discover how the SS Great Britain was built then hunt for some of Brunel's
  engineering tools in one of our museums. 10:30-11:30, 60 mins, Medlock classroom, Dry
  Dock and Being Brunel Museum. For children working at Key Stage 1 or 2. £3 per
  participating child, £1 per non-participating child, adults free.
- **Mission: Save the Ship** (education workshop) — Investigate the dehumidification system
  that protects the SS Great Britain and discover the science and engineering behind it
  with hands-on experiments led by the Ship's Conservation Engineer. 13:00-14:00, 60 mins,
  Medlock classroom and Dry Dock. For children aged 12+. £3 per participating child, £1 per
  non-participating child, adults free.

As the site is only open for home educating families it is likely to be quieter than it
would normally be at weekends or during school holidays. A covered picnic area with patio
heaters is available, and The Board Walk kiosk is open 8:30am-4:00pm.

events.title: A Way of Love launch with Peter Parker and Lurid Editions

price.text: £7 (includes a glass of wine or soft drink)

events.raw:
**A Way of Love launch with Peter Parker and Lurid Editions**

— Bookhaus

workshops & classes / talks / lgbtq+
events.summary: Biographer Peter Parker (*Some Men in London: Queer Life 1945-67*, now in Penguin Modern Classics) and Lurid Editions' D-M Withers celebrate the first new edition of James Courage's 1959 gay novel *A Way of Love*, and talk about queer life in pre-Stonewall London. £7 with a drink and £2 off the books.
events.description:
Peter Parker and D-M Withers will be in conversation at bookhaus to celebrate the publication of three books which provide insight into the experiences and lives of gay men in the post-war, pre-Stonewall era.

Parker’s critically acclaimed two volumes _Some Men in London: Queer Life 1945-59_ and _1960-67_ have just been published in paperback in the Penguin Modern Classics series. _Some Men in London_ features letters, diaries, psychological textbooks, novels, films, plays and police records, covering a wide range of viewpoints, from those who deplored homosexuality to those who campaigned for its decriminalisation.

Parker’s collections are the perfect companion piece to the latest reissue from Bristol based indie Lurid Editions, A Way of Love by James Courage (1903-1963). Originally published in 1959, Lurid’s publication is the first ever new edition of this important queer novel, written by a seriously underappreciated author.

_A Way of Love_ tells the story of the worldly architect Bruce Quantock and his younger, inexperienced lover, Philip Dill. It is a beautifully written novel set in the late ’50s when queer communities were forced to live at constant risk of blackmail or prison. Yet it also shows a thriving and joyous subculture, and the defiant struggle gay men faced to live ordinary lives, on their own terms.

Parker and Withers will discuss the life and times of James Courage, and celebrate the career of this underappreciated mid-century author. Tickets cost £7 and include a glass of wine or a soft drink and £2 off the books. Presented by bookhaus.

**Peter Parker** is the author of biographies of J. R. Ackerley and Christopher Isherwood, _The Old Lie_, _The Last Veteran_, _Housman Country_ and _A Little Book of Latin for Gardeners_. He edited _A Reader's Guide to the Twentieth-Century Novel_ and _Twentieth-Century Writers_, is an advisory editor of the _Oxford Dictionary of National Biography_, and contributed essays to _Britten's Century_ and _Fifty Gay and Lesbian Books Everybody Must Read_. He has written about people, books, art, architecture and gardening for a wide variety of newspapers and magazines, and lives in London's East End.

D-M Withers is Director of Lurid Editions, a publisher of rediscovered queer literature.

events.title: The Disappearers: Marlon James
events.raw:
**_The Disappearers_: Marlon James**

Wednesday 23rd September, Lantern Hall, Bristol Beacon at 7.00 pm

One of the 21st century's most significant writers in conversation with Vanessa Kisuule

[Book tickets](https://bristolbeacon.org/whats-on/marlon-james-priority/) (this link will take you to external site HeadFirst Bristol)
events.summary: Booker winner Marlon James introduces, reads from and discusses *The Disappearers* — a return to 1980s Kingston, following seven gay actors after a deadly attack on a rehearsal — in one of only four UK events for the book. In conversation with Vanessa Kisuule, in the Lantern Hall at Bristol Beacon; tickets through the Beacon.
events.description:
We are delighted to announce that we will be hosting Booker Prize winner and one of the 21st century's most acclaimed novelists, Marlon James, in September.

Marlon is coming to Bristol to introduce, discuss and read from his hugely-anticipated new novel, _The Disappearers_, in what is one of only four UK events the US-based author is undertaking for the book. He will be in conversation with the celebrated author, poet and performer, Vanessa Kisuule.

The novel marks a return to the territory of Marlon's brilliant Booker winning, _A Brief History of Seven Killings_; the publication that fully established him as an international literary star.

Set in late 1980s Kingston Jamaica, _The Disappearers_ is an uncompromising, acutely thought-provoking portrait of queer life in an often brutally unaccepting society. Seven gay actors confront bigotry and hate following a deadly attack at a rehearsal. Epic in its scale and awash with an unbreakable humanity, the novel confirms Marlon James' place at the forefront of modern fiction.

This is an unmissable opportunity to hear from one of the great writers of our time.

'Epic in every sense of that word'
— _New York Times_ on _A Brief History of Seven Killings_, selected in NYT's 100 Best Books of the 21st Century

'The way James uses language is amazing . . . Vigorous, intricate and captivating, [it] is hard to put down'
— _Ebony_ on _A Brief History of Seven Killings_

'Showcases the extraordinary capabilities of a writer whose importance can scarcely be questioned'
— _Independent_

price.text: £8.00 – £19.00 (ticket only £8; ticket + copy of Agate Head / Stone Soup £19)

**Patricia Lockwood: Agate Head / Stone Soup**

Wednesday 23rd September 2026, 6:30 pm

£8.00 – £19.00
events.summary: Patricia Lockwood — *Priestdaddy*, the Booker-shortlisted *No One Is Talking About This* — in the shop for the first time, marking her new poetry collection *Agate Head / Stone Soup*, in which she turns metalsmith and blends meme-speak with geological time.
events.description:
_Storysmith, 236 North Street, Bristol, BS3 1JD ([click here for a map](https://maps.app.goo.gl/9N9dxXfnwxac83FY7))_

Join us as we welcome a Storysmith all-time favourite, live in the shop for the very first time! The one and only **Patricia Lockwood**, the original Priestdaughter, will be in Bristol to mark the release of her new poetry collection, **Agate Head / Stone Soup**, and in conversation about this alongside other matters.

You may know Patricia from her life-defining memoir Priestdaddy, her devastating yet delirious novels No One Is Talking About This ([Storysmith Book of the Year 2021](https://storysmithbooks.com/list/storysmith-books-of-the-year-2021/)) and Will There Ever Be Another You, her poetry collection Motherland Fatherland Homelandsexuals, or [that video where she slowly extrudes a crystal egg from her mouth](https://x.com/TheBookerPrizes/status/1455100456699670534). We’re very excited.

_**Pre-order your copy of Agate Head / Stone Soup** (rrp £18.99)  for a special discounted price with your ticket, then collect on the night!_

**About Patricia Lockwood**

Patricia Lockwood is the author of six books, including the 2021 novel No One Is Talking About This, an international bestseller which was shortlisted for the Booker Prize and the Women’s Prize for Fiction, and translated into 20 languages. Her 2017 memoir Priestdaddy won the Thurber Prize for American Humor and was named one of the Guardian’s 100 best books of the 21st century. Her other books include the novel Will There Ever Be Another You and two poetry collections, Motherland Fatherland Homelandsexuals (2014) and Balloon Pop Outlaw Black (2012). Lockwood’s work has appeared in the New York Times, the New Yorker, and the London Review of Books, where she is a contributing editor. She lives in Savannah, Georgia.

_Photo credit: Grep Hoax_

**About Agate Head / Stone Soup**

Many have called Patricia Lockwood a wordsmith, but in the latest iteration of her life, she has become, quite literally, a metalsmith too. Stones, gems, metals, fossils – she forges them into bodies, faces and, with her typical irreverence, vaginas.

In these poems, a robot dog discovers the Lascaux caves in France. Jane Austen shoots a perfect 147. A rock gets a girlfriend. The Pope blesses McLovin (kind of).

Lockwood’s most successful work of metal- and wordsmithing yet is her blend of the Internet world with the natural one, as she slips meme references and algospeak into evocations of geological time, explorations of organic bodies, and observations of youth. Her most personal collection of poetry yet, you may find you understand yourself – and Patricia – more than you’d like to by the end.

events.timesText: Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.
events.raw: **Translated Fiction Book Club: 24/09 TWO YEAR BOOK CLUB ANNIVERSARY!** — £0.00.
events.summary: The translated fiction club turns two: a mini party and a discussion that revisits two years of reading.
events.description:
**Join us for an exciting evening to discuss translated literature. Whether you're a fan of literary fiction or just looking to try something new, this book club hopes to achieve just that. **

**In September, we'll be celebrating our book club's two year anniversary! Come along for a mini party and book club discussion that takes a trip down memory lane...**

***Date:***

Thursday 24th of September

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**
Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us via info@maxminervas.co.uk.

All you have to do is read the book and show up on the night.

**THE TWO YEAR BOOK CLUB SPECIAL:**

To celebrate the book club's two year anniversary, we're going to take a trip down memory lane and revisit the books we've explored together in our book club.

The goal is simple: pick your favourite book club title and bring it on the night so we can discuss what we all liked, didn't like, and see what titles we're all fond of.

*Eligible books:*

- ***Brandy Sour*** by Constantia Soteriou, translated from Greek by Lina Protopapa (Cyprus)

- ***Elevator in **Sài Gòn*** by Thuận, translated from Vietnamese by Nguyễn An Lý (Vietnam)

- ***Down the Rabbit Hole*** by Juan Pablo Villalobos, translated from Spanish by Rosalind Harvey (Mexico)

- ***The Vegetarian*** by Han Kang, translated from Korean by Deborah Smith (South Korea)

- ***Ceasaria*** by Hanna Nordenhök, translated from Swedish by Saskia Vogel (Sweden)

- ***Spanish Beauty*** by Esther García Llovet, translated from Spanish by Richard Village (Spain)

- ***Drive Your Plow Over the Bones of the Dead*** by Olga Tokarzcuk, translated from Polish by Antonia Lloyd-Jones (Poland)

- ***The National Telepathy*** by Roque Larraquy, translated from Spanish by Frank Wynne (Argentina)

- ***On the Calculation of Volume I ***by Solvej Balle, translated from Danish by Barbara J Haveland (Denmark)

- ***From Savagery ***by Alejandra Banca, translated from Spanish by Katie Brown (Venezuela)

- ***The Little I Knew ***by Chiara Valerio, translated from Italian by Ailsa Wood (Italy)

- ***Just A Little Dinner*** by Cécile Tili, translated from French by Katherine Gregor (France)

- ***The Memory Police*** by Yoko Ogawa, translated from Japanese by Stephen Snyder (Japan)

- ***Heart Lamp ***by Banu Mushtaq, translated from Kannada by Deepa Bhasti (India)

- ***On the Calculation of Volume II ***by Solvej Balle, translated from Danish by Barbara J Haveland (Denmark)

- ***Chess*** by Stefan Zweig, translated from German by Anthea Bell (Austria)

- ***The Palace on the Higher Hill*** by Karim Kattan, translated from French by Jeffrey Zuckerman (Palestine)

- ***Sánchez ***by Esther García Llovet, translated from Spanish by Richard Village (Spain)

- ***The Rarest Fruit*** by Gaëlle Bélem, translated from French by Karen Fleetwood and Laëtitia Saint-Loubert (Réunion)

- ***The Love of Singular Men*** by Victor Heringer, translated from Portuguese by James Young (Brazil)

- ***Before The Rocket ***by Loranne Vella, translated from Maltese by Kat Storace (Malta)

- ***Cathedrals*** by Claudia Piñeiro, translated from Spanish by Frances Riddle (Argentina)

- ***Taiwan Travelogue ***by Yáng Shuāng-zǐ, translated from Mandarin by Lin King (Taiwan)

- ***She Who Remains ***by Rene Karabash, translated from Bulgarian by Izidora Angel (Bulgaria)

"The book club was born out of a love for translated literature and a desire to find a community. When I started the book club two years ago, I had no idea that it would have become so integral to my routine. We've had the pleasure of welcoming translators, new faces, and discussing books from 22 different countries together. I hope to keep reading around the world with you all for many more years! Thank you for everything." - Ev

events.title: An Evening with Jonn Elledge

price.text: £29 includes a copy of the book / £5 admission only

events.raw:
**An Evening with Jonn Elledge**

Thursday 24th September 2026 19:00 at Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries

From electric lighting to pedestrian crossings

£29 includes a copy of the book / £5 admission only
events.summary: Jonn Elledge, author of *A History of the World in 47 Borders*, on the ideas and inventions — elevators, electric light, parks, pedestrian crossings — that made modern urban life possible. Talk, audience Q&A and signing.
events.description:
For over 10,000 years, we humans have been busy altering our environment and embracing 'progress', evolving seamlessly from hunter gatherers to the modern urban sophisticates we see ourselves as today.

But what are the ideas and inventions that enabled humanity to become, by the early 21st century, a majority urban species for the first time? How did the essential infrastructure of modern life - the innovations that we barely even notice, but without which our world would fall apart - actually come to be?

With his characteristic wit and boundless curiosity, Jonn Elledge invites us to join him on a fascinating and often surprising tour of the ideas and technologies that made modernity possible. From elevators to electric lighting, parks to pedestrian crossings, he guides us through the history of civilisation itself.

Jonn will talk about his new book before an audience Q&A and book signing.

Jonn Elledge is the author of the number-one bestseller, A History of the World in 47 Borders. A New Statesman andNewWorld columnist, he is a regular on the podcasts Oh God, What Now? and the late, lamented Paper Cuts, and a frequent contributor to The i Paper, the Guardian and assorted other publications. He was previously an assistant editor at the New Statesman, where he created and ran its urbanism-focused City Metric site, spending six happy years writing about cities, maps and borders and hosting the Skylines podcast. He has written three books, as well as over 200 editions of the Newsletter of (Not Quite) Everything. He lives in London, with the best dog in the world.

**Join us for a fantastic lunchtime discussion packed with gripping secrets, sharp wit, and psychological suspense! We are thrilled to host an exclusive conversation between global phenomenon **Liane Moriarty** and highly acclaimed **Charlotte Philby. **Come along for a riveting discussion!**

**Date:**
Friday 25th of September

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 12:30 pm. Discussion at 1:00 pm. The event should finish at around 2:00 pm, and books will be signed.

**Tickets:**
£5 ticket only
£22 ticket with *Big Little Truths* (hardback)
£30 ticket with *Big Little Lies* (paperback) and *Big Little Truths *(hardback)

You don't need to bring your ticket with you, we will have a list of names on the door. Books will be available to buy on the night.

**ABOUT THE BOOK**

***BIG LITTLE TRUTHS***

After the lies, come the truths . . .

Ten years ago, at the Pirriwee High School gates, the friendships of Celeste, Jane and Madeline were forged in the fires of young motherhood, the big little lies we all tell to hide our deepest fears and secrets – and the event that changed everything.

Now mothers to hormonal teens, these frazzled friends are starting to worry about the strangers newly occupying their kids’ bedrooms. Or they would, if they weren’t so distracted by their own problems. Because Madeline’s landmark birthday is about to land a bombshell. Jane’s rock-solid marriage is suddenly crumbling. And Celeste’s mother-in-law is asking awkward questions about the past. Not to mention the mystery of who sent the school receptionist a freshly severed finger. So many difficult little truths that each is facing.

Such a pity then that not a one of them can see the biggest ugliest truth hiding in their midst . . .

***Big Little Truths is the sequel to Big Little Lies, the breakout worldwide phenomenon that has sold over 6 million copies and is an Emmy- and Golden Globe-winning HBO sensation, produced by and starring Reese Witherspoon and Nicole Kidman. This novel follows Madeline, Celeste and Jane and their teenage kids years later, and will inspire the upcoming TV series.***

**ABOUT THE AUTHORS**

**Liane Moriarty** is the bestselling author of ten novels, including *Here One Moment*, *Apples Never Fall, The Husband's Secret, Big Little Lies* and *Nine Perfect Strangers*. Her novels have sold more than 25 million copies worldwide and have been translated into over 40 languages. *Big Little Lies* is now an Emmy and Golden Globe-winning HBO series, produced by and starring Nicole Kidman and Reese Witherspoon. *Nine Perfect Strangers* and *Apples Never Fall* have both been adapted for TV. *Here One Moment* is being adapted for TV by Nicole Kidman and Bruna Papandrea. Liane lives in Sydney with her husband, son and daughter.

**Charlotte Philby** is a critically acclaimed author of six novels. As a journalist, she worked for eight years as a newspaper reporter, editor and columnist at the *Independent*, where she was shortlisted for the Cudlipp Prize for investigative reporting. She is a former contributing editor and features writer at *Marie Claire*, and has written for publications including the *Sunday Times, New Statesman* and *Financial Times*. With the support of the BFI, she is currently adapting for film her novel *Edith and Kim*, which reimagines the lives of her grandfather, the double-agent Kim Philby, and Edith Tudor-Hart, who recruited him to the Soviet cause. Charlotte has three children and lives in Bristol.

events.title: Play Fridays
events.raw:
When: 25 Sep 2026, 10am - 12pm
Best for ages: 0-5

For families with children under 5, these special sessions once a month are all about
sensory play, having fun and exploratory learning.
events.summary: The monthly under-fives sensory play morning. Only the September date is currently listed.
events.description:
Relax, play and have fun together in our Play Friday sessions for under 5s and their
grown-ups.

Each month, our Theatre of Curiosity space comes alive with a different mini-adventure
developed specially for our youngest visitors.

Our Play Friday sessions are developed using the theory of schematic play to encourage
open-ended exploration and help children learn about the world through play.

**Upcoming events:** 25 Sept, 6 Nov, 4 Dec.

September's theme is 'On A Roll'. It's time to twist, turn, spin and roll. Experiment with
spinning tops and rolling toys or turn yourself around. This session is based on the Rotation
Schema: where a child is fascinated by objects or their own body spinning, twisting, rolling,
or moving in circles. It helps toddlers and young children develop balance, coordination,
spatial awareness, and an understanding of cause and effect.

**Access considerations** — Play Friday takes place in a large open space in the centre of
the ground floor. On busy days, the space can be noisy. Most activities will be at floor
height and the space can get a bit messy. You can come and go as you please between Play
Friday and the rest of the exhibition.

**BEVERLY BUCHANAN — WEATHERING**
Saturday 26 September to Sunday 31 January 2026

Spike Island presents the first European survey exhibition of the work of Beverly Buchanan (b.1940; d.2015), bringing together five decades of sculpture, painting, drawing, earthworks, artists’ books and rarely-seen archival material. Rooted in the landscapes and histories of the American Southeast, Buchanan developed a singular practice shaped by memory, materiality and place, exploring the enduring legacies of slavery through the histories embedded in architecture, landscape and everyday materials.

events.description:
### Stand Up For The Weekend with Mike Gunn Featuring Michelle Shaughnessy plus compere Jeremy Flynn

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: MIKE GUNN

Widely regarded as one of the UK’s finest circuit comedians, Mike Gunn blends darkly intelligent observations with a brilliantly understated delivery, finding humour in family life, middle age and the everyday frustrations we can all relate to. A misspent youth and a series of grim jobs cultivated his cynical outlook on life and a perverse desire led him to the world of stand-up. A self-confessed pessimist, he describes himself as “not a natural choice for a career in laughter”. He has a rare ability to walk close to the line of what audiences find acceptable and yet still remain likable and funny. His reputation for being a bit unfriendly, a touch dark and even morose is really not true. In real life he’s loving, warm and philanthropic. Just a bit misunderstood.

#### “*Piercingly funny… fiendishly funny, as dry as a dead man’s bones*.” — The List

#### “*There is plenty of enjoyment to be had in his downbeat meanderings on the futility of life*.” Chortle

#### “*Mike Gunn will make you die laughing*.” — The Guardian

#### Highly Commended Comedy Award — Time Out Dubai

[https://www.mikegunn.co.uk/](https://www.mikegunn.co.uk/)

events.description:
**_Update_ This has been moved forward from 3:30 to 2pm.**

**We are very excited to say that Stewart Lee will be at bookhaus to sign copies of his new Illustrated book Pea Green Boat. He will be here for an hour to sign books so come early to avoid disappointment.**

'Stewart Lee is not funny and has nothing to say.' – _**The Daily Telegraph**_

'Stewart Lee’s take on Edward Lear’s _The Owl and the Pussycat_ employs the qualities I admire in his comedy stand-up work. It is funny, violent, surreal, compassionate, existential, vulgar, elegant, very funny, and very sad. I love it.' _–_**** **Dame Sheila Hancock**

_**I am having problems relating to my crew member, having never been a great fan of cats, nor they of birds. Why have we been press ganged into service together? What can they hope to achieve by sending this absurd duo out to sea? I am an owl. The Cat is a cat...**_

In _Pea Green Boat_, Stewart Lee and David Waywell create a dark, grotesque retelling of _The Owl and the Pussycat_ in which Edward Lear's characters are revealed to be catastrophically poorly-equipped for maritime travel. Told through the increasingly deranged diary of the Owl, the real story is unmasked – he cannot open the honey jar due to his lack of opposable thumbs, he is terrified the cat will eat him in his sleep, and he struggles to play the guitar despite having no fingers. As hunger, exhaustion and poor navigation take their toll, it becomes clear that these two creatures should never have been put in a boat together.

Inspired by the cult 2001 stage piece, _Pea Green Boat_ blends Lee’s fascination with Edward Lear with his own comedy. Now, with David's gothic-comic illustrations, the story is brought vividly, hilariously and unsettlingly to life.

events.description:
Star of Live At The Apollo, Have I Got News For You, QI, Richard Osman’s House of Games & Comedy Central Live; Ignacio Lopez returns with perhaps his most ambitious and pretentious project yet.

Nada is the captivating comedy experiment which sees Spain’s Best Export create a brand new, completely unique and blisteringly funny stand up show right in front of your eyes, from absolutely nothing!

Mining his hilarious upbringing, growing up in Mallorca and South Wales, as well as suggestions from the crowd, and everything he’s learnt performing comedy since 2010, Ignacio crafts an intricate story of mystery and suspense packed with sarcasm, silliness and huge laughs.

As well as dazzling viewers with his quick-wit and charm on almost every UK TV station, Ignacio’s talents have seen him headlining all the top comedy clubs, cruises, corporate and military shows worldwide and his acclaimed, sold out tour shows all over the UK prove he’s an act not to be missed.

#### “*Charming, charismatic, hilarious. Will have you leaving with a smile on your face*” – Deadline News

events.summary: Mark Thomas celebrates forty years of stand-up, counted out in numbers.
events.description:
What?! Mark Thomas has been ‘standing up’ for 40 years? Impossible!! But how old does that make you…? Alas it is true; one of our oldest surviving alternative comics celebrates 40 years at the mic.

So, here’s what he has done so far in numbers; performed comedy for 40 years, won 8 awards for performing, 4 for human rights work and 1 he invented for himself, made 6 series of the Mark Thomas Comedy Product (Channel 4), written 6 books and 5 play scripts, made 5 series of the Manifesto for Radio 4, made 3 Dispatches for Channel 4, sued the police (and won) 3 times, curated and authored 2 art exhibitions with artist Tracey Moberly and had 1 Guinness World Record for holding 20 protests in 24 hours.

If that’s not enough, he’s also walked 724km around the length of the Israel Wall in the West Bank, been credited with changing the law on tax avoidance, started a comedy club in Palestine with Dr Sam Beale and campaigned successfully for things like trade union recognition for cinema workers and getting multinationals to change their practices. You’re right, there’s more, but your attention is running out and we’re running out of space. So let’s just say he’s generally mucked about trying to have fun and upset the right people…which he is really, really good at.

So basically expect a taster menu of government and personal mayhem, jokes, rants and a personal state of the nation broadcast as he tries to turn ‘what the f*ck is going on’ into a cogent hour of stand-up.

★★★★★ “*Once again shooting laughter-laden political bullets from the lip*” THE RECS
