events.title: Doom Painting launch with A. K. Blakemore

price.text: £7 (includes a glass of wine or soft drink)

events.raw:
**Doom Painting launch with A. K. Blakemore**

— Bookhaus
events.summary: A. K. Blakemore (*The Manningtree Witches*, *The Glutton*) launches *Doom Painting*, her retelling of the 1381 Peasants' Revolt over sixteen days from Brentwood to London, in conversation with Bristol novelist Danielle Giles (*Mere*). £7 with a drink and £2 off the book.
events.description:
It is 1381. England, reeling from plague and years of conflict abroad, is a tinderbox waiting to spark.

Two childhood friends ride into the town of Brentwood, Essex, where they come upon an altercation with a local Justice bent on squeezing more coin from the masses. Thus begins a rebellion of the common folk - loyal to the king, but not to those wealthy landowners who curtail their freedoms; the multitude finding cause against the powers that threaten their livelihoods. Set over sixteen days, Doom Painting roves across England as the revolt grows and swells and the rebels march to London to take their demands to the child-king Richard II.

Out of the rebellion emerges its enigmatic and charismatic leader Wat Tyler, an opportunistic and mercurial rogue whose morality is birthed by the cause, and who shapes an identity for the English which has never been lost. A. K.

Blakemore's thrilling retelling of the Peasants' Revolt renders it a definitive moment in British history. In the meeting of peasantry and nobility, new versions of England are born, and - for one bloody summer - the people of England seize control.

We are delighted to be joined by A. K. here at bookhaus, who will be in conversation with Danielle Giles, author of MERE. Tickets cost £7 and include a glass of wine or a soft drink and £2 off the book. Presented by bookhaus.

Danielle Giles is a writer and researcher based in Bristol. She has been published in Extra Teeth and Dear Damsels, shortlisted for the Bristol Short Story Prize and the Brick Lane Bookshop Short Story Prize, and longlisted for the Galley Beggar Press Short Story Prize. She won the Local Prize in the 2023 Bath Short Story Award. MERE is her first novel; her second historical gothic, GENTLE THINGS, will be released in late July.

On _The Glutton_ and _The Manningtree Witches_:

'Riveting, appalling, addictive' _Megan Nolan_

'There are few writers who can be truly likened to Hilary Mantel, but Blakemore is one' _Observer_

events.timesText: Exhibition Sat 3 – Thu 8 Oct, daily 11:00–18:00; Private View/Opening Night Fri 2 Oct 18:00–22:00

price.text: Admission is free; tickets are not required.

events.raw:
**Faces/Spaces #6** — Fri, 2 Oct 2026 11:00 to Thu, 8 Oct 2026 18:00, Centrespace Gallery & Studios

Faces/Spaces #6 is the sixth annual joint exhibition by collage artist Kelvin Jenkins and ceramicist Rose Pettit.

Exhibition Dates: Saturday 3rd October - Thursday 8th October
PV: Friday 2nd October, 6:00 pm - 10:00 pm
Opening Hours: Daily, 11:00 am - 6:00 pm
events.summary: Sixth annual pairing of collage artist Kelvin Jenkins and ceramicist Rose Pettit — improvised non-representational collage alongside playful hand-built stoneware creatures of sea and air; opening night Friday 2 October. Free.
events.description:
Faces/Spaces #6 is the sixth annual joint exhibition by collage artist Kelvin Jenkins and ceramicist Rose Pettit.

For the past year, Rose Pettit has found herself drawn to ‘making animals of the sea and air’, using a play on words ending in “fish”. All of her work is hand-built using stoneware clay and glazes. She remarks that ‘these pieces are meant to amuse and make others smile’.

Kelvin Jenkins, staying true to the recycling ethos of collage, has been improvising with non-representational collage, using cut-offs from previous works as a starting point and seeing where it leads. ‘This process can take my visual language in unexpected directions, which I then work with to complete the picture.’

**Dates:** Saturday 3rd October - Thursday 8th October
**Private View/Opening Night:** Friday 2nd October | 6:00 pm - 10:00 pm
**Opening Hours:** Daily | 11:00 am - 6:00 pm
**Participating Artists:** Kelvin Jenkins | Rose Pettit
**Social Media / Websites:** @faces.spaces.ceramics
**Entry:** Admission is free; tickets are not required.

**Accessibility:** The exhibition space is fully wheelchair accessible, with step-free entry and wide pathways throughout. An accessible toilet is available on-site. Seating is provided within the exhibition for visitors who may need to rest. We welcome assistance dogs, and staff are available to offer support if needed.

If you have specific access requirements or would like to plan your visit, please contact centrespacegallery@gmail.com — we’re happy to help.

PROGRAMME: to include a selection of the absolute stand-outs from the world of opera, featuring the sublime 'Soave sia il vento' from Mozart's _Così fan tutte_, Puccini's 'Nessun dorma', and the iconic 'Habanera' from _Carmen_, alongside much-loved favourites such as Rossini's 'Largo al factotum', Verdi's 'La donna è mobile', and Puccini's soaring 'O mio babbino caro'.

events.description:
## Stand Up For The Weekend with Carey Marx & Guests Featuring Joey Page plus compere Jack Campbell

#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available.

#### Headliner: CAREY MARX

Carey Marx is an unapologetic gagsmith. The jokes are short and sharp, often uncomfortably so, as any morality is sacrificed on the altar of quick laughs. And there’s no better way of guaranteeing a reaction than storming headlong into decidedly dodgy territory.

There’s plenty here for the connoisseur of comedy writing. The lines are efficient, original and potent – and rarely fail to blindside the audience.

And they come at a blistering rate, thanks to a hugely economical delivery. He doesn’t go out of the way to befriend an audience, yet there is a subtle charm and intelligence to him, even when the material is blatantly offensive.

#### “*Hilariously demented*” Edinburgh Evening News

#### “*Anecdotally debauched … But if his lines are frequently sick, they’re elegantly written, too, and there’s a childlike glee to his naughtiness*.” The Herald

https://www.facebook.com/CareyMarxComedy/

events.description:
# Woodwork for Beginners Level 1 – The Toolbox

This introductory woodworking course teaches students to create a
softwood toolbox with a handle and inset base using traditional hand
tools and corner rebate joints. Upon completion, participants take
home their finished toolbox and gain foundational skills to pursue
home projects or advance to Level 2 classes.

**LEARN HOW TO:**

- Sawing straight and square
- Accurately marking out and cutting joints
- Effectively using hand tools including chisels and planes
- Fitting and finishing woodwork projects

**Skill level:** "Suitable for those with no previous woodwork
experience or, more experienced woodworkers wanting to improve their
skills and accuracy."

**Course options available:**

1. Thursday or Friday Daytime Classes — 10:30am to 3:40pm
2. Tuesday Evening Classes — 6:20pm to 8:45pm
3. Weekend Daytime Classes — 10:30am to 4:40pm

events.summary: Pulitzer winner Benjamin Moser launches *Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History*, tracing generations of Jewish thinkers who opposed Zionism, in conversation with Matt of Working Class History. £7 includes a drink and £3 off the book.
events.description:
### What is _Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History_ by Benjamin Moser about?

**‘An important and revelatory contribution’** WILLIAM DALRYMPLE

**‘A book of extraordinary moral clarity’** NATHAN THRALL

**A sweeping and revelatory history of the hidden tradition of Jewish thinkers who opposed Zionism from Pulitzer Prize winner Benjamin Moser.**

In _Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History,_ Benjamin Moser uncovers a suppressed tradition that has shaped Jewish thought for generations. Through a cast of artists, rabbis, poets, lawyers, activists, journalists and politicians – from Europe and Africa and Asia and Latin America – Moser traces a lineage of Jewish dissenters who confronted Zionism’s moral and political stakes – often at devastating personal cost, including censorship, exile and death.

Their lives form a sweeping, global narrative that dismantles a powerful myth: that anti-Zionism is synonymous with antisemitism. Spanning continents and centuries, these voices – people from the right and the left, Reform and Orthodox, Ashkenazic and Sephardic, men and women, gay and straight – differ sharply in belief and background, yet converge on a shared warning about the consequences of a nationalist project built on exclusion. What emerges is not only a rediscovered tradition of Jewish moral thought, but a startling reappraisal of Zionism itself.

Moser’s work restores the full scale and depth of Jewish ethical imagination, affirming that Judaism is older and larger than any single political project. Lucid, unsparing and deeply humane, _Anti-Zionism_ cements Moser’s place as one of our foremost Jewish writers and presents a framework through which this history – and its meanings – will be understood for years to come.

We are delighted to welcome Benjamin to Bristol for this urgent and timely event. He will be in conversation with Matt (Working Class History). Tickets cost £7 and include a glass of wine or soft drink and £3 off the book. Presented by bookhaus.

**‘A lovingly-written historical primer for the free-thinkers of the West today’** ISABELLA HAMMAD, author of _Enter Ghost_

**‘What I learned in these pages has profoundly changed my understanding of history – the world's, my people's, my family's, and my own’** AYELET WALDMAN, author of _A Perfect Hand_

**‘An urgently necessary refutation … I hope it will be widely read’** PETER SINGER, author of _The Life You Can Save_

Lecture/Talk

events.summary: Unveiling of three new public artworks at the Temple Quarter campus — by John Wood and Paul Harrison, Ellie Shipman and Room 13 Hareclive — with a drinks reception, a screening of Room 13's short film and a panel with the artists chaired by Beth Williamson. Opens the Autumn Art Lecture Series; book via Eventbrite.
events.description:
Join us for an evening of celebration as we unveil three new public artworks by John Wood and Paul Harrison, Ellie Shipman, and Room 13 Hareclive. The new commissions include two permanent installations on the ground floor of the Sloane Robinson Building, alongside a newly commissioned short film.

[Click here to book your place via Eventbrite.](https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/introducing-public-art-at-temple-quarter-enterprise-campus-tickets-1997967803484)

The evening will include an opportunity to experience the artworks, followed by a panel discussion exploring the ideas, collaborations, and creative processes behind the commissions.

- 6 pm - 7 pm - View the Artworks and Enjoy a Drinks Reception
- 7 pm - 8:15 pm - Screening and Panel Discussion

Professor Beth Williamson will be in conversation with artists John Wood and Paul Harrison, Shani Ali of Room 13 Hareclive, and Ellie Shipman, alongside Megan O'Shea, Contemporary Art Society Consultancy.

This talk forms part of the [Autumn Art Lecture Series](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/arts-law-social-sciences/research/autumn-art-lectures/), which explores the public art programme for the Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus.

Watch Rivers - A Race Against Time, a newly commissioned short film by Room 13 Hareclive: [Wild Spaces – Public art at the University of Bristol](https://public-art.bristol.ac.uk/public-art-at-temple-quarter/wild-spaces/rivers-a-race-against-time/).

**We are absolutely delighted to be hosting David McKay, the award-winning translator of Dutch fiction and non-fiction, who will be discussing his latest translation of Anjet Daanje's *The Song of Stork and Dromedary*. This will be a fantastic and riveting evening spent discussing what it takes to bring a Dutch novel into English.**

**Date:**
Tuesday 6th of October

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 19:00. Finish approx 20:00.

**Tickets:**
£6 ticket only
£25 ticket with The Song of Stork and Dromedary (hardback)
£12.99 ticket with The Remembered Soldier (paperback)

You don't need to bring your ticket with you, we will have a list of names on the door. Books will be available to buy on the night.

**ABOUT THE BOOKS**

***The Song of Stork and Dromedary***

**Inspired by the life and work of Emily Brontë, this masterful, multi-award-winning book — acclaimed as the best Dutch novel published this century — pulls readers into a narrative that redefines time itself.**

In the early 1800s, in Yorkshire, Eliza May Drayden and her sisters live far from the public eye, devoted to their shared love of reading and writing books. When, after dozens of rejections, Eliza May’s only novel, *Haeger Mass*, is finally published, it’s labelled as ‘ghastly’ and ‘immoral’. Over time, however, it is embraced by generations of readers as a masterpiece, and tales about its mysterious, reclusive author take on a life of their own.

In eleven extraordinary chapters, the story of Eliza May — both before and after her death — unfolds: through the tales of people who met her; her sister’s letters; her biographers’ words; the pages of a mysterious notebook; and the lives that become intertwined with hers, even centuries later.

In *The Song of Stork and Dromedary*, Anjet Daanje has crafted an absorbing literary mystery and an unforgettable meditation on love, life, loss, and the inexplicable nature of time. As the Brontës themselves did, Daanje shows us that storytelling is our only way to transcend death.

***The Remembered Soldier***

**An extraordinary love story and a captivating novel about the power of memory and imagination.**

Flanders 1922. After serving as a soldier in the Great War, Noon Merckem has lost his memory and lives in a psychiatric asylum. Countless women, responding to a newspaper ad, visit him there in the hope of finding their spouse who vanished in battle. One day a woman, Julienne, appears and recognises Noon as her husband, the photographer Amand Coppens, and takes him home against medical advice. But their miraculous reunion doesn’t turn out the way that Julienne wants her envious friends to believe. Only gradually do the two grow close, and Amand’s biography is pieced together on the basis of Julienne’s stories about him. But how can he be certain that she’s telling the truth?

In *The Remembered Soldier*, Anjet Daanje immerses us in the psyche of a war-traumatised man who has lost his identity. When Amand comes to doubt Julienne’s word, the reader is caught up in a riveting spiral of confusion that only the greatest works of literature can achieve.

*Longlisted for the 2026 International Booker Prize.*

**ABOUT THE TRANSLATOR**

**David McKay** is an award-winning translator of Dutch fiction and nonfiction. Born and educated in the United States, he has lived in and around The Hague since 1997.

**Manuscripts, Monks, and the Merit of Incremental Knowledge - Inaugural Lecture of Professor Benjamin Pohl** @ Clifton campus — Wed, 7 Oct @ 4:00pm

Inaugural lecture

We are pleased to invite you to the inaugural lecture of Benjamin Pohl, Professor of Medieval History, being held in B.H05 Lecture Theatre, 7 Woodland Road. Doors will open from 3:45 pm for a prompt start.
events.summary: Benjamin Pohl's inaugural lecture as Professor of Medieval History: a career in manuscript culture retraced from Germany to Bristol, and a case for knowledge built incrementally by forensic detective work. Free and open to the public, in person or livestreamed, followed by a drinks reception; Eventbrite registration is essential.
events.description:
We are pleased to invite you to the inaugural lecture of **Benjamin Pohl, Professor of Medieval History**, being held in **B.H05 Lecture Theatre**, 7 Woodland Road. Doors will open from 3:45 pm for a prompt start.

In his lecture, **Manuscripts, Monks, and the Merit of Incremental Knowledge**, Benjamin reflects on an academic career driven by curiosity, passion for detail, and a fascination for the unknown. Re-tracing his journey from his native Germany to the UK in pursuit of historical research on the Middle Ages and its manuscript culture, he discusses personal highlights and turning points in his path to a professorship. The discoveries presented in this inaugural lecture urge us to embrace the incremental way in which our knowledge about the past is generated through forensic detective work and skills that are built over time, allowing us to stand on the shoulders of giants.

The lecture will be followed by a **drinks reception, from 5:00 to 6:30 pm**, providing an opportunity to celebrate the occasion and meet with colleagues and guests.

For those unable to join in person, the lecture will be **livestreamed via MS Teams (link via Eventbrite confirmation)**. Please note that the lecture will be recorded.

If you are attending in person and have any accessibility requirements (e.g. use of mobility aids, sight or hearing impairment, etc.), please let us know so that we can put in place the necessary arrangements.

**IMPORTANT: This is a free but ticketed event. Registration via Eventbrite is essential for all attendees, whether joining in person or online.**

**[Tickets via Eventbrite](https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/inaugural-lecture-of-professor-benjamin-pohl-in-person-and-online-tickets-1991367382447?aff=oddtdtcreator)**

Your attendance and support at this event are greatly appreciated, and we hope you will be able to join us in marking this important milestone in Benjamin's career.

Inaugural lectures are an opportunity for academics to share their achievements in research, innovation, engagement and teaching activities before an audience of members of the University community and the general public.

Organiser: School of Humanities.

events.title: The Past Pursues Us: Juan Pablo Villalobos
events.raw:
**_The Past Pursues Us_: Juan Pablo Villalobos**

Wednesday 7th October, Gloucester Road Bookshop at 7.00 pm

Mexican author in conversation with poet, translator and academic, Rebecca Kosick

[Book tickets](https://hdfst.uk/e160904) (this link will take you to external site HeadFirst Bristol)
events.summary: A rare UK appearance by Mexican novelist Juan Pablo Villalobos (*Down the Rabbit Hole*) on *The Past Pursues Us Like Detectives, Debt Collectors, Thieves*, translated by Daniel Hahn — a darkly funny novel in which JP returns to Mexico to care for his mother and becomes a murder suspect. In conversation with Rebecca Kosick of the Bristol Poetry Institute; ticketed through Headfirst.
events.description:
In a rare UK appearance, master of surreal humour, wit and invention, Juan Pablo Villalobos, is joining us to discuss his superb novel, _The Past Pursues Us Like Detectives, Debt Collectors, Thieves_, in conversation with the poet, translator and academic, Rebecca Kosick.

Translated by Daniel Hahn, the novel follows JP on his return to Mexico to care for his increasingly frail mother. His plan is upended when he becomes the prime suspect in a murder enquiry following an altercation with a childhood 'friend'. The result is a very witty, humane and darkly engrossing novel that further enhances Villlalobos' reputation as a wonderfully singular writer and makes this an event not to be missed!

---

Juan Pablo Villalobos was born in Mexico in 1973. He's the author of the novels _Down the Rabbit Hole_ (shortlisted for The Guardian First Book Award), _Quesadillas_, _I'll Sell You a Dog_, _I Won't Expect Anyone to Believe Me_ and _The Invasion of the Spirit People_, and of the non-fiction book _The Other Side: Stories of Central American Teens Who Dream of Crossing the Border_. His books have been translated into more than 15 languages. _Down the Rabbit Hole_ and _I Won't Expect Anyone to Believe Me_ were adapted for film and premiered on Netflix. He lives in Barcelona, where he teaches writing.

Rebecca Kosick is a poet, translator, and Associate Professor of Comparative Poetry and Poetics at the University of Bristol, where she also codirects the Bristol Poetry Institute. She has published four books, most recently _Dispatches from the Avant-Garage: The Alternative Press_.

'A rambunctious picaresque of contemporary Mexican life, rendered into English by [Daniel] Hahn with appropriate energy.'
— Kit Maude, _Times Literary Supplement_

'Juan Pablo Villalobos ... demonstrates his classic wit and penchant for the absurd, blurring the lines of genre and protagonist with its author.'
— Andrés Ordorica, The Skinny

'_The Past Pursues Us_ is a masterful example of how to push autobiography to the extremes of fiction, allowing the imagination to explore themes rooted in the author's life. Themes that, when taken to their limits, reveal a sharp glimpse of an inexorable truth.'
— Nicolás Giacobone, screenwriter of Birdman

**Everyone is welcome at our Contemporary Fiction book club, where on the first Wednesday of every month we discuss a recently-published paperback novel. In October, we'll be delving into *Drayton and McKenzie by Alexander Starritt*, a Sunday Times, GQ, and Financial Times 2025 Book of the Year. **

***Date:*
Wednesday 7th of October

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**

Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *Drayton and McKenzie***

**A TIMES/SUNDAY TIMES, GQ, FINANCIAL TIMES AND BLOOMBERG BEST BOOK OF THE YEAR 2025**

*‘A big, bustling novel about love, friendship, money, ambition and the 21st century, packed with humour and intelligent observations … I finished it tear-stained’ Sunday Times*

*‘Will have you hooked … an ode to the enduring power of male friendship’ The Times Best Summer Books*

*‘My book of the summer’ Janice Turner*

*‘Thrilling’ Guardian*

For the first time since university, James and Roland’s paths through life – one drawn in straight lines, the other squiggled and meandering – began to cross…

James Drayton has always found things too easy. By the time he leaves university, he’s still waiting for a challenge worthy of his ambitions. Roland Mackenzie, on the other hand, is an impulsive risk-taker, a charismatic drifter with a knack for derailing his own attempts to get started in life.

When a chance encounter in a pub reunites these old acquaintances, it sets them on an unpredictable course through the upheavals of the twenty-first century, and sparks an unlikely alliance. Sent to Aberdeen during the financial crisis to lay off hundreds of workers, James and Roland begin to wonder: what if they were made for more than this? What if together they could build something grand and lasting – something that might even change the world?

events.title: Bring Down the Haus: JLM Morton

price.text: £7 (includes a glass of wine or soft drink)

events.raw:
**Bring Down the Haus: JLM Morton**

— Bookhaus

spoken word / poetry
events.summary: Bring Down the Haus poetry night: JLM Morton launches *Borrowed Ground*, her second collection, rooted in west-of-England woodland and river country and the mythic drowning of Sabrina, goddess of the Severn — with other poets to be confirmed. £7 with a drink.
events.description:
We are pleased to welcome back JLM Morton for the launch of her second poetry collection, Borrowed Ground.

_Borrowed Ground_ is JLM Morton's second full collection, a reckoning with land, climate grief, and the entanglement of human and more-than-human life. Rooted in the woodland and river country of the west of England, the poems move between close observation and myth: a central creation sequence follows a black pine through litany and shaped, fragmenting text, while a closing sequence stages the drowning and mythic rebirth of Sabrina, goddess of the Severn. Morton works through erasure, found material, and liturgical forms without losing lyric precision, holding ecological dread against humour, domestic comfort, and ancient, feminist modes of knowing.

Come along and hear JLM (and other poets tbc). Tickets cost £7 and include a glass of wine or a soft drink. Presented by bookhaus.

JLM Morton is a writer, celebrant and creative producer based in the west of England. Her poetry has featured on BBC6 Music and is widely published, including in _Poetry Review_, _Poetry London_, _Rialto_, _Magma_, _Mslexia_, and _The London Magazine_. Winner of the Geoffrey Dearmer, Laurie Lee and Poetry Archive Worldview Prizes, her debut poetry collection was _Red Handed_ (Broken Sleep Books, 2024), highly commended by the Forward Prizes and a Poetry Society book of the year. Her first nonfiction book is forthcoming in Spring 2027.

events.title: Meg Mason: Sophie, Standing There

price.text: £8.00 – £20.00 (event ticket only £10; low income £8; ticket + copy of Sophie, Standing There £20)

events.raw:
**Meg Mason: Sophie, Standing There**

Thursday 8th October 2026, 7pm

£8.00 – £20.00
events.summary: Meg Mason, whose *Sorrow and Bliss* won British Book of the Year and was shortlisted for the Women's Prize, on her new novel *Sophie, Standing There* — a bittersweet story of loneliness and an unlikely connection — in conversation with Monica Heisey (*Really Good, Actually*, Schitt's Creek). At The Station on Silver Street, not the shop.
events.description:
_The Station, Silver Street, Bristol, BS1 2AG ([click here for a map](https://maps.app.goo.gl/3exg7KQv8vD3BaEGA)) For venue access info, [click here](https://www.accessable.co.uk/bristol-city-council/access-guides/the-station)._

We are delighted to welcome the international bestselling author of the seminal novel Sorrow and Bliss, **Meg Mason**, to Bristol this autumn! She’ll be here to discuss her new novel **Sophie, Standing There** with fellow author and chronicler of life’s ineffable difficulties, **Monica Heisey**(author of equally-beloved bestseller [Really Good Actually](https://storysmithbooks.com/product/really-good-actually-2/), writer on Schitt’s Creek).

Sorrow and Bliss won Book of the Year at the British Book Awards, was shortlisted for the Women’s Prize, and has been translated into more than 30 languages. Sophie, Standing There is one of the most anticipated books of the year, and has already won praise from Gillian Anderson and Ann Patchett (no biggie).

**Pre-order your copy of Sophie, Standing There** (rrp £20.00) for a special discounted price with your ticket, then collect on the night!

**About Meg Mason**

Meg Mason is the author of You Be Mother and Sorrow and Bliss, which became an international bestseller after it was published in 2021. Winner of the British Book Industry Book of the Year, and shortlisted for the Women’s Prize, it has since been translated into twenty-five languages. Her first career was in journalism, beginning at The Times of London, and later writing for Vogue, Elle, GQ, and humour for the New Yorker’s Daily Shouts. Born in New Zealand, she lives in Sydney with her husband and two daughters.

**About Sophie, Standing There**

**From the award-winning, bestselling author of Sorrow and Bliss comes an achingly tender, poignant, funny and bittersweet new novel**

_‘Heartwarming, tender and so funny, Sophie, Standing There is a wonderful, bittersweet story of what it means to be truly, achingly lonely. I loved it’_ – Gillian Anderson

_‘So smart, so funny, so moving. I absolutely loved it’_ Bonnie Garmus, bestselling author of Lessons in Chemistry

_‘A moving examination of what it means to be alone in the world, and what it means to find connection. It is, by turns, heartbreaking, hilarious, and deeply hopeful. Meg Mason is a dazzling talent’_ Ann Patchett, bestselling author of Tom Lake and The Dutch House

Sophie Pattison is a lovely person – warm, kind, relentlessly positive. She’s cherished by her brother Laurie, adored by her best friend Emma and valued by her colleagues. Sometimes, it’s true, one day in her life can feel like the entire month of January. It’s also true she can go an entire day without speaking. But she’s fine really. She spends her time alone reading, finding comfort in the pages of the books she devours.

Until one day she stumbles upon an author she hasn’t read in years. Her books, interviews and podcasts soon become a lifeline; every word is a solace, company she hasn’t felt in so long. It’s almost like love.

A lot like love. And Sophie would love to meet the author, although she never will obviously. In a way, thank goodness, because that would change everything. Sophie’s entire life. Wouldn’t it?

**Hilariously candid and raw, Sophie, Standing There is a bittersweet story of love, loneliness and finding connection in the most unlikely of places.**

_‘Sophie, Standing There unfolds like a strange origami crane in reverse – so achingly tender and so brilliantly subtle that I could never put it down… Dazzling’_ Catherine Newman, bestselling author of Wreck and Sandwich

_‘I loved Sophie, and I love Meg Mason’s brain and the strange, wonderful, funny stories she gives us’_ Ann Napolitano, bestselling author of Hello, Beautiful and Dear Edward

**About Monica Heisey**

Monica Heisey is a writer and comedian from Toronto. She has been published in The New Yorker, The New York Times, Vogue, Elle, The Guardian, Glamour, New York magazine, and VICE, among others. She has written for television shows like Schitt’s Creek, Workin’ Moms, Baroness von Sketch Show, and more. Her debut novel — Really Good, Actually — was published by 4th Estate in 2022 and is a Sunday Times Bestseller. She currently lives in London.

events.description:
How about a trip to the stars on your Thursday night? Planetarium Nights are back this
Autumn!

Discover how astronomers capture the light from distant objects with advanced telescopes in
our revamped science show. Investigate how that light is used to calculate the scale of the
cosmos and to find alien worlds. Join us in the Planetarium to explore our galaxy… and
beyond!

**Highlights:**

- Where is the best place to go stargazing? And how do astronomers see beyond the haze of
  Earth's atmosphere?
- How can we read the fingerprints in the light? And what do they tell us about alien worlds?
- How many galaxies are in the Universe? And how can we work it out by studying one patch of
  sky?

events.description:
The Geologists of 1979 are delighted to invite you to a reunion on 9 and 10 October 2026, celebrating 50 years since they started the course.

Their plans include meeting for lunch on the Friday, followed by a visit to the Geology Department and a tour of the Wills Building including a trip up the tower, followed by an evening meal in a restaurant in Bristol.

On Saturday morning there are the possibilities of a trip down to the caverns below the Clifton suspension bridge (only rediscovered about 20 years ago) with a guide who is a geologist or a walking tour of St Nicks market (they will do a poll once they know who is able to come).

Please forward this invitation to any friends who graduated in 1979 that you are still in touch with.

**Contact**

If you are interested in coming, please email the organiser, John Leeson (BSc Geology 1979) at johnleeson@aol.com. Further details will be communicated closer to the time.

This event is organised by alumni volunteers and is independent of the University of Bristol. The University of Bristol does not accept any liability for this event.

events.raw:
**The Sleep Thief launch with Ibtisam Azem**

— Bookhaus

workshops & classes / talks
events.summary: International Booker-longlisted Palestinian author Ibtisam Azem launches *The Sleep Thief*, her surreal, experimental first novel following Gharib Haifawi's coming of age in Haifa, in conversation with Sabrin Hasbun. £7 with a drink and £2 off the book.
events.description:
‘Sleep thief is what the interrogator called me. I’ll never forget that. I would steal a few seconds of sleep so I could remain steadfast before them. The name stuck; I even dreamt about it, the same dream, night after night. I woke up not knowing what to do and drenched in sweat.’

The experimental first novel from International Booker-Prize longlisted Palestinian author Ibtisam Azem, _The Sleep Thief_ follows the life of Gharib (“the Stranger”) Haifawi as he comes of age, is drawn into resistance, makes friends, meets lovers, pushes back against traditional values, longs to be free of the labels and expectations that burden him, rails against the commodification of suffering, and dreams of a Palestinian identity that will transcend sorrow.

We are delighted to welcome Ibtisam Azem to bookhaus, where she will be in conversation with Sabrin Hasbun. Tickets cost £7 and include a glass of wine or soft drink and £2 off the book. Presented by bookhaus.

Molly Crabapple

> ‘The bohemian Gharib Haifawi is an irresistable guide through the dreams and nightmares of a Palestine that still exists despite the violent superimposition of the Israeli state. Written in prose that evokes in the spirits of Emile Habibi and Daniil Kharms, The Sleep Thief is a surreal, brilliant dagger of a book.’

### Hannah Lillith Assadi

> ‘Ibtisam Azem's _The Sleep Thief_ is the surreal and gorgeously imagined story of Palestinian Gharib Haifawi of Haifa. Rendered in the poetic register of a dream, this narrative tracks its protagonist's coming of age against the historical years between the Naksa and the Intifadas. This beautiful debut novel is a portrait of resistance, grief, and ultimate triumph.’

### The International Booker Prize 2025 Judges (On The Book of Disappearance)

> 'Speculative and haunting, this is an exceptional exercise in memory-making and psycho-geography'

events.description:
Has an artwork ever made you hot under the collar? How often have you walked through a gallery, tried to focus on the text panel, but, really, just been enamoured by the drop dead gorgeous guy staring back at you?

Offering a fresh and humorous introduction to art and written by Museum Bums co-author **Jack Shoulder**, this book searches art history, across movements and throughout the world to find the most alluring artworks - some famous while others rarely ever seen before. Whether you are looking for boyfriend material, a heavenly hunk, a bright young thing or even holding out for a hero, there is a Museum Hottie carefully curated for you.

Originally from Melbourne, Michael Schafar is now based in London where he has quickly become one of the most exciting new acts on the UK comedy circuit. He regularly performs at the country’s biggest clubs where he gets to mock British people for their awful history and terrible food to their faces.​​

If you have lived in Australia, or even just visited there, you might already know Michael from his appearances on Network 10’s The Project and Studio 10, ABC’s Comedy Bites and triple j’s Good Az Friday. Of course, traditional media is dead, so it’s more likely that you might be one of his 100,000+ followers on social media or the 100+ million people who have seen his videos online. You may have also watched his debut special A(LIVE) on Amazon Prime or his most recent special Alright, Next Joke on YouTube.​

events.description:
The University of Bristol is opening its doors on Saturday 10 October for a public programme of events, in celebration of our 150th year and the opening of the new Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus. We would love to see you there.

**Discover** the weird and wonderful research, innovation and creativity happening behind the scenes, told from the perspective of academics, students and community partners.

**Explore** the University's Clifton and TQEC campuses as they come alive with walking tours, exploration zones, lively conversations and debates, and interactive, family-friendly activities.

**Celebrate** with friends, family, neighbours, Bristol residents and our University community. Everyone is welcome; the more the merrier!

Curious about our new campus? Excited by research? Interested to know what student life looks like today? This is an amazing opportunity to go behind the scenes of the University of Bristol, learn something new, and see how this new campus is the start of a wider regeneration project in the heart of our city.

This is a free programme of events and is suitable for all ages.

Some events are ticketed, and others are drop-in. The ticketed events are signposted on the website - please do RSVP to any ticketed events you wish to join to guarantee your place.

[You can see the emerging programme of events here](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/university/150-years/events/).

events.description:
The biggest UK Flight Simulation event of 2026 is landing at Aerospace Bristol!

After six years, the UK is once again hosting its very own flight simulation show and it’s
happening here at Aerospace Bristol. Headlined by Platinum Sponsors MOZA and iniBuilds,
the event will showcase some of the biggest names in flightsim software development and
hardware innovation.

FSimUK will take place over two days with plenty to keep you occupied throughout. Whether
you’re a casual desktop flyer, a hardcore cockpit builder, a pilot in the making or an
interested bystander, this will be an unmissable weekend.

Visit https://fsimuk.bfsg.club for more information and to reserve your free goody bag.

**What to expect?**

- Discover the latest software and hardware from some of the best in the industry.
- Speak to the experts for advice on building or extending your own flightsim environment.
- Find out what’s happening behind the scenes at the FSElite stage in the John James
  Theatre.
- Get to the top of the leader board in the landing challenges to nab yourself a prize.
- Join hands-on workshops for tutorials and demonstrations.

Remember! Annual ticket holders can visit for free with a valid ticket. You can visit at
anytime between 10am-5:30pm.

events.description:
Welcome all you funk brothers and soul sistas to:

**Late Night Funk Club**
 Featuring:
 •⁠ ⁠**Brass Junkies** (All-Star Bristol Brass Band)
 •⁠ ⁠**Black Wax Solution** (DJ)
 •⁠ ⁠Sat 10th October / 10:30pm-2:30aM

_"Autumn hits Bristol, but the night stays warm…_
 _Seven Brass Junkies about to raise a storm!_
 _Full brass, full funk, full room - that's the deal…_
 _October never sounded quite this real."_

—

- ⁠**Brass Junkies** -

All Star Bristol-Based Brass Heroes: The Brass Junkies bring the Mardi Gras sounds of New Orleans street bands to the LNFC dancefloor!

With a diverse repertoire, they perform New Orleans style pop and funk classics in the tradition of the finest American street bands such as Hot 8 Brass Band, The Soul Rebels and The Rebirth Brass band.

Band members have played with some of the best in the business including Kasabian, Tom Jones, Kellis, and Muse in venues such as The Royal Albert Hall, Glastonbury main stage and 'Later' with Jools Holland.

Whatever and wherever they’re playing, you can be certain that this high-energy, good-time music will bring some carnival atmosphere to the place!

Plus, having booked them 5 times before, we’ve requested even more fire power for this one with added musicians for extra horns and extra rhythm for dancefloor euphoria!

—

•⁠ ⁠**Black Wax Solution** -

Funk, Soul and Disco connoisseur, Black Wax Solution is one of our favourite DJ residents. From honing his craft over 25 years, expect immaculate selections and the smoothest of blends to keep the dance floor bouncing all night.

-

Celebrating a birthday or special occasion? Maybe we can sort you out!

Get in touch with us on FB or IG at @latenightfunkclub

Join us for a special Black History Month screening of The Six Triple
Eight, the remarkable true story of the only all-Black, all-female
battalion to serve overseas during World War II. Against the odds, these
trailblazing women overcame discrimination and adversity to make a
lasting impact on history.

Come and be inspired by this powerful story of courage, resilience, and
determination. Don't miss this opportunity to celebrate and reflect on
the extraordinary contributions of these pioneering women.

Settle in with a cup of tea and make yourself a delicious toastie
sandwich while you watch.

This is a free event, and all are welcome.

events.description:
Don’t miss the all-new show from Scotland’s hilarious new stand-up superstar who is widely hailed as one of the most exciting breakthrough artists in the global live comedy scene.

A social media sensation with 100’s of millions of online views, FLOW is Connor Burns’ 5th solo show – an hour of new standup featuring his intelligent and razor-sharp wit, brilliant jokes and his now-signature, single-malt level of Scottish cynicism that blends perfectly with his relatable everyman take on life, and which in 2025, won him the coveted Forth Fringe Award.

Connor sold more than 17,000 tickets for FLOW’s premiere at the 2026 Edinburgh Fringe – before the festival even started! The massive demand for tickets saw him add three extra shows at the 3000 seat Edinburgh Playhouse – the UK’S largest purpose-built theatre – in addition to his full fringe run. His last tour GALLUS also sold huge numbers of seats, added encore dates UK-wide and finished up with a record breaking five sold-out shows in the flagship King’s Theatre during 2026’s Glasgow International Comedy Festival.

He tours extensively across the UK, Australia, Europe, and off-Broadway in 2024 and 2025 as part of the prestigious Fringe Encore Series and the New York Comedy Festival. He released 2 comedy specials GALLUS and Vertigo* (*on comedy powerhouse 800LB Gorilla)

We say all this because you haven’t seen Connor on UK television – no panel shows, no chat shows, no stand-up showcases. It’s all happening as a result of his hilarious live shows and laugh-out-loud social media clips so we are incredibly excited to welcome Connor back to Bristol’s Hen & Chicken – book your tickets fast!

events.raw:
**Emerson's Green** — 11.10.2026, 2:00 pm. Leader: David Hawkins. Category: Botany.

"An exciting chance to make some significant records in an extremely under-recorded
part of town. The monad (1km OS map grid square) that we will target currently has
just a single record to its name in the Botanical Society of Britain and Ireland's
database: Fine-leaved Sandwort *Sabulina tenuifolia*. And what's more, that record
was made in 1898 by none other than the great J. W. White, author of the seminal
The Bristol Flora."

"Meet on Emerson's Green Common just off Emerson's Green Lane at ST668768
///events.ears.brave. Postcode BS16 7HB."
events.summary: Recording botany in a Bristol kilometre square that has exactly one record against it — made in 1898 by J. W. White, who wrote The Bristol Flora. David Hawkins is fairly sure the sandwort he found has gone, and equally sure the afternoon will turn up something. The one meeting on the programme actually inside the city.

events.summary: A movement and clowning show for babies and toddlers up to three, touring early years settings and community spaces across the South West through late October. Ninety minutes including a gentle start and a break; individual tour dates were still unannounced when the page was read.
events.description:
What does that first step feel like? How does interacting with someone else make us feel? Why does rolling over feel so good!

Join us as we journey from 0-3 years old, finding our feet, our feelings and our fun. Find a connection whether you have children of your own, or from when you yourself were a child.

Using movement and clowning, *Wonder Baby* invites children and families to explore physical play and experience the joy of creating space to play together.

Grown from the imaginations and experiences of babies, toddlers and their families – *Wonder Baby* was developed in collaboration with families who took part in the early development of the show.

For 0-3's and their families.

**Duration:** This is a play and performance experience, lasting approximately 90 minutes - this includes a gentle start and time for a break if needed.

**At A Glance:** 11 - 29 October 2026. Various early years settings and community spaces across the South West. Suitable for 0-3's and their families and carers. No public tickets currently available. We will be announcing tour dates in early September.

events.description:
Wednesday Night Improv returns to the Hen & Chicken with two halves of unscripted comedy – all made up on the spot, all inspired by your suggestions. Expect quick wit, bold characters, and the kind of laughter that only happens when nobody knows what’s coming next (including the performers).

**## FIRST HALF ##Comedy Games, Improvised Live**

*(Think Whose Line Is It Anyway? meets Game Changer, with a sprinkling of Taskmaster.)*

A fast, funny first half built around short improvised games – the kind where performers get a prompt from the audience and have seconds to turn it into something brilliant. Points will be awarded. Consequences may follow.

With your host, Ste Brown.

**## SECOND HALF ##The BLANK Who BLANKED Me**

Love stories are with us from a very young age, usually stories of love that is pure and sweet and true. *The BLANK who BLANKED me* is not that kind of love story.

This is the kind of love story where passion strikes like a wrecking ball, leaving you dazed, confused, and madly in love with an unaccountable asshole who does admittedly look really good climbing out of a lake in a thin white shirt…

—

Whether you’re a seasoned comedy fan or just curious about what happens when performers make it all up as they go, this is a perfect night to dive into Bristol’s thriving improv scene. Expect laughter, surprises, and something completely different — every single time.

—

*Part of the Wednesday Night Improv series – second Wednesday of every month.* *Details: https://linktr.ee/wednightimprov*

events.summary: An introduction evening at Grow Wilder with filmmaker and journalist Izzy A'isha, for 16 to 25-year-olds thinking about Wildscreen's free nine-session wildlife filmmaking course that follows on Wednesday evenings from November. This booking is for the taster only; the course itself is by interest form.
events.description:
**Location:** [Grow Wilder](https://www.avonwildlifetrust.org.uk/nature-reserves/grow-wilder), 181 Frenchay Park Road, Bristol, BS16 1EL

Outdoor Activity · Volunteering · Young People

Book on to a taster session to find out more about some FREE wildlife filmmaking workshops running this autumn and winter for 16-25yr olds

**Date:** Wednesday 14 October 2026
**Time:** 6:00pm - 7:30pm

**About the event**

Please note this booking is for the introduction session only. To attend the workshops, we ask you complete an interest form and we will be in touch.

Come to Grow Wilder on Tuesday 14 October to meet Izzy A'isha, filmmaker and journalist and find out more about our upcoming workshops....

We're excited to be hosting Wildscreen, who will be facilitating free wildlife filmmaking workshops for 16-25-year-olds this autumn and winter. Each session will be based at Grow Wilder from 6pm-7.30pm on the following dates:

- 4 November
- 11 November
- 18 November
- 25 November
- 2 December
- 9 December
- 16 December
- 13 January
- 20 January

These workshops will be an opportunity to:

- Learn techniques in storytelling
- Understand how to engage different audiences
- Use and try high quality hands-on equipment
- Learn and use editing and film production techniques
- Explore wildlife filmmaking career options through meeting and hearing from experts in the industry

If you're interested in attending the workshops please fill out this form: [Wildlife Filmmaking Workshops with Wildscreen [Nature Story] – Fill out form](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/sgm1s8ahpn)

**How to get here**

Grow Wilder (181 Frenchay Park Rd, Bristol, BS16 1EL) is well connected to walking, cycling and bus routes. If you're coming by bike, there are bike racks as you come in the main entrance of the site.

If travelling by car, Begbrook Social Club has kindly offered space in their car park which is located nearby - less than a five-minute walk away. If you have any accessibility needs, please let me know and we can get you access to park on site.

If coming by bus from central Bristol the m1, m3 and m4 metrobuses run regularly, and stop at Begbrook, which is located at the back entrance of Grow Wilder.

**Booking:** Email [youngpeople@avonwildlifetrust.org.uk](mailto:youngpeople@avonwildlifetrust.org.uk)

**Know before you go:** Assistance dogs only. Facilities: toilets, picnic area, accessible toilet, baby changing facilities.

events.raw:
**IEEE Public Event: Flexible Electronics in Healthcare** @ The Sloane Robinson Building — Thu, 15 Oct @ 6:30pm

Workshop

Agenda: 6:30 pm – 6:40 pm: Registration (Open to all IEEE and non-IEEE Members); 6:45 pm – 6:50 pm: Welcome by Dr Faezeh Arab Hassani, Senior Lecturer, School of Electrical, Electronic, and Mechanical …
events.summary: An evening panel on how wearable, implantable and skin-mounted electronics could change diagnosis, monitoring and NHS care, with speakers from academia, industry and clinical practice, followed by posters, canapés and drinks. Open to non-members of the IEEE; register via the online form.
events.description:
**Agenda**

- **6:30 pm – 6:40 pm**: [Registration](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=MH_ksn3NTkql2rGM8aQVG2fD-ThcxFhBuJ6J0Cb32r5UN1A0UzRLTUpXQlE5SkUyM0NVM1NIM1JXNi4u&route=shorturl) (Open to all IEEE and non-IEEE Members)
- **6:45 pm – 6:50 pm**: Welcome by Dr Faezeh Arab Hassani, Senior Lecturer, School of Electrical, Electronic, and Mechanical Engineering, University of Bristol
- **6:50 pm – 7 pm**: Introduction to research at the University of Bristol by Prof. Annela Seddon, Associate Pro Vice Chancellor (Research & Innovation) for the Faculty of Science and Engineering, University of Bristol
- **7 pm – 7:10 pm**: Introduction to the IEEE UK and Ireland Section activities by Prof. Nagham Saeed, Chair of the IEEE UK and Ireland Section, University of West London
- **7:10 pm – 8:30 pm**: Panel: Flexible electronics in healthcare
- **8:30 pm – 9 pm**: Networking and posters (Canapés and drinks)

**Panel: Flexible electronics in healthcare**

In this panel, we will discuss how flexible electronics can transform healthcare by enabling next-generation wearable, implantable, and skin-mounted medical technologies.

The conversation will explore how these devices can support continuous monitoring, early diagnosis, personalised treatment, and remote patient care. Panellists from academia, industry, and clinical practice will share perspectives on the scientific advances, clinical needs, and commercial opportunities driving the field.

The panel will also examine key challenges, including device reliability, patient comfort, data interpretation, regulation, and NHS adoption. Overall, the discussion will highlight what is needed to move flexible electronics from research prototypes into real-world healthcare solutions.

**[Click here to register.](https://forms.cloud.microsoft/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=MH_ksn3NTkql2rGM8aQVG2fD-ThcxFhBuJ6J0Cb32r5UN1A0UzRLTUpXQlE5SkUyM0NVM1NIM1JXNi4u&route=shorturl)**

events.title: Bring Down the Haus: Laura Blomvall, Matt Haw and Isabelle Thompson

price.text: £7 (includes a glass of wine or soft drink)

events.raw:
**Bring Down the Haus: Laura Blomvall, Matt Haw and Isabelle Thompson**

— Bookhaus

spoken word / poetry
events.summary: Bring Down the Haus returns with three poets reading from recent work: Windmill Hill-based Finnish poet Laura Blomvall (*Enter Moon*), Matt Haw (*Nordic Sublime*, longlisted for the Jerwood Prize) and Isabelle Thompson (*Stalin's Parrot*). £7 with a drink.
events.description:
We are excited to bring back our Bring Down the Haus series fo poetry readings with this trio of poets.

Laura Blomvall is a Finnish poet living in Windmill Hill, Bristol. Her poems have appeared in _The Poetry Review, Propel Magazine_, A Mouthful of Air podcast and elsewhere. Her debut poetry pamphlet, _Enter Moon_, was published by Broken Sleep Books in September 2025.

Matt Haw was born in south-east England and educated at Bath Spa University and Lancaster University. He is the author of _Nordic Sublime_ (Shearsman 2026) and two chapbooks, _Saint-Paul-de-Mausole_ (tall-lighthouse, 2014) and _Boudicca_ (Templar, 2021). _Nordic Sublime_ was longlisted for the Jerwood Prize for Best First Collection 2026 and his work has also been recognised with an Eric Gregory Award, the iOTA Shots Pamphlet Award and an East Anglian Book Award.

Isabelle Thompson is a graduate of Bath Spa University’s MA in Creative Writing, where she now works as a research assistant supporting programmes looking into story skills and inclusive support for writers. She is widely published in magazines, and her poetry has appeared on BBC Upload. She was the winner of the 2022 _Poets and Players_ competition, finalist in the 2021 _Mslexia_ single poem competition, and shortlisted for the 2025 Bridport Prize. Her debut pamphlet, _Stalin’s Parrot_, is published with Poetry Space. Her unpublished pamphlet, _All Those Who Will Be Saved_, was highly commended in the Cinnamon Press pamphlet competition.

Come and hear these poests read from their recent work. Tickets cost £7 and include a glass of wine or a soft drink. Presented by bookhaus.

events.description:
St Anne's House is pleased to be hosting the Home Energy Fair,
delivered by Retrofit West and funded by the West of England Mayoral
Combined Authority.

Whether you're planning improvements or simply curious about making
your home warmer, healthier and more energy efficient, this free
event is a great opportunity to explore the latest retrofit solutions
and speak directly with experts.

**What to expect**

- Learn about energy-efficient home improvements and the upgrades
  available for your property.
- Explore virtual tours of homes that have already been retrofitted
  through the popular Green Open Homes programme.
- Speak with homeowners who have made energy-saving improvements and
  hear about their experiences.
- Meet trusted suppliers and industry professionals.
- Watch installer talks, case studies and product demonstrations
  showcasing the latest energy-efficient technologies.
- Discover practical ways to reduce your energy bills while improving
  comfort and creating a healthier home.
- Enjoy free refreshments throughout the event.

Exhibitors and product demonstrations: To be confirmed.

**About the organisers**

This event is hosted by Retrofit West and funded by the West of
England Mayoral Combined Authority.

Retrofit West supports homeowners across the West of England to
improve the energy efficiency of their homes through high-quality
retrofit. Their mission is to help accelerate the transition to
low-carbon housing, reducing carbon emissions while creating warmer,
healthier homes, lowering energy costs and supporting local jobs and
skills.

address.street: Great Western Dockyard, Gas Ferry Road

events.raw:
17 October 2026

Calm Sessions have been designed for anyone who benefits from visiting Bristol Dockyards
when there is a reduced sensory environment – particularly neurodivergent people of all
ages.
events.summary: A reduced-sensory opening of the whole site, run for neurodivergent visitors and anyone else who needs it quieter.
events.description:
Calm Sensory Sessions have been designed for anyone who benefits from visiting at a time
when there is a calmer background sensory environment – particularly neurodivergent people
of all ages.

**What will the sessions include?** We understand that the sensory experience at SS Great
Britain can be challenging for some of our visitors. Where possible these calm sensory
sessions will include:

- Audio, visual, and smell effects will be turned off or reduced.
- Lighting levels will be adjusted.
- Capacity will be reduced.
- Dedicated sensory room.

These sessions will vary throughout the year with some happening on weekends and some
during weekdays in school holidays. Some will be mornings and some afternoons.

**Upcoming dates:** Sunday 17th October 10am-5pm. Sunday 31st January 10am-5pm.

Visual and sensory guides are available to download: Visual Story, Visual Timetable,
Sensory Information Guide, Sounds & Smells Guide and Mannequin Map.

Now, for the very first time, he’s taking his unique brand of humour on tour across the UK , ready to meet the people who helped propel him to international fame.

With over 2 million followers on Instagram, more than 800,000 fans on TikTok, and 1+ billion views, Greipur has taken the internet by storm. His rise began with viral videos featuring his razor-sharp wit, perfectly deadpan delivery, and brutally honest observations on parenting, relationships, and life on a tiny island full of volcanoes, glaciers, and questionable weather choices.

Online he’s known simply as @greipjokes — a comic voice that travels far beyond Iceland. His material leaps from everyday quirks to cultural weirdness, with a twist of Icelandic charm. One moment he’s lecturing about elves, the next he’s dismantling Nordic stoicism — and audiences everywhere crack.

Fresh off his digital domination and a guest spot on the award-winning Comedy Roundtable podcast, Greipur now steps off the screen and onto real stages across the UK. Expect sharp storytelling, sneaky sarcasm, and a mischievously charming presence that’s even better in person.

**From volcanoes and glaciers… to audiences across the UK. Greipur Hjaltason — live, unfiltered, and funnier than ever.**

Wednesday 21st October 2026 19:00 at Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries

On video games, politics and the battle for global influence

£28 includes a copy of the book / £6
events.summary: George E. Osborn, editor of the Video Games Industry Memo, on *Power Play* — how states, money and political movements are using video-game communities as a battleground for influence. Panel with Dr Richard Cole (Bristol Digital Game Lab) and Dr Tomas Rawlings (Bristol Games Hub, Sumo Digital), in partnership with both.
events.description:
**In partnership with Bristol Games Hub and Bristol Digital Game Lab.**

Video games are the world's largest entertainment medium. They are played by billions of people of all ages every year, generating hundreds of billions of dollars in revenue.

But they are more than an entertainment product. They connect people across the globe, creating digital third places where people talk, share ideas and build identities, fostering diverse communities capable of dominating the digital discourse now shaping our reality.

While democracies continue to underestimate the potential for influence in this space, others have seized the opportunity to control, co-opt or collaborate with video game communities to wield the power of these vast information ecosystems.

Saudi Arabia is spending tens of billions of dollars acquiring video games businesses to wash its reputation. Russia has funded video game development to help spread disinformation about the war in Ukraine. Steve Bannon utilised tactics deployed by online video game communities to propel Donald Trump into the White House, and Charlie Kirk's alleged assassin even carved video game references into his bullets.

Supported by the insights of politicians, academics and industry experts, Power Play is the vital guide for understanding this new political frontier, highlighting what democracies must do to protect and harness the immense power of play before the essential battle for digital influence is lost for good.

We're excited to welcome **George Osborn** to Bristol, to discuss _Power Play._

**George E. Osborn** is the Editor of the _Video Games Industry Memo_ newsletter, and the founder of _Half-Space Consulting_, a strategic consultancy which helps NGOs, regulators, governments and businesses to understand the video game sector.

He will be in conversation with **Dr Richard Cole**, Senior Lecturer in Digital Futures at the University of Bristol, and co-founder of the _Bristol Digital Game Lab_. Also on the panel, **Dr Tomas Rawlings**, who is the co-founder and director of the _Bristol Game Hub_, and VP at _Sumo Digital_.

events.raw:
**Highlights Tour** — Thu 22 Oct | 17:30 – 18:00.

Join one of Bristol Cathedral's dedicated tour guides as they take you on a journey spanning 900 years of history, heritage, and architecture at the extraordinary Bristol Cathedral! From the tale of St Jordan of Bristol (yes, Bristol has a saint!) through to the ordination of the first women priests in 1994, joining a Bristol Cathedral Highlights Tour is the best and most fascinating way to get to know one of the grandest buildings in the city of Bristol!

The tours last between 45-60 minutes, and your guide will meet you inside the Cathedral at the Welcome Area.

_The entrance to Bristol Cathedral is level access. However, some areas of the Cathedral included in the highlights tours involve uneven floors and steps, particularly when accessing the Norman Chapter House. Sensible footwear is advised. If you have any accessibility requests or concerns and you would like to go on a highlights tour please contact Bristol Cathedral at visitor.experience@bristol-cathedral.co.uk before booking your tickets._

**Cream Tea Add-On.** A freshly baked scone with clotted cream and jam, served with a pot of tea by Pinkmans Café in our cloister. The perfect way to round off your tour.

events.raw: **Event 22/10: Phil Melanson introduces Florenzer** — From £6.00.
events.summary: Phil Melanson on his debut Florenzer, a queer historical novel set in fifteenth-century Florence.
events.description:
**Join us for a fantastic evening with Phil Melanson to discuss his brilliant debut, *Florenzer:* a queer, historical novel that paints a richly imagined portrait of a city that paints over its own decay; where an untested artist, not yet marked by greatness, will dare to follow his most unholy desires.**

**Date:**
Thursday 22nd of October

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 19:00. Finish approx 20:00.

**Tickets:**
£6 ticket only
£14.99 ticket with *Florenzer* (paperback)

You don't need to bring your ticket with you, we will have a list of names on the door. Books will be available to buy on the night.

**ABOUT THE BOOK**

***Florenzer***

*THE DAZZLING NEW HISTORICAL FICTION NOVEL FOR FANS OF THE SONG OF ACHILLES AND MARRIAGE PORTRAIT.*

15th-century Florence: where the river runs red with slaughterhouse blood and bronze statues glow in every square. Into its fold comes a young Leonardo da Vinci. Wayward and dreamy, he is different from the other artists' apprentices, drawn to what passes behind veils of steam in the baths and along the moonlit banks of the Arno.

Such habits have long belonged to Florence, but they carry risk in a city where anonymous accusations slipped into letterboxes destroy reputations overnight. Alongside Leonardo, two men pursue their own forms of immortality: Francesco Salviati, a priest willing to endure any degradation in the name of salvation, and Lorenzo de' Medici, heir to a great banking fortune, for whom wealth proves a shifting, uncertain thing.

Weaving together these three lives, *Florenzer* is a sensuous and richly imagined portrait of a city that paints over its own decay; where an untested artist, not yet marked by greatness, will dare to follow his most unholy desires.

*'The rift between Rome and Florence brings Melanson's three characters together in a bloody, vivid climax. All three characters are superbly drawn and Renaissance Florence leaps from the page...A stunning debut.' - The Times*

*'A captivating portrait of an all-too-human genius - subtle, erudite and exquisitely sexy.' - James Cahill, author of The Violet Hour*

*'Florenzer is a heady, intoxicating debut that examines the meaning of art in a time of turmoil. Melanson draws subtle, intimate portraits of his three protagonists, each of them caught between the worldly and the divine. Tortured Leonardo, ambitious Lorenzo and fanatical Salviati: the lives of these men intersect in surprising and sometimes bloody ways in the cutthroat world of Renaissance Italy. Told in rich, vivid prose, passion and desire permeate every page.' - Danielle Giles, author of Mere*

*'Introduces us to a teenage Leonardo still struggling to find himself amid the roiling artistic and political atmosphere of late-15th-century Florence... For a young man sexually attracted to other young men, this can be particularly dangerous...Yet his work may be his salvation.' - New York Times Book Review*

*'Impressively ambitious. . . An enjoyably sticky web of intrigue is spun, with much gossiping, bribing and backstabbing, and much shifting of allegiance between the great centres of power on the peninsula.' - TLS*

***ABOUT THE AUTHOR***

**Phil Melanson** is the author of the queer historical novel *Florenzer*, which was a National Bestseller, long-listed for the Centre for Fiction’s First Novel Prize, and an Allstora “(Very) Gay Book Club” Selection. He is a graduate of NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts and the University of Warwick, and in another life was a digital marketer for Hollywood film studios, working on campaigns for movies such as *Little Women, Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again *and* Once Upon on a Time… in Hollywood*. He teaches with Boston University in London, where he lives with his husband.

events.title: Nao-Cola Yamazaki & Polly Barton: Don’t Laugh At Other People’s Sex Lives

price.text: £8.00 – £12.00 (ticket only £8; ticket + copy of Don't Laugh At Other People's Sex Lives £12)

events.raw:
**Nao-Cola Yamazaki & Polly Barton: Don’t Laugh At Other People’s Sex Lives**

Friday 23rd October 2026, 6:30 pm

£8.00 – £12.00
events.summary: Japanese novelist Nao-Cola Yamazaki and their translator Polly Barton (*Butter*, *Fifty Sounds*) discuss the first English edition of *Don't Laugh At Other People's Sex Lives*, the Bungei Prize-winning 2004 novella of an art student's affair with his older tutor. Presented with the Japan Foundation.
events.description:
_Storysmith, 236 North Street, Bristol, BS3 1JD ([click here for a map](https://maps.app.goo.gl/9N9dxXfnwxac83FY7))_

We are delighted to be hosting a conversation between multi-award-winning author **Nao-Cola Yamazaki** and literary translator **Polly Barton**! They will be joining us in person to discuss Polly’s translation of Nao-Cola’s novella **Don’t Laugh At Other People’s Sex Lives**.

First published in Japan in 2004, it’s the book that launched Yamazaki’s career, earning them the 41st Bungei Prize and a movie adaptation. It’s now finally available in this deft English translation, and we can’t wait to hear more about the process of bringing it to new readers after all these years.

_**Pre-order your copy of Don’t Laugh At Other People’s Sex Lives** (rrp £9.99)  for a special discounted price with your ticket, then collect on the night!_

**This event is presented in collaboration with the Japan Foundation.**

**About Nao-Cola Yamazaki**

**Nao-Cola Yamazaki (山崎 ナオコーラ)** is a Japanese writer. They pride themselves on writing ‘things no one else can say in words anyone can understand’. They have won the Bungei Prize and the Shimase Award for Love Stories and been nominated multiple times for the Akutagawa Prize. Their first title to be translated into English was FRIENDSHIP FOR GROWN-UPS, a chapbook published by Stranger Press in 2017 and similarly translated by the acclaimed Polly Barton. The Japan Times praised Yamazaki’s ‘skill in evoking the ambiguity of contemporary life’, and called the collection ‘a small book that says a lot about the way we live today’. Their debut novel DON’T LAUGH AT OTHER PEOPLE’S SEX LIVES and their prize-winning BEAUTIFUL DISTANCE published this spring with Daunt Books in the UK, and is set to publish in the US with SJP Lit this September.

_Photo credit: Bungeishunju Ltd_

**About Polly Barton**

**Polly Barton** is a writer and literary translator from the Japanese. Her translations include _Butter_ by Asako Yuzuki, _Hunchback_ by Saou Ichikawa, _Where the Wild Ladies Are_ by Aoko Matsuda and _There’s No Such Thing as an Easy Job_ by Kikuko Tsumura. She has published two works of non-fiction, _Fifty Sounds_, for which she won the 2019 Fitzcarraldo Editions Essay Prize, and _Porn: An Oral History_. Her debut novel, _What Am I, A Deer?,_ was published in 2026.

_Photo credit: Garry Loughlin_

**About Don’t Laugh At Other People’s Sex Lives**

**A love story that feels both new and achingly true, capturing the intensity, uncertainties and intimacy of falling for someone.**

Art student Isogai first models for one of his tutors, the much older Yuri, then begins a passionate affair with her. As he gets to know her better, he struggles to understand his own emotions and his place in the world, just as he yearns to be closer to her and for her to share more of herself with him.

_Don’t Laugh at Other People’s Sex Lives_ was a smash-hit in Japan, winning the prestigious Bungei Prize, and selling over 250,000 copies. A touching portrait of late adolescence, with Isogai captured with exasperation, humour and tenderness, it is also, and above all else, an exploration of the exhilarating and destabilising experience of a love that defies prediction or explanation.

‘Razor-sharp emotional intelligence beneath a prose style that is as refreshing, as, well, a Diet Coke on a hot summer’s day . . . Pack[s] a devastatingly emotional wallop.’ **_Crack Magazine_**

‘A story full of nostalgia and beauty and hope. First love is perfectly imperfect, and Yamazaki renders it here with all the charm and respect that it deserves.’ **Sarah Jessica Parker**** **

‘Slyly transgressive, singularly weird – a happy/sad confection of innocence to unsettling experience, and big feelings that go almost totally unsaid. Reminded me of Francoise Sagan’s _Bonjour Tristesse _mixed with Bae Suah’s _Nowhere to Be Found_.’ **Sharlene Teo**** **

‘A strange and beguiling love affair, one rich in all the distances and intimacies that pull new lovers together. I loved it. I haven’t devoured something like that in a long time.’ **Naomi Wood**

#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our weekly flagship comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online

## Stand Up For The Weekend with Matt Stellingwerf featuring Milo Edwards plus compere Tom Glover

#### Headliner: MATT STELLINGWERF

Hamilton-Born New Zealander and Wangnui-raised farmer’s son, trained criminologist and stand up comedian…Matt Stellingwerf is a man of contradictions.

He expertly brings these contradictions to the stage with his typical low-key style and confidence finding the humour in topics as diverse as love, politics and a crazy interview he once conducted with a serial killer in Death Row!

Highly regarded by his peers, Matt Stellingwerf has won four NZ Comedy Guild Awards, including Best Newcomer. He is now UK based and respected nationwide by promoters and comedy venues.

A renowned MC and compere, Matt is a 3-time nominee for Best MC in New Zealand. Matt was a 2015 and 2016 nominee for the prestigious Billy T Award.

When this erudite satire-superstar gets onto the stage, the acceleration from zero to a hundred jokes is measured in seconds. Matt Stellingwerf’s deftly crafted jokes display a man full of seriously good comedic talent.

#### “*Stellingwerf’s comedy is intelligent, clever and thoroughly researched..all of the while being really likeable*” Libel

#### “…*an intellectual ‘Fonze’..extremely laid back and relaxed with the audience, seamlessly having banter and keeping his cool*” Keeping Up With NZ

Concorde After-Hours Tour: Mach One — 24 October 2026 | arrive by 4pm for 4:30pm start

Hear about what it was like to fly faster than the speed of sound at 60,000 ft on a
technical tour of Concorde Alpha Foxtrot by former employees of BAC Filton & Weybridge,
as well as former Concorde at Filton guides.
events.summary: Two hours with Concorde after closing, in three rotating groups — under the aircraft, inside the forward cabin and flight deck, then the simulator. Thirty-three places only.
events.description:
Hear about what it was like to fly faster than the speed of sound at 60,000 ft on a
technical tour of Concorde Alpha Foxtrot by former employees of BAC Filton & Weybridge, as
well as former Concorde at Filton guides. Perfect for the Concorde aficionado or those who
want to know more about the iconic supersonic passenger jet.

Enjoy a thrilling two-hour journey, beginning with a refreshing welcome drink upon
arrival. You will be divided into groups each rotating through three sections:

- **Underneath Concorde:** Discover the technical feats of the aircraft, highlighting its
  engineering innovations.
- **Onboard Concorde:** Explore the forward cabin and the flight deck, with a unique photo
  opportunity.
- **Concorde Flight Deck Simulator:** Experience the mock flight deck and delve into
  Concorde’s history through the exhibition.

To commemorate this unforgettable adventure, each guest will receive a personalised
certificate signed by a Concorde VIP. There are just 33 spaces for the exclusive tour.

events.description:
Step into history this Halloween at The Red Lodge for a week of stories and exploration!

This enchanting event will immerse you in the rich history of one of Bristol’s most
intriguing historical houses, where the past comes alive.

Peep into our tiny world spooky doors and spot the ghosts and ghouls that live behind
them, can you find them all? What Spooky stories do they tell? Let your creativity flow
and create your own story or poem inspired by our spooky creatures to take home with you.

As you wander through the dimly lit halls, you’ll encounter former residents who will
guide you on a journey through time, sharing tales of the lives and the history of the
house. You can find out all about:

- Sir John Young, an Elizabethan gentleman, the first owner of the Red Lodge and host to
  Queen Elizabeth I
- Annie Woolham, a young Victorian girl and early resident of the Red Lodge Reform School
- Mary Henley, a Georgian lady who modernised the Red Lodge and turned it into a home

**What’s on:** story time with our volunteers during the year of reading; a creative
activity — make a God's Eye to ward off unfriendly spirits, a spooky paper pal, or
decorations to take home; spooky face and body painting; historical costume to dress up
in; and a drink and a tasty treat in our Tudor Knot garden.

**Happening on:** Saturday 24 October, Sunday 25 October, Thursday 29 October, Friday 30
October, Saturday 31 October, Sunday 1 November.

**Book tickets.** Entry tickets are £5 per person (except children under 4). Activities are
included in entry price. Discounted family group tickets available.

events.description:
_Storysmith, 236 North Street, Bristol, BS3 1JD_

Join us in the shop for a very special book signing with the one and only **Oliver Jeffers**!

Oliver will be joining us to celebrate not only the release of his new picture book **A Day Off School** (written by Oliver and illustrated by Kevin Waldron), but also the new paperback edition of his classic **There’s a Ghost in This House**.

**You’ll get a free art print with every purchase of either of those two books**, and we’ll also have an array of Oliver’s incredible backlist on sale too, ready for him to sign just for you.

Here’s the lowdown on how it’ll work on the day:

- _You must purchase a £5 ticket to attend: this can be redeemed against any Oliver Jeffers book on the day (we’ll have a large selection of his books available as well as the new ones!)_

- _One ticket required per group (up to 5 people)_

- _The signing will begin at 3:30pm and tickets are limited to ensure everyone will have time to get their books signed, but please be aware that you will have to queue!_

**About Oliver Jeffers**

Oliver Jeffers’ career in children’s books began with his highly acclaimed debut, How to Catch a Star, first published in 2004. Since then, he has become a worldwide phenomenon and a genre-busting creative force in the world of children’s books with book translations in forty-nine languages. Oliver has exhibited in museums and galleries such as the Brooklyn Museum in New York, the National Portrait Gallery in London and the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston. In 2022 Oliver received a Member of the Order of the British Empire Award (MBE) for his Services in Art and in 2026 Oliver joined Smartphone Free Childhood as their ambassador.

_Photo credit: Caroline Tompkins_

**About A Day Off School**

A hilarious story full of action and adventure from two highly regarded, award-winning picture book creators.

When Herbie has the sniffles, he stays home from school. It’s exciting to have time to play Space Blasters and watch cartoons.

But, by lunchtime, he starts to wonder what he might be missing at school. What if there’s an extra playtime, a dog on the loose… or even A PIRATE INVASION?

Is Herbie missing out on all the action? A hilarious, action-packed story from the globally bestselling creator of Lost and Found and Here We Are, Oliver Jeffers, and the award-winning illustrator of Chocolate Cake, Kevin Waldron.

**About There’s a Ghost in This House**

_“Hello, come in. Maybe you can help me?”_

A young girl lives in a haunted house, but has never seen a ghost. Are they white with holes for eyes? Are they hard to see? She’d love to know!

Step inside and join in an entertaining ghost hunt, from behind the sofa, right up to the attic. With lots of friendly ghost surprises and incredible mixed media illustrations, this unique and funny book will entertain young readers over and over again!

A perfect Halloween picture book from the New York Times bestselling creator of Here We Are. Oliver Jeffers has sold more than 18 million books worldwide, in 49 languages!

_‘Hauntingly adorable’_ Guardian

_‘Another absolute winner from this inventive author’_ Daily Mail

_‘Absolutely brilliant’_ BookTrust

_‘Thrilling’_ Big Issue

[Accessibility information can be found here.](https://storysmithbooks.com/access/)
