events.summary: A three-day half-term project for 14-17 year olds building a creative tool to get people talking about smartphones and digital life, with an option to carry on afterwards as a paid peer researcher.
events.description:
Who gets to decide what's good or bad about smartphones? Join a team of
young co-creators to explore one of the biggest debates facing your
generation. Work with artists and researchers to invent a fun, creative
tool that gets people talking about digital life and puts young
people's ideas at the centre of the conversation. After October half
term, you'll have the opportunity to continue with the project over the
until January, as a paid peer researcher, testing your tool with young
people across Bristol.

**Dates:** Tuesday 27 - Thursday 29 October 2026, 10am-3pm.
**Location:** KWMC, Leinster Avenue, South Bristol, BS4 1NL
**For ages 14-17**

These sessions are FREE but lunch is not provided. If food security is
a challenge for your family, please do write to us and we can provide
support with lunch for families who need it.

Our programmes are for young people living or studying in BS4, BS3 5,
BS13 & BS14. Places are limited and will be allocated based on
eligibility and funding priorities.

events.raw:
**WOOFYT: Explore the Science of Music** — Wed 28 Oct | 9:30 – 15:30.

Build, Play and Discover: The Science of the Organ. _Featuring WOOFYT._

Ever wondered how an organ creates its powerful sound? Join us for a hands-on family experience exploring the science, technology and creativity behind one of the world's most remarkable musical instruments. Through WOOFYT, the Wooden One-Octave Organ for Young Technologists, children and families can investigate how organ pipes work, discover the mechanics behind music, and experiment with sound for themselves.

Alongside the workshop, families can also enjoy **Crafty Cathedral**, with free drop-in musical arts and crafts activities running throughout the morning. No booking is needed for the craft activities.

**Workshop sessions (75 minutes):** 9.30am, 10.50am, 1.00pm, 2.20pm. Workshop places are free but must be booked in advance.

Part of **The Grand Organ Festival**, celebrating the return of Bristol Cathedral's organ following its major restoration. [Discover the full programme of events.](https://bristol-cathedral.co.uk/whats-on/the-grand-organ-festival/)
events.summary: Children build and play a wooden one-octave organ to find out how pipes make sound, in free 75-minute sessions through the day, booked in advance, with drop-in musical crafts running alongside all morning. Part of the Grand Organ Festival.

events.description:
**WOODWORKING HAND TOOL SHARPENING AND SET UP**

On this one day course you will learn how to sharpen and maintain
your chisels, planes and scrapers so that they are effective and are
a pleasure to use. We will cover all the essential sharpening know
how and then give you the opportunity to put it into practice under
our guidance.

You will also learn how to set hand planes and make fine adjustments
to get the best performance from them. Gain the confidence to get
your home workshop chisels and planes into shape!

**LEARN ABOUT:**

- Angles, bevels and shapes
- Sharpening stones and other abrasives
- Honing fluids
- Freehand sharpening and honing guides
- How to create a turned edge
- Hand plane tuning and set up

**COURSE LENGTH & TIMES:** 1 Day (Wednesday 10.30am – 3.30pm)

**SKILL LEVEL:** Suitable for everyone

**COURSE FEE:** £65.00

**INCLUDED IN THE COURSE FEE:** All materials, tutoring and tool use
– there are no additional costs.

Please bring along a woodwork chisel and/or plane from home to
practice on. If you don't have any to bring, just let us know and we
will make sure there is something available in the workshop for you to
use.

**CANCELLATION SPACES:** We run waiting lists for cancellation spaces
on all of our fully booked courses – to be added to a waiting list
please email hello@themakershed.co.uk.

**in the dark: HUSH** — Thu 29 Oct | 21:00 – 22:30. **Doors open: 8.30pm. Performance begins: 9pm.**

Bristol Cathedral will host **in the dark: HUSH**, an immersive music experience that reimagines how live performance is heard and experienced.

Rather than performing from a stage, musicians move through and around the audience, creating an evolving soundscape that surrounds listeners throughout the performance. The result is a distinctive musical experience where sound, space and movement combine in unexpected ways.

Tickets are available from the event organisers. _Please note: this event is presented by an external organiser and hosted at Bristol Cathedral._
events.summary: A late-evening performance in which the musicians move through the darkened cathedral around the audience rather than playing from a stage. Doors at half past eight; tickets through the organiser.

events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend with Chloe Petts & Guests Featuring Jonny Pelham plus compere Jack Campbell

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available.

#### Headliner: CHLOE PETTS

Chloe Petts is one of the sharpest, funniest voices on the UK comedy circuit. Armed with razor-sharp observations, effortless charisma and an infectious warmth, they transform everyday life into brilliantly crafted stand-up. Whether they’re dissecting sport, politics, relationships or the glorious absurdities of modern Britain, Chloe’s quick wit and playful confidence keep audiences hooked from start to finish. A regular on television, radio and some of the country’s biggest comedy stages, they’ve earned acclaim for their intelligent, fearless and gloriously entertaining performances. Smart, energetic and laugh-out-loud funny, Chloe Petts is a comedian not to be missed.

Chloe Pett’s most recent show Big Naturals premiered at the Edinburgh Fringe in August 2025, and achieved a sell out run, with multiple sold out extra shows being added across the month. Chloe’s previous show, How You See Me, How You Don’t, came to the Fringe in 2024. The show was lauded with multiple four- and five-star reviews, with the Evening Standard telling audiences “Don’t mess with Petts and don’t miss [them] either”.

On television and radio, Chloe has appeared on Have I Got News For You (BBC 1) three times across 2024 and 2025, as well as Live at the Apollo (BBC) in 2025 and Bake Off: An Extra Slice (Channel 4), and hosted their own segment every Saturday morning on Sky Sports News.

#### “*Smart, insightful, hilarious, and completely relatable.*” Diva Magazine

#### “*One of the most compelling young comics*” The Guardian

#### “*Clearly a rising star whose name will soon be in lights*” London Evening Standard

#### “*World-class stand-up skills… drenched in laughs and warmth. We must never take Chloe Petts for granted.*” The Scotsman

Discover Chloe Petts here: [https://www.chloepetts.org/](https://www.chloepetts.org/)

events.description:
Yoga Foundations Workshop — Breath, Meditation, Posture & Balance

This Yoga Foundations workshop offers time and space to explore yoga
from the ground up.

We'll work with the four core parts of yoga — Breath, Meditation,
Asana (postures) and basic Philosophy — with a particular focus on
standing postures and balance, including Warrior I, II, III & IV, and
a small number of balance poses.

We'll take our time and work carefully, starting with the basics:

- where to place your feet
- how to breathe within the postures
- how the body organises itself to stand and balance

Alongside the physical learning, we'll explore the essence of these
postures — "what do you stand up for?" "What do you show up for?"

With 2.5 hours together (10:00–12:30), there is space to explore,
explain, rest & repeat – so learning has time to settle and
integrate.

The workshop finishes with Chinese tea for contemplation and light
snacks, offering a gentle close to the morning.

**Make a day of it?** Stay on site for brunch at the excellent
Cibomatto Italian Canteen, book in advance for the sauna and cold
plunge, or head out for a walk in the beautiful Nightingale Valley or
along the river towards Crews Hole.

**Why St Anne's House?**

- Free on-site parking (including accessible spaces)
- Accessible ground-floor Mill Room with step-free access
- Bristol Community Sauna & Cold Plunge on site for post-class
  relaxation
- A vibrant community hub with creative studios, café, and local
  projects

**What to Bring** — Wear comfortable clothes you can move in. Bring
your own yoga mat and props if you have them, plus a blanket and
pillow for relaxation. Mats are available to borrow if needed.

events.raw:
Bristol's Biggest Ever Silent Disco – Halloween Special at Bristol Aquarium & We The
Curious! 2 Museums – 1 Ticket. Saturday 31st October, 7pm – 11pm. Over 18s.

We’re bringing you Bristol’s biggest silent disco ever across two of the city’s most
iconic venues; Bristol Aquarium and We The Curious. Dive into the abyss with non-stop
floor filling-bangers from the 80s, 90s, and 00s across several channels including indie
anthems hosted by Propaganda!

Here’s the rundown:

- **Bristol Aquarium:** Navigate through chilling underwater realms and vibrant jungles
  adorned with cutting-edge Halloween vibes until 9pm. Please note that the last entrance
  to the aquarium display will be at 8.45pm to ensure that everyone gather in the main
  area no later than 9pm to experience one of Bristol’s most epic Halloween Silent Discos
  until 11pm.
- **We The Curious:** Step into the shadow of Bristol’s most chilling science experience
  and enjoy interactive exhibits whilst dancing to killer tunes all the way until 11pm!

This exclusive event is promoted by Iconic Silent Discos, a collaboration between the UK’s
biggest Silent Disco provider, Silent Disco King, and Propaganda.
events.summary: One ticket, two Halloween dancefloors — the aquarium until 9pm, then We The Curious until 11pm, with 80s, 90s and 00s channels plus an indie channel from Propaganda. Over 18s.

events.raw:
**All Souls' Requiem** — Mon 2 Nov | 18:00 – 19:30.

Join us for a gentle and reflective service as we remember those we love who have died.

Through music, readings, prayers and hymns, we will give thanks for the lives of those we hold in our hearts and pray for all who grieve. Whether your loss is recent or many years ago, you are warmly invited to come and spend time in remembrance and reflection.

During the service, there will be an opportunity to light a candle in memory of a loved one and to join with others in a shared act of hope and remembrance. Everyone is welcome.
events.summary: The cathedral's All Souls' evening service of remembrance, sung as a requiem, with a chance to light a candle for someone who has died. Open to anyone; no price is printed.

events.description:
Energetic, loud and funny, Nathan Macintosh is a comedian and writer originally from Halifax, Nova Scotia now living in New York.

Most recently performing for his third time on **The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon **on NBC, Nathan has also appeared on **The Late Show With Stephen Colbert** on CBS, **Conan** on TBS, and multiple **Just For LaughsGalas**.

His debut album ‘I Wasn’t Talking’ was featured in Ex!aim Magazine’s ‘Top Ten Hilariously Good Comedy Moments’ and his special, ‘Money Never Wakes’, was reviewed highly and named ‘Best Youtube Special of 2023’ by The New York Times. His newest special, ‘Down With Tech’, has been reviewed by Vulture and named one of the ‘5 Stand Up Specials You Should Definitely Watch’ by them.

Nathan also wrote and starred in ‘Trapped’, which is on Bell Fibe, was reviewed by The Globe And Mail and has two seasons.

He can be heard regularly on Sirius Satellite Radio and CBC’s radios ‘The Debaters’.

Read more about Natan Macintosh here: [Nathan Macintosh](https://nathanmacintosh.com/)

#### “*Convulse with laughter*…” – The New York Times

#### “*Macintosh’s stage presence is explosive*…” – Exc!aim

**ABOUT *Dream Count***

**THE INSTANT SUNDAY TIMES NO.1 BESTSELLER; LONGLISTED FOR THE WOMEN'S PRIZE FOR FICTION**

*'Magnificent' SUNDAY TIMES*

*‘Extraordinary’ NEW STATESMAN*

*'The return of a literary titan' TELEGRAPH*

A searing, exquisite novel by the bestselling and award-winning author of Americanah and We Should All Be Feminists – the story of four women and their loves, longings and desires.

Chiamaka is a Nigerian travel writer living in America. Alone in the midst of the pandemic, she recalls her past lovers and grapples with her choices and regrets. Zikora, her best friend, has been successful at everything until – betrayed and brokenhearted – she must turn to the person she thought she needed least. Chiamaka’s bold, outspoken cousin Omelogor is a financial powerhouse in Nigeria who begins to question how well she knows herself. And Kadiatou, Chiamaka’s housekeeper, is proudly raising her daughter in America – but faces an unthinkable hardship that threatens all she has worked to achieve.

Dream Count is Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie’s searing, unforgettable story of these four women – a sparkling, transcendent novel that takes up the very nature of love itself.

**PROGRAMME** to include: **Mozart** – Overture to The Marriage of Figaro; **Vaughan Williams** – The Lark Ascending; **Mozart** – Flute Quartet in D; **Vivaldi** – The Four Seasons.

Experience breathtaking music by some of classical music's greatest composers, performed by some of the country's finest classical musicians, all presented in stunning candlelight.

At the heart of the concert is Antonio Vivaldi's The Four Seasons, the most recorded work in classical music and a defining showpiece for solo violin. Alongside this, Vaughan Williams' _The Lark Ascending_, composed on the eve of the First World War, offers a more reflective perspective.

#### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: GARRETT MILLERICK

Garrett Millerick is an acclaimed stand up comedian, writer and director. His unique and versatile style has led to him being in great demand on the alternative and club circuits both in the UK and internationally.

Garrett is known for his grumpy, grouchy persona who is fed up with the pretenses of the modern world, aiming his criticism at everything from the fraudulent activity of the recycling industry to growing depression inflicted by miserablist, oversharing celebrities. His shouty, ironic delivery keeps you on the edge of your seat and the crushing punchlines can leave you exhilarated as he rages against yet more societal hypocrisies.

#### “*A virtuoso display of unforgivingly grumpy stand up delivered with fire in his soul*” Chortle

#### “*Stand up with an insolent twist*” The Sunday Times

#### “*Wonderfully funny*” The Times

#### “*Watching him let rip for one hour at an arts festival is a unique joy*.” The List

Discover Garrett Millerick here: [https://www.garrettmillerick.com/](https://www.garrettmillerick.com/)

events.title: Remembrance Sunday
events.raw:
**Remembrance Sunday** — Sun 8 Nov | 9:30 – 10:30. Free.

Join us at Bristol Cathedral this Remembrance Sunday as we gather to remember and give thanks for all those who have served in the Armed Forces, and especially those who gave their lives in war and conflict.

Our Sung Eucharist offers an opportunity to come together in prayer, reflection and remembrance. Through music, scripture, hymns and silence, we will honour the courage, sacrifice and service of generations past, while holding in our hearts all those affected by conflict today.

Following the service, we join people from across Bristol at the Cenotaph for the Act of Remembrance and the two-minute silence, standing together to honour those who have served our nation. **Everyone is welcome.**
events.summary: The cathedral's Remembrance Sunday sung Eucharist, at 9:30 rather than the usual 10:00, after which the congregation joins the city at the Cenotaph for the Act of Remembrance and the two-minute silence. Free, everyone welcome.

events.raw:
**Meet Cody Dahler!**

Monday 9th November 2026 13:00 - 15:00 at Waterstones, Bristol - Galleries

Want to stop feeling like a thicky thicky dumb dumb in front of all your mates?

No booking required / Books will be available to purchase at the event
events.summary: Comedian, satirist and podcaster Cody Dahler signs copies of *The State of This!*, his comic explainer of British politics — Reform, Brexit, the Lords, the rivers, the lettuce. A two-hour afternoon signing, no booking required; books on sale on the day.
events.description:
We are delighted to welcome writer and comedian Cody Dahler to Deansgate, signing copies of his hilarious yet informative book, The State of This!

Want to stop feeling like a thicky thicky dumb dumb in front of all your mates?

Award‑winning comedian, satirist, and political writer **Cody Dahler** launches his blisteringly funny, sharply researched and pointedly accessible deep‑dive book, The State of This! at a time when UK politics feels more like a never‑ending circus of culture wars, personality clashes and questionable decision‑making. Cody uses his signature wit and razor‑sharp commentary to tackle the questions that leave people baffled, exhausted or simply shouting at the telly: Why are people voting for Reform UK? Why did we Brexit? What even is the House of Lords? Why are our rivers full of crap? Are we at risk of becoming like the US? Why do our Prime Ministers keep changing? And why, exactly, did outliving a lettuce become the benchmark for political longevity?

The State of This! transforms complex political issues into something readers can understand and laugh about. It is the perfect antidote to the confusion, frustration and existential dread generated by the state of Britain today.

CODY DAHLER is an award-winning comedy creator, writer, and podcaster whose sharp wit and unique voice have made him one of the most exciting talents emerging from the UK comedy scene. Known for blending clever satire with authentic human observation, Cody has built a reputation for delivering laughs and facts among his dedicated following of over 2 million across all platforms.

In addition to his writing credits, Cody is the creator and host of The Truth (In My Opinion) podcast. Whether he's connecting with audiences over socials, writing for iconic UK comedy shows, or performing live, Cody continues to push boundaries with work that's smart, surprising and undeniably funny marking him out as a creative force in contemporary comedy.

**G4 Christmas** — Thu 12 Nov | 19:30 – 21:30.

Gather to celebrate the most wonderful time of the year as G4 bring glad tidings of great joy this festive season, with the return of their 'G4 Christmas' tour in the most awe-inspiring cathedrals, priories, minsters, halls and abbeys across the UK.

events.venueName: Multiple venues across Bristol city centre
events.raw:
**Festival of Economics** @ City centre — Fri, 13 Nov — Fri, 20 Nov

Lecture/Talk · Debate

The 15th edition of the Festival of Economics arrives at a time when artificial intelligence, geopolitical instability and rising costs of living have shifted the global economic mood away from hope a…
events.summary: The fifteenth Festival of Economics, a week of talks and debates with economists, policymakers and journalists at venues across the city centre, asking whether AI, instability and the cost of living are growing pains or the start of a dystopia. Full programme and tickets on the festival's own website; the University is a supporter.
events.description:
The 15th edition of the Festival of Economics arrives at a time when artificial intelligence, geopolitical instability and rising costs of living have shifted the global economic mood away from hope and toward cynicism.

This year, we will examine whether these are growing pains that are necessary to achieving resilience and a stronger future, or signs that we are quietly transitioning into a 'Brave New World'-style dystopia.

Join world-class economists, policymakers, journalists and thinkers in November to share your perspective on the state of today's economy, learn from and challenge the experts, and contribute towards a vision for renewed economic prosperity.

The Festival of Economics takes place 13-20 November 2026 at multiple venues across Bristol.

**Full programme and tickets are available at: [www.economicsfestival.co.uk](http://www.economicsfestival.co.uk/)**

Proudly supported by the University of Bristol.

Organiser: Festival of Economics, info@economicsfestival.co.uk.

**Comedy: Stand Up For The Weekend with Ali Woods & Guests**

14 November · 20:00 – 22:00 · From £12
events.summary: Comedian and podcaster Ali Woods headlines, on football, the environment and everything in between.
events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend with Ali Woods & Guests Featuring Harriet Dyer plus compere Adam Beardsmore

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: ALI WOODS

Ali Woods is a half-English, half-Scottish comedian, podcaster and content creator. Ali is a refreshing mix of the ‘every man’ and the ‘modern man’, whose sensitivity and genuine interest in men’s mental health gives him a great perspective on the modern ‘lad’ culture which often features in his comedy. Ali is that wonderful blend of comedy with a heart, speaking on topics such as football, the environment, and many social causes close to his heart.

His online comedy sketches under the tag @aliwoodsgigs have gained millions of views and likes, and featured on LadBible and Buzzfeed UK. In 2022, he supported Russell Kane and Axel Blake on tour and in 2024 supported Adam Kay.

In 2024, Ali starred on Comedy Central Live and Stand Up Sketch Show. He also had a third sold out Edinburgh run with his show ‘At the Moment’ he then embarked on his first ever solo tour across the UK and Ireland to sold-out audiences, including a date at Bristol’s Hen & Chicken.

#### “*Ali Woods is a simply brilliant storyteller*” Everything Theatre

#### “*In a world of wannabes, Woods is the real deal.*” London Evening Standard

Discover Ali Woods here: [https://www.aliwoodsgigs.com/](https://www.aliwoodsgigs.com/)

events.raw:
**Festival of Economics: Marshall Paley Lecture with Alan Manning ('Why Immigration Policy Is Hard: And How to Make It Better')** @ Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus — Tue, 17 Nov @ 6:30pm

Lecture/Talk

Join us for the 2026 Marshall Paley Lecture which will be delivered by Alan Manning. This lecture is based on the newly published book, Why Immigration Policy Is Hard.
events.summary: LSE labour economist and former Migration Advisory Committee chair Alan Manning gives the 2026 Marshall Paley Lecture on why immigration policy is so hard to get right, drawing on his new book, hosted by Bristol's Toman Barsbai. Part of the Festival of Economics; free, with registration opening in the autumn.
events.description:
Join us for the 2026 Marshall Paley Lecture which will be delivered by Alan Manning. This lecture is based on the newly published book, Why Immigration Policy Is Hard.

In this lecture Professor Manning examines why immigration policy is hard and why we make such a mess of it. This session will be hosted by Toman Barsbai (University of Bristol).

This year's Marshall Paley lecture is kindly sponsored by the School of Economics, University of Bristol.

Alan Manning is Professor of Economics at LSE and is director of the Centre for Economic Performance's labour programme. From 2009-2012 he was Head of the Economics Department at LSE; from 2004 to 2011 he was a member of the NHS Pay Review Body and from 2016-2020 the Chair of the Migration Advisory Committee.

Toman Barsbai is a Professor of Economics at the University of Bristol. His research focuses on the causes and consequences of international migration, with a particular emphasis on migrants and their countries of origin. His research has informed migration policies in the Philippines, and he is currently evaluating the use of income share agreements for international educational migration.

**Registration for this event will open in the autumn - visit the Festival of Economics [website](https://www.economicsfestival.co.uk) for updates.** Tickets will be free of charge.

events.title: Festival of Economics: The new economics of the left
events.raw:
**Festival of Economics: The new economics of the left** @ Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus — Wed, 18 Nov @ 6:30pm

Lecture/Talk

The election in 2024 of the first Labour government in a generation was followed by higher spending, increases in taxation and a loosening of fiscal rules. Workers rights were strengthened, parts of t…
events.summary: A Festival of Economics panel on whether the left has a coherent economic strategy after Labour's first years back in power — Eshe Nelson of the New York Times, Adrienne Buller, David Klemperer and former McDonnell adviser James Meadway. Tickets via the festival website.
events.description:
The election in 2024 of the first Labour government in a generation was followed by higher spending, increases in taxation and a loosening of fiscal rules. Workers rights were strengthened, parts of the rail system were nationalised and a state-owned energy company, GB Energy, created.

Despite this, the government has lost support on the left while the Greens have surged under the leadership of Zack Polanski. Politicians, commentators and thinktanks on the left have made proposals for how a social democratic government could go further on economic policy, despite the constraints imposed by high interest rates and public debt.

This panel brings together leading commentators to discuss whether a coherent economic strategy of the left is possible, the barriers to implementing such a strategy, and the likely economic consequences — for growth, living standards and inequality — of the choices the government has made and those it has yet to face.

**Tickets are now available via [the Festival of Economics website.](https://economicsfestival.co.uk/)**

**Speakers:**

- **Eshe Nelson (The New York Times)** — A business and economics reporter for The New York Times in London. Before joining The New York Times, she was a global economics and markets reporter for Quartz and a currency and bond markets reporter for Bloomberg News. In 2020, she completed the Knight-Bagehot Fellowship in Economics and Business Journalism at Columbia University.
- **Adrienne Buller (The BREAK-DOWN)** — The Founding Editor of The BREAK—DOWN, a new media initiative focused on the political economy of climate and ecological crisis. She is the author, with Mathew Lawrence, of Owning the Future (Verso, 2022) and The Value of a Whale (Manchester University Press, 2022), which won the 2024 Eric Zencey Prize in Ecological Economics. She is an Associate Fellow at Common Wealth.
- **David Klemperer (RENEWAL)** — Co-editor of RENEWAL: A Journal of Social Democracy, and a researcher within the Institute for Policy Research at the University of Bath. He specialises in political economy, the history of social democracy and constitutional reform, and has held previous research roles at the Constitution Society and Institute for Government (IfG).
- **James Meadway (Verdant Thinking)** — Director of Verdant Thinking, a progressive think tank. He was formerly a political advisor to Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell, and Chief Economist at the New Economics Foundation. He has taught in economics at SOAS, Cambridge, Sussex and City Universities, and has published widely on economic policy and theory in the New Statesman, Guardian, Jacobin, Tribune, and Novara.

Artwork by [Alys Jones Illustration](https://www.alysjonesillustration.com/).

events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend with Stephen Bailey & Guests Featuring Emma Coyne & Alex Mitchell plus compere Adam Beardsmore

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: STEPHEN BAILEY

The multi-award nominated Stephen Bailey is a comedian, presenter, actor and writer whose brand of gossipy humour has singled him out as one of the UK’s most sought-after talents, as well as boasting over 100k followers on Instagram after one of his videos was shared by none other than Melissa McCarthy.

Stephen’s quick-wit, playful sarcasm and enigmatic charm captivates audiences instantly. As well as being a prominent presence on the UK comedy circuit, he has also supported the biggest names in stand-up, including Micky Flanagan on his arena tour, Lucy Beaumont, Katherine Ryan, Jenny Eclair, Jason Manford, John Bishop and Sarah Millican.

Stephen is very much in demand and his numerous TV credits, let alone making a name for himself on Channel 5’s Celebs On The Farm, include hosting BBC’s Live at the Apollo and appearing on shows including Unbreakable, co-host on Date or Drop, alongside Amanda Holden, Would I Lie To You. Richard Osman’s House of Games, Celebrity Bridge of Lies and Celebrity Weakest Link, The Apprentice: You’re Fired, Between The Covers and Strictly: It Takes Two, and Pointless Celebrities. ​

#### “*A rising star*” The Sun

#### “*Bailey has a natural chemistry with his audience and this is where he truly comes into his own*” Broadway Baby

#### “*A natural talent for making audiences laugh*” Metro

21 November 2026, 2.00 PM - 21 November 2026, 5.00 PM

5th and 6th Floor of the Richmond Building, 105-115 Queens Road, Bristol BS8 1LN
events.summary: Film and Television graduates return to the Richmond Building to meet final-year and MA students over drinks, with a panel on career routes into the industry. Aimed at department alumni rather than the general public.
events.description:
Alumni of the Department of Film and Television are invited to their alumni networking event.

This event has been organised primarily for their current third-year undergraduate and MA students, providing them with the opportunity to connect with alumni working across the film and television industry, gain valuable insights, and explore potential career pathways.

Don't miss this fantastic opportunity to reconnect with fellow graduates, share your experiences since leaving the University of Bristol, and expand your professional network in an informal setting over drinks and nibbles.

The Department are looking for a small number of alumni to take part in a panel discussion during the event, sharing their career journeys, experiences of working in the industry, and advice for students preparing to enter the profession. If you are interested in joining the panel, they would love to hear from you.

**Booking.** To reserve your free place, [click here to sign up via the booking form](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=MH_ksn3NTkql2rGM8aQVG4VU87ed0hRFqqlrDhNr7j5UODk2SVZGWFNWOThGSVNUVllMVVBYV01LUC4u&route=shorturl).

events.summary: A new after-dark winter lights trail through the zoo grounds, running nightly through Advent. Timed entry from 4.30pm, animals off show, hot drinks and festive food along the route.
events.description:
Brand new for 2026, Wild Lights will bring to life the beautiful features of Bristol
Zoo Project through an awe-inspiring display of light and sound.

Just 30 minutes from central Bristol, with easy access from the M5, meet friends and
family for a festive experience you won't forget.

Every evening from 27 November to 23 December, the zoo will transform into an
immersive winter lights experience to delight all ages. Follow the trail through
towering trees and along winding pathways, uncovering new surprises at every turn.
With bright spectacles, interactive elements and plenty of surprises, Wild Lights
offers something for everyone.

As you explore, enjoy warming drinks and festive treats, including black forest hot
chocolates, burgers and sausage rolls (veggie and vegan options available). Every
ticket sold supports our vital conservation work in the UK and around the world.

**Know before you go.** Please pre-book to guarantee entry and arrive no more than 15
minutes prior to your booked timeslot. We are a natural, outdoor site — some paths
are uneven and can get muddy in winter. Wild Lights is a winter lights trail rather
than a normal zoo visit: for animal welfare reasons the animals will be off show and
away from the lights, so to see them please book a standard day ticket in addition.
The first Wild Lights entrance slot is at 4.30pm and the trail finishes 1.5 hours
after the end of the last time slot. The trail is fully accessible, with wheelchairs
and mobility scooters available to borrow if booked in advance.

Bristol Zoological Society members are entitled to 20% off tickets on the first three
nights only. (The page states this twice and disagrees with itself on the weekdays —
"Friday 27, Saturday 28, and Sunday 29 November" in the body, "Thursday 27, Friday 28,
and Saturday 29 November" in the FAQ. 27 November 2026 is a Friday.)

events.title: New Bristol Sinfonia
events.raw:
**New Bristol Sinfonia** — Sat 28 Nov | 19:30 – 21:30.

Join New Bristol Sinfonia and the organists of Bristol Cathedral for a spectacular evening celebrating the power, drama and beauty of music for organ and orchestra.

Part of The Grand Organ Festival, this concert marks an exciting moment in the life of the Cathedral's newly restored organ, bringing together musicians from across Bristol for a performance of some of the most inspiring works ever written for the instrument.

The evening opens with Widor's much-loved _Toccata_, the final piece played on the organ before its restoration began. Audiences will then hear works by Bach, Elgar and Poulenc before the concert culminates in Saint-Saëns' magnificent _Symphony No. 3_, often known simply as the "Organ Symphony".

Presented by New Bristol Sinfonia and Bristol Cathedral as part of **The Grand Organ Festival**. [Click here to find out more](https://bristol-cathedral.co.uk/whats-on/the-grand-organ-festival/)
events.summary: The Grand Organ Festival's orchestral centrepiece: New Bristol Sinfonia and the cathedral organists open with the Widor Toccata that was the last thing played before the restoration, then Bach, Elgar and Poulenc, ending with Saint-Saëns's Organ Symphony.

events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend with Pierre Novellie & Guests Featuring Sally-Ann Hayward plus compere Tom Glover

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: PIERRE NOVELLIE

Pierre Novellie is a stand-up comedian, writer, radio host and podcaster. He was co-host of The Frank Skinner Show on Absolute Radio, and TV appearances have included World’s Most Dangerous Roads (Dave), The Mash Report (BBC2), and Stand Up Central (Comedy Central). On the radio, Pierre has performed on The Now Show (Radio 4), hosts the BBC Sounds podcast series Obsessed With… SAS: Rogue Heroes and co-hosts the hit podcast Budpod with Phil Wang. As a writer, Pierre was one of the regular writers on the rebooted Spitting Image (ITV/Britbox) and has also written on shows including Mock the Week (BBC2), The News Quiz (Radio 4) and The Mash Report (BBC2).​

One of the UK’s most acclaimed live acts, Pierre‘s latest show Why Can’t I Just Enjoy Things? saw a sold-out run at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, and was his third show to have been placed in the top 20 best-reviewed comedy shows across the entire festival. His first special, Quiet Ones, was distributed by US comedy label 800 Pound Gorilla Records and has amassed over 250,000 views online.​

#### “*Dawn of a major talent*” The Guardian

#### ​”*A show packed full of belly laughs…impressively well written, perfectly building and building and rich with detail…Novellie delivers it all with real astuteness and skill*” The Metro​

#### “*A big presence…He will go far*” The Times

Discover Pierre Novellie here: [https://www.pierrenovellie.com/](https://www.pierrenovellie.com/)

events.title: The Advent Procession
events.raw:
**The Advent Procession** — Sun 29 Nov | 18:00 – 19:30. Free.

**Begin Advent with one of Bristol Cathedral's most powerful and atmospheric services.**

Beginning in complete darkness, the Advent Procession follows a journey from darkness into light. The voices of the Cathedral Choir are first heard from the far end of the Cathedral before the procession begins. As the choir and vergers move through the building, candles are gradually lit throughout the congregation, transforming the Cathedral with light. Through music, scripture and prayer, the service unfolds the story of God's promises and the hope of Christ's coming into the world.

Rich in symbolism, music and beauty, the Advent Procession marks the beginning of the Church's year and the start of the journey towards Christmas.
events.summary: The cathedral choir's Advent Sunday procession, which starts in total darkness and lights the building candle by candle as the choir moves through it. Free, and the most theatrical service of the cathedral's year.

events.summary: November's romance club leaves Prythian for Ali Hazelwood's The Love Hypothesis.
events.description:
**Whether you’re a fan of the series or looking to delve into romance fiction, our Romance book club offers a joyful escape. We're building a community to gush over swoon-worthy characters and a safe space to discuss themes like relationships. **

**In November, we will be looking at *The Love Hypothesis *by Ali Hazelwood. Let’s share the love!**

**Date:**
Monday 30th of November

**Venue:**
Max Minerva's, 47 Henleaze Road, BS9 4JU

**Time:**
Doors at 18:30. Discussion at 18:45. Finish at 19:45.

**Tickets:**
Attendance for the book club is free, but if you could register your place through the website, it helps us to gauge numbers.

If you would like to buy a copy of the book, you can order it through us and show up on the night.

**ABOUT *THE BOOK***

***The Love Hypothesis***

**When a fake relationship between scientists meets the irresistible force of attraction, it throws one woman’s carefully calculated theories on love into chaos.**

As a third-year Ph. D. candidate, Olive Smith doesn’t believe in lasting romantic relationships but her best friend does, and that’s what got her into this situation. Convincing Anh that Olive is on her way to a happily ever after was always going to be tough, scientists require proof. So, like any self-respecting woman, Olive panics and kisses the first man she sees.

That man is none other than Adam Carlsen, a young hotshot professor and well-known ass. Which is why Olive is positively floored when he agrees to keep her charade a secret and be her fake boyfriend. But when a big science conference goes haywire and Adam surprises her again with his unyielding support (and his unyielding abs), their little experiment feels dangerously close to combustion.

Olive soon discovers that the only thing more complicated than a hypothesis on love is putting her own heart under the microscope.

**ABOUT THE AUTHOR**

**Ali Hazelwood** is an Italian romance novelist and neuroscience professor based in the United States. Many of her works center on women in STEM fields and academia. Her debut novel, The Love Hypothesis, was a New York Times best seller and is currently being developed into a feature film.

**From access to achievement: Celebrating 20 years of Access to Bristol and 10 years of Bristol Scholars**

Join us as we celebrate a milestone year for widening participation at the University of Bristol.

Marking 20 years since the launch of Access to Bristol and 10 years of the Bristol Scholars programme - alongside the University's 150th anniversary - this special event brings together colleagues, partners, and students past and present to reflect on impact, share stories, and look ahead to the future.

We warmly invite university staff, school and college partners, current participants, and alumni of these programmes who have progressed to study or graduate from Bristol and beyond.

Enjoy light refreshments while connecting with the community that has helped shape two decades of opportunity and achievement.

**Please note, this event is exclusively for alumni that completed either Access to Bristol or Bristol Scholars.**

events.title: Ian Stone Is Looking for the Wow
events.raw:
**Comedy: Ian Stone IAN STONE IS LOOKING FOR THE WOW**

4 December · 20:00 – 22:00 · £22
events.summary: An extra show added for Ian Stone, whom The Times called a masterful exponent of self-mocking Jewish humour.
events.description:
#### EXTRA SHOW DUE TO POPULAR DEMAND

***“Life can’t just be the humdrum, the mundane and the routine before the inevitable slide to disease, decay and death. Why can’t we sneak in a bit of awesome, a tad of amazing and maybe a smidge of wonderful? A forest canopy opening onto a huge vista would be enchanting for some but my ancestors wandered in the desert for forty years, I think we’ve been outdoors enough. Others get their fix from the spiritual but I’ve been harbouring a grudge against God since my mother stopped me going to Arsenal after my Barmitzvah. Forty nine years ago. ’God will be watching’ she said. Well, at least he got to see the game. The point is, life could be so much better so I’m on the lookout. Come and join me on the hunt.”***

Ian Stone is a hugely experienced broadcaster, podcaster and writer and a brilliantly funny comedian. He performs at major comedy festivals and venues globally. His popular posts and reels on social media have quickly earned him a following of over 60k across BlueSky, Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook, amassing millions of views.

In the last three years, Ian has performed his one-man shows at the Edinburgh Festival to packed rooms and great reviews. In 2023, he won the prestigious Spirit of the Fringe Award. He took his last show on tour across the UK, finishing with a sold-out performance at London’s Comedy Store. Ian recently returned from making his debut at the Melbourne Comedy Festival. He will be returning to Edinburgh with Looking for the Wow before kicking off his UK tour.

Aside from stand-up comedy, Ian co-hosted the award-winning Rock ‘N’ Roll Football show on Absolute Radio for five years with Ian Wright. He currently presents a very popular (50k downloads per episode), twice-weekly Arsenal podcast, Handbrake Off, for The Athletic. A live version of the podcast recently sold out Leicester Square Theatre in London. Ian is also a regular contributor on Times Radio. His book To Be Someone was published in 2020 and has received nearly 500 four- and five-star reviews on Amazon.

events.title: Stand Up For The Weekend with Matt Stellingwerf & Guests
events.raw:
**Comedy: Stand Up For The Weekend with Matt Stellingwerf & Guests**

5 December · 20:00 – 22:00 · From £12
events.summary: Matt Stellingwerf headlines the club night again, six weeks after his October date.
events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend with Matt Stellingwerf, featuring Thor Stenhaug plus compere Jeremy Flynn

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our weekly flagship comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: MATT STELLINGWERF

Matt Stellingwerf’s comedy blends sharp intellect with warm, conversational storytelling, drawing on his background in criminology, anthropology and life as a New Zealander navigating Britain. His style is thoughtful rather than confrontational, weaving research, personal anecdotes and audience interaction into routines that feel spontaneous, inclusive and quietly incisive. He tackles subjects from politics and psychology to relationships and human behaviour with self-deprecating wit and effortless charm.

Highly regarded by his peers, Matt Stellingwerf has won four NZ Comedy Guild Awards, including Best Newcomer. He is now UK based and respected nationwide by promoters and comedy venues.

A renowned MC and compere, Matt is a 3-time nominee for Best MC in New Zealand. Matt was a 2015 and 2016 nominee for the prestigious Billy T Award.

When this ***“erudite satire-superstar”* (Theatreview)** gets onto the stage, the acceleration from zero to a hundred jokes is measured in seconds. Matt Stellingwerf’s deftly crafted jokes display a man full of seriously good comedic talent.

#### “*Stellingwerf’s comedy is intelligent, clever and thoroughly researched..all of the while being really likeable*” Libel

#### “…*an intellectual ‘Fonze’..extremely laid back and relaxed with the audience, seamlessly having banter and keeping his cool*” Keeping Up With NZ

Discover Matt Stellingwerf here: [https://www.mattstellingwerf.com/](https://www.mattstellingwerf.com/)

events.summary: Canadian crowd-work specialist Ian Bagg, whose show is a dialogue with the room rather than a monologue at it.
events.description:
Ian Bagg is a world-touring comedian whose comedy was recently described as “dangerously flawless” on the JRE. But he is not just a comedian, he is also the co-host of the weekly hockey podcast, **Enjoying Orange Slices with Jeff and Ian**.

Early in his life, he discovered a love for hockey. Whether he was involved in minor, junior, pro, or friends getting together to play shinny, he loved hockey! He went to some camps and was cut, realizing he had no chance of making the pros. He knew it was time to use his natural talent to make people laugh.

Life has been fantastic for this energetic and wildly funny boundary-pushing entertainer. Touring nonstop across North America, he has started taking over the world with Australia, China, and the Middle East. With Europe being one of his latest stops. His fast-paced, off-the-cuff, quick-witted, animated style has him winning over television audiences.

He placed in the finals of NBC’s **Last Comic Standing**. He made appearances on **Late Night with Conan O’Brien** and **The Tonight Show.** A popular guest on WTF, YMH, a half-hour comedy featured on Comedy Central and HBO, not to mention one-hour specials on Showtime **Getting To Know You** and Amazon Prime **Conversations!**. His fast-paced multi-direction show has made patrons want to see multiple shows on a weekend. The audience becomes characters in his performance as they answer questions. Most comedians have a monologue; Ian has a dialogue. Attend a show immediately and see why his high school history teacher asked Ian’s parents if there was something he should know about Ian

[Ian Bagg | World-Touring Comedian](https://ianbagg.com/)

events.title: Stand Up For The Weekend with Dan Tiernan
events.raw:
**Comedy: Stand Up For The Weekend with Dan Tiernan**

12 December · 20:00 – 22:00 · From £12
events.summary: Dan Tiernan headlines the pre-Christmas club night with anarchic physicality and disarming vulnerability.
events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend with Dan Tiernan, featuring Joe Sutherland plus compere Ross Smith

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: DAN TIERNAN

Dan Tiernan’s comedy is a thrilling collision of anarchic physicality, razor-sharp writing and disarming vulnerability. He storms the stage with explosive, unpredictable energy, turning stories about addiction, neurodiversity, identity and working-class life into relentless laugh generators. His style veers from absurd one-liners to confessional storytelling, always delivered with a mischievous grin that makes chaos feel joyfully controlled. Critics have praised his ***“dynamic force”* (The Skinny)**, ***“unique ferocity… in utter command”* (Chortle)**, and ***“crude comedy with a big payoff” *(The Guardian)**. The result is exhilarating stand-up that feels dangerous, heartfelt and utterly original, leaving audiences laughing, wincing and wanting more.

Dan made a big impact on the UK comedy circuit back in 2022 after winning both the **BBC New Comedy Award **and the **British Comedian Of The Year**, and if this wasn’t enough he was winner of the **Best Newcomer at the ISH Comedy Awards** in 2023 and nominated for **Best Newcomer at the Edinburgh Festival** the same year. Since then, Dan has also been nominated for the **Next Big Thing** by the British Comedy Guide in 2025. With all of these accolades it does make you wonder where Dan can go from here.

Dan is hugely in demand and has performed at the **Melbourne Comedy Festival**, the **Cat Laughs Comedy Festival** in Ireland, and the **BBC Comedy Festival**, and has appeared on various radio and TV shows including **The Last Leg**, **Live At The Apollo**, **8 Out Of 10 Cats does Countdown**, and **The Stand Up Sketch Show**.

#### “*Raucously entertaining*” The Guardian

#### “*A furious yet friendly, thrilling rollercoaster ride*” The Telegraph

#### “*He’s a real force-of-nature comic who sweeps the room up in his exhilarating performance into a frenzy of laughter*” Chortle

#### “*Witness a future stand-up star*” British Comedy Guide

Follow Dan Tiernan here: [https://www.instagram.com/tiernancomedian/](https://www.instagram.com/tiernancomedian/)

events.description:
#### Stand Up For The Weekend with Daliso Chaponda Featuring Erich McElroy plus Jeremy Flynn

##### Stand Up For The Weekend is our flagship weekly comedy show featuring top circuit headliners and guest acts plus incredibly funny and engaging comperes who host the show. A choice of table seats, reserved row seats and unreserved row seats are available to book online.

#### Headliner: DALISO CHAPONDA

Daliso Chaponda’s comedy blends razor-sharp wit, intelligent social commentary and warm, conversational storytelling. Drawing on his experiences of growing up between cultures, he tackles race, politics, identity and current affairs with playful curiosity rather than confrontation, delivering deft one-liners alongside thoughtful observations. His engaging, personable stage presence invites audiences to laugh while reconsidering familiar assumptions. As *Metro* observed, he is “**Full of sharp one-liners and well crafted gags… a real talent**,” while *The Guardian* praised his ability to “**Gets laughs out of topics other comedians shun**.” The result is comedy that is insightful, accessible, provocative and consistently entertaining.

Daliso Chaponda shot to fame in the UK on Britain’s Got Talent, making it to the final of the 2017 series and establishing himself a firm favourite with the judges and the British public. He became a Facebook and YouTube star amassing over 300 million views of his performances.

Daliso is also the writer, creator, and host of his Rose d’Or nominated BBC Radio 4 show Citizen of Nowhere that has aired for two series.

As seen and heard on The Royal Variety Performance 2020 (ITV), Britain’s Got Talent 2017 (ITV), Britain’s Got Talent Champions 2019 (ITV), QI (BBC2), The Apprentice: You’re Fired (BBC2), Good Evening Britain (ITV), The News Quiz (BBC Radio 4), and The Now Show (BBC Radio 4).

Discover Daliso Chaponda here: [DALISO CHAPONDA](https://dalisochaponda.com/)

Britain
events.summary: A one-night murder mystery staged aboard the ship in the run-up to Christmas.
events.description:
Take part in an exhilarating evening of entertainment on board the captivating SS Great
Britain. During your dinner, keep your eyes open for clues as you become the detective and
help solve the mysterious crime. We offer guests the ultimate, memorable evening.

**The plot** — Introducing the strange case of Santa's 'Claws'…

Christmas 1937. Mr Uffton Harlecombe had just left the December meeting of the Board of
Governors at St David's School. However, there was very little 'Christmas cheer' at the
meeting this evening. In fact, as he pulled his thick coat tightly around him to shield him
from the silently falling snow, he smiled to himself. He had left no one at that meeting in
any doubt that crossing him was not a smart career move.

Still laughing to himself, he crossed the road and walked along the snow-covered side
street back to his Bentley Sports motor car. Everywhere was silent; a chill wind suddenly
picked up, making him huddle in a doorway to light his cigar. Perhaps he may have seen the
white-bearded face and the crimson costume for a fleeting second. Maybe he even saw the
weapon—a wicked steel claw!

Uffton Harlecombe had misjudged tonight's meeting. The information he had spilt to the
assembled people had been taken far more to heart than he could ever have imagined. One
person would make this a Christmas everyone wants to forget. The spirit of Christmas may
never die, but there are people here tonight who are going to do just that!!

**Key info** — Price: £99pp. Time: 6.30pm-12am. Includes: arrival drink, 3 course festive
menu & murder mystery experience. Group bookings: for tables of 8, contact
events@bristoldockyards.org.

events.title: Lecture: The Knepp Estate
events.raw:
**Lecture: The Knepp Estate** — Thursday 21 January 2027 at 7:30 pm to 9:00 pm,
The Frank Lecture Theatre, Wills Physics Laboratory, Tyndall Avenue, Bristol.

"Friends' Winter Lectures will take place on the third Thursday of the month at
the Frank Theatre, Wills Physics Laboratory, Tyndall Avenue, Bristol BS8 1TL at
7:30pm. Lectures are free to Friends on production of their membership card, and
free to students on production of their student card. […]"
events.summary: The Friends' Winter Lecture on Knepp, the Sussex estate whose rewilding became the reference case for the whole idea in Britain. No speaker is named on the index.
events.description:
Friends' Winter Lectures will take place on the third Thursday of the month at
the Frank Theatre, Wills Physics Laboratory, Tyndall Avenue, Bristol BS8 1TL
at 7:30pm. Lectures are free to Friends on production of their membership card,
and free to students on production of their student card. Guests who are not
members or students will be asked for a donation (suggested £5).

Speaker: Charlie Harpur, Head Gardener, Knepp Estate.

Charlie joined the Knepp team as Head Gardener in early 2022 to oversee the
rewilding of Knepp's Walled Garden, as well as the development of the Market
Garden and the landscape at the Wilding Kitchen. Having trained as an
architect, he worked for landscape architect Tom Stuart-Smith for several
years, then gained practical experience in horticulture and ecology at Chelsea
Physic Garden and Kew, where he completed the Kew Diploma in Horticulture.

events.title: Andrew Bird: Bird on Edge
events.raw:
**Comedy: Andrew Bird – BIRD ON EDGE**

25 February · 20:00 – 22:00 · £18
events.summary: Andrew Bird's new hour, on being permanently worried about everything from global events to parking.
events.description:
Back with a brand-new show Andrew Bird has just supported Russell Howard on his current national tour including four straight shows at The London Palladium. He has also recently supported Rhod Gilbert and Troy Hawke and at The UK Comedy Awards 2023 was voted Comic’s Comic-Best Act.

Andrew is always worried or stressed about something. From global events to finding free parking. From a wife hitting the perimenopause combined with two teenage kids, to hanging a wine-rack. How can he not be “on edge”?

Having previously supported Russell at Bristol’s Ashton Gate Football stadium he’s also supported Rob Brydon, America’s Brian Regan and Michelle Wolfe on their only London shows and Michael McIntyre on an entire arena tour including Wembley and the O2.

He was only 1 of 7 comedians to perform in front of Banksy at Dismal Land and he’s written on the recent series of 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown.

#### “*A brilliantly funny comedian*” Russell Howard

events.title: Chorister for the Day
events.raw:
**Chorister for the Day** — Sat 27 Feb 2027 | 10:00 – 15:00. Booking coming soon.

**Be a Chorister for the Day – Explore Life as a Chorister at Bristol Cathedral.** Is your child in Year 4 and passionate about singing? _Chorister for the Day_ is a unique opportunity for children and their families to experience what it's like to be part of the renowned Cathedral Choir.

Throughout the day, your child will participate in a fun and interactive singing workshop, try on chorister robes, and gain an understanding of what life as a chorister involves. They will also learn about Evensong and the musical traditions of the Cathedral. Parents will have the chance to meet and chat with chorister families over coffee, learning about the commitment, rewards, and opportunities that come with being a chorister.

Choristers receive free vocal lessons, funding for instrumental lessons, and perform in prestigious events, including appearances on national TV, radio, and international tours. All of our choristers are educated at Bristol Cathedral Choir School.

For more information contact William Forrest, Music Assistant, 0117 946 8173, William.forrest@bristol-cathedral.co.uk. [Click here to find out more about the choir](https://bristol-cathedral.co.uk/worship/choir/)
events.summary: A taster day for Year 4 children thinking about joining the cathedral choir — a singing workshop, robes to try on, an introduction to Evensong — while parents meet current chorister families over coffee. Booking not yet open.

price.text: Free; retiring collection for the Choir Tour Fund after the recital

events.raw:
**Trinity Sunday Eucharist** — Sun 23 May 2027 | 10:00 – 11:15. Free.

Bristol Cathedral is formally known as The Cathedral Church of the Holy and Undivided Trinity. We celebrate Trinity Sunday, our Feast of Title, with a joyful Eucharist sung by the full Cathedral Choir. This will be followed by an instrumental; recital given by the Cathedral Choristers, with a retiring collection going towards the Choir Tour Fund.

**Children of all ages are also invited to join us for prayers, bible readings, teaching and fun activities in a safe, playful, and prayerful environment during the 10.00am Eucharist in term time.**

events.description:
Travelling Light in partnership with Alibi present *The Forest Door*.

We are currently making plans and fundraising to tour the show to primary schools in Bristol, Bath and surrounding areas, plus Exeter and the South West in autumn 2027.

**About the show**

What happens when you go through a mysterious portal into another world? On the other side you find yourself in a magical forest, alive with wonder and excitement. Here, you'll meet other enchanting creatures preparing for a big festival… but there is a problem.

Join us on this brand-new adventure, as we explore traditions, memories and solve problems; resulting in one unforgettable celebration.

*The Forest Door* is a new theatre offer for primary aged children, incorporating performance, interactive in-classroom activities, and support and resources for teachers and families.

Grown from the imaginations of young people – The Forest Door is based on ideas from local children who took part in the development in Bristol and Exeter.

**Booking The Forest Door**

To place a booking request for autumn 2027, please complete our School Booking Request Form. Suitable for all primary aged children and their families aged 4-11 (targeted at Reception - Year 4). Performance: 50 mins. Full experience: 2 hours.

**At A Glance:** 27 September - 10 December 2027. Primary schools and community spaces across the South West. No public tickets currently available.

**Choral Evensong** — 5.15pm | Mon – Fri, except Thursdays (term-time only). 3.30pm | Sun.

Choral Evensong is usually sung by the Cathedral choir and consists of the singing of texts taken from the bible interspersed with prayers and readings. This service offers a chance to reflect and immerse yourself in the presence of God at the end of the day, through outstanding choral music.

The service is held in the Nave and lasts around 40 minutes. Please check the Music List (there is a link at the bottom of this and every page) for upcoming details of upcoming services, music, and who is singing.

**Evening Prayer** — 5.15pm | Thu. 5.15pm | Sat (and other days when there is no choir).

The diary for the week of 12–18 September lists Choral Evensong at 17:15 on Fri 11, Mon 14, Tue 15 and Wed 16 September, Choral Evensong on Sunday at 15:30 on Sun 13, and Evening Prayer at 17:15 on Sat 12 and Thu 17.

events.title: All God's Children
events.raw:
All God's Children is an exhibition in Bristol Cathedral that explores the impact of the slave economy on Cathedral life, past and present.

All God's Children is part of the Cathedral's work to understand its links with the transatlantic trade of enslaved people. Research that informed the exhibition discovered that between 1670 and 1900, roughly 1,000 people were buried or memorialised in the Cathedral and its grounds. Around 200 (20%) of them had a close connection to the slavery-based economy.

This exhibition presents the first findings of a research project into Bristol Cathedral's connections with slavery as revealed through its memorials and grave-markers. We hope that it will help to inform a wide-ranging conversation about the stories we tell, the ways in which we can repair and restore damaged relationships and the ways we can work together for a better future for everyone.

The exhibition is available whenever the Cathedral is open.

Listed daily, 10:00 - 16:00. Free.
events.summary: A standing exhibition on what the cathedral's own memorials record about Bristol's slave economy: of roughly a thousand people buried or memorialised here between 1670 and 1900, about a fifth had a close connection to it. Free, and open whenever the cathedral is.

We're proud of our beer and proud of the brewery in which we make it,
and gladly welcome groups into our "office" on guided tours of Bristol
Beer Factory.

It's a pleasure to open our doors again to reveal our BRAND NEW
BREWERY! After 20 years on North Street, we have simply outgrown our
tanks and are excited to brew in a sustainably focused site within the
same postcode. Our new brewery is located in the Ashton Gate Trading
Estate, the same distance to Ashton Gate Stadium as the Tap Room is,
just in the other direction! The address of our new brewery is 50-52
Ashton Vale Road, BS3 2HQ.

**About brewery tours.** Public brewery tours will be held every
Saturday throughout the year, with some exceptions over holiday dates
and additional weekday nights available. These tours are a great way
to learn about the brewing process and give an opportunity to answer
those burning questions you have about how your favourite drink is
made.

**What's included in the tour**

- 2 hour visit including tour of the Brewery
- 3 gluten free pints from freshly racked kegs
- 1x free pint and 10% off BBF products thereafter at the North Street
  Tap Room — head over after the tour to sample more beers or buy
  merch, cans, mini tins or growlers to take home.

**Private brewery tours.** We offer large groups (10+) the option to
have a private tour of the brewery. These are flexible and can be on
weeknight evenings or Saturdays at 12pm. Prices start from £300. Email
tours@bristolbeerfactory.co.uk to enquire.

**Vouchers.** There is no expiry date on the vouchers. If you have an
existing voucher for a tour or tasting bought before tours at the new
site were possible, get in touch to upgrade your ticket.

**Cancellations and rebooking.** Brewery tour tickets are
non-refundable, unless there are exceptional circumstances. Please let
us know at least 24 hours in advance if you are unable to attend your
booking and we will be happy to help you rebook for another date.
Tickets cannot be rescheduled with less than 24 hours notice.

events.description:
Each winter, we offer 1-day workshops teaching traditional hedgelaying: a craft
that preserves the past and protects the future. Courses are taught by
professional hedgelayers and accommodate all skill levels, from beginners to
experienced enthusiasts.

Hedgelaying involves partially severing the stem of the trees in the hedgerow,
allowing them to be laid at an angle of around 45 degrees. This fills gaps in
the hedge while encouraging new vertical shoot growth for denser coverage. The
laid hedge is secured with stakes and binding, varying by regional style.
Previously taught styles include North Somerset and Midland approaches, and
examples of the various techniques can be seen around the Grow Wilder site.

**Winter 2026/27 Dates To Be Announced.** "Future hedgelaying course dates will
be displayed in this section, once confirmed."

Grow Wilder, 181 Frenchay Park Road, Bristol, BS16 1EL. Toilets, picnic area,
accessible toilet and baby changing available; assistance dogs only.

**Book Clubs at Storysmith**

Our book clubs are genuinely our thing about Storysmith. We've held book clubs in the shop since 2019, and now run a total of seven monthly book clubs for curious readers on regular Tuesdays and Wednesday evenings.

We like to read widely, so nothing is off limits – at the end of each meeting, we encourage attendees to pitch the next book the group will read, and then we take a vote to decide. We also provide a glass of wine, and 10% off the following month's book.

We run five general book clubs, a queer book club and an eco book club.

This is a space to explore art, crafts, and get creative. Everyone is

in mind, want to meet new people in your local area, or just need
some 'you' time. No artistic experience is needed, but if you have
skills to share, that's great too. As a new group, we'll decide what
we want to explore. Welcoming all ideas and creating projects we can
learn together!

Every Tuesday, 9.30am–11am.

"I've set this up because I love being creative, whether that's
getting my paints out, crafting things with my kids, crocheting or
making presents. After speaking to other parents, I realised that my
desire to have a creative meeting space, open during school hours,
was something others would also enjoy. Knowing this, it inspired me
to create one. So the plan is to create a relaxed space for anyone
who wants to join…Parent or not." – Elisha

We will set up a theme for each session, where I can give inspiration
and projects everyone can get involved in. There will be a WhatsApp
group set up to share ideas and inspiration. The aim is to provide a
creative space where we can all explore in a safe, relaxed & friendly
way. But please also feel free to bring any projects you're working
on, your work may inspire us.

Sessions are free and open to those aged 18 and over, no booking
necessary.

If you have a small child, you're welcome to bring them along, as
long as you're still able to participate fully in the session. The
focus is on taking time for yourself, so we ask that you judge
whether you can take part with your child alongside.

We know it can be hard to anticipate, so you are welcome to come
along and test it out!

events.raw:
**Foundations for the Future Exhibition** — an exhibition celebrating
KWMC past and present. Everyone is welcome to pop in anytime Mon-Fri,
9:30am-5pm, in the Main Studio. KWMC, Leinster Avenue, South Bristol,
BS4 1NL.
events.summary: A free weekday-hours exhibition charting nearly thirty years of Knowle West Media Centre, with an open invitation to add your own stories to it. Call ahead — the Main Studio is also used for workshops.
events.description:
An exhibition celebrating KWMC past and present...

This exhibition charts almost thirty years of KWMC, exploring how ideas
have grown and the differences we have made together. At a pivotal
moment for KWMC, as our founder Carolyn Hassan retires, we look
backwards to go forwards.

We remember the social, political, environmental and economic backdrops
that shaped our work, reflect on the challenges faced and the insights
acquired. We see our history as 'usable past', providing rich
foundations for KWMC's growth into the future.

The exhibition is clustered around ideas of practice. In each cluster
you will find key activities and insights that help demonstrate these
ideas.

**What now?** Throughout 2025-26 there will be a series of events,
including reunions, in-conversations and workshops.

Fancy seeing the exhibition for yourself? Everyone is welcome to pop in
anytime Mon-Fri, 9:30am-5pm. The exhibition is set up in our Main
Studio space, which we also use for workshops or events. Give us a
quick call or email first if you'd like to check if the space is
available before arriving (enquiries@kwmc.org.uk / 0117 903 0444). Our
address is: KWMC, Leinster Avenue, South Bristol, BS4 1NL.

events.description:
## Discover Bristol's Vibrant Finzels Reach Market

Step into a world of incredible street food at Finzels Reach Market.

Open every Wednesday and Friday lunchtime, discover street food from around
the world.

## Our traders

Where would we be without our wonderful traders? Whilst some loyal traders
have been with us since the start; we're committed to keeping things exciting
by rotating traders each week and inviting guest traders to join us to bring
variety.

We rigorously vet our traders to not only ensure they're turning out the
tastiest street food but to check they are minimalizing food waste and using
eco-friendly packaging.

Want to know who's trading each week? Sign up to our weekly newsletter and
get details of who's trading each week into your in-box every Monday.

## History of Finzels Reach Market

Founded 9 years ago by Sophie Bowden and David Pyne, Finzels Reach Market
opened whilst Finzels Reach was still in development and has become part of
the make-up of this exciting and vibrant quarter. Located on a site which was
once the home to Courage Brewery and previously George's Brewery; the market
has gone through quite the journey. Having launched whilst the area was still
a building site; the market reopened during lockdown covid secure and has
since grown from a weekly market to a successful twice weekly market
showcasing over 40 different traders every month.

The market is carefully curated meaning traders change twice weekly resulting
in an ever-changing selection of street food on offer. Look out for guest
traders, seasonal food and themed markets.

## Visit us

A short walk from the city centre, Finzels Reach Market is located opposite
Castle Park surrounded by independent restaurants, cafes and bars and even
its own brewpub. Find the market located in Old Temple Street just off
Counterslip.

There are 3 routes into the market on foot, via Bath Street, Hawkins Lane
(over Castle Bridge) and Counterslip. Parking is available nearby at The
Galleries and Gardiner Haskins. There is free bike parking in and around
Finzels Reach, with major bike lanes along Counterslip. Many bus services
pass near the market, including the MetroBus. The market is only a 10 minute
walk from Bristol Temple Meads Station. Bristol Ferry runs a waterbus service
which stops at Castle Park jetty, just a minute's walk to the market.

## Frequently asked questions

**What sort of food can you expect at the market?** "With plently of options
for vegan, veggie and meat eaters; the market line-up changes twice weekly to
provide an ever-changing selection of top quality street food." From sushi,
deep fried chicken wings and Thai curry to Filipino spring rolls and Greek
gyros. "For those with a sweet tooth, we always have a cake stall!"

**How sustainable is the market?** "All of our traders use biodegradable
packaging and we don't allow any single use plastic." Customers are welcome
to bring their own lunchboxes.

**When is the market open?** "The market is open all year round on Wednesday
and Friday from 11am - 2pm. We are closed at Christmas, New Year and on Good
Friday. Please check our socials for the most up to date information about
whether the market is open as we always update there if we've had to cancel
the market because of challenging weather conditions."

**Are there toilet facilities?** "As an outdoor pop-up market, unfortunately
we're unable to provide toilets." Public toilets are available at the nearby
Galleries Shopping Centre.

**Do you cater for customers with food allergies?** "All traders have an
ingredient and allergen list available on their stall."

**Is the market family friendly?** "We welcome all customers to the market
whether you bring the kids or a furry friend."

Located within Bristol's old city, St Nicholas Indoor Market is home to over
60 independent retailers that sell a mixture of gifts, original fashion and
hand-crafted accessories.

eclectic array of stalls from jewellery to hot sauce.

visiting the Glass Arcade eateries for delicious food and drink.

**What you can find at the market**

With a wide range of unique stalls and shops, the thriving indoor market is
a great place to shop, eat and drink or just soak up the atmosphere.

The market is divided into three sections: Exchange Hall, Glass Arcade and
Covered Market. You can wander your way through the Covered Market which has
a series of individual shops through its quirky alleyways, or while away the
time in The Exchange Hall; a large open plan trading area with a broad
collection of items for sale. The Glass Arcade is home to a unique offering
of world foods so whatever your tastes, you're sure to find it here.

**When it is:** Monday to Saturday, 9.30am to 5pm

inside and discover interactive exhibitions, digital recreations, historic artefacts and
new community-led research uncovering voices and stories from SS Great Britain's 41 years

close collaboration with local community groups and researchers.

events.description:
**Master the climb.** Discover what it was like to be a Victorian sailor of the SS Great
Britain crew, and climb the ship’s rigging 25 metres into the sky. Feeling even braver?
Edge out 9m over the Great Western Dockyard for hands down the best birds-eye view in
Bristol.

**The only way is up.** Each session lasts roughly 30 minutes and is limited to two
climbers at a time. You’ll be guided through every step by trained instructors from Young
Bristol’s Outdoor Employment Programme. We’re proud to support the youth-driven charity in
its mission to help young locals develop leadership skills and gain nationally recognised
qualifications. They’ll make sure you’re safe at all times, in an experience we promise is
as authentic as the mid-19th century.

Admission ticket or add a Go Aloft + Day Pass | Child bundle.

events.summary: A free weekly 5km run around the Ashton Court estate, held every Saturday and open to anyone who has registered with parkrun. The council page states the distance, the weekly pattern and that it is free; it gives no start time or meeting point.
events.description:
### What is Ashton Court parkrun?

A free, fun, and friendly weekly 5k community event. Walk, jog, run, volunteer or
spectate – it's up to you!

### When is it?

Every Saturday at 9:00am.

### Where is it?

The event takes place at the Ashton Court Estate, just across the River Avon from Bristol
city centre.

### What does it cost to join in?

Nothing - it's free! but please register before you first come along. Only ever register
with parkrun once and don't forget to bring a scannable copy of your barcode. If you forget
